items.title: [order-monitor] bybit_2 XRPUSDT SL amend failing — Bybit's 20-leg tpsl cap likely hit under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial's per-order qty-scoped brackets
items.description: BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial (live-verified + rolled out per BL/PR #7115, see the health-review-backlog entry above and performance-review-backlog) attaches a qty-scoped Partial-type TP/SL leg PER ORDER rather than one position-level bracket. Bybit's own API enforces a hard cap of 20 combined tp+sl legs per symbol (`oldTpNum+oldStNum+newNum > 20`, ErrCode 110061). If XRPUSDT on bybit_2 (traded by multiple strategies incl. `xrp_pullback_2h`, and as of PR #7254 `ict_scalp_xrp_5m` on bybit_1 — different account, not a factor here) has accumulated legs from many prior partial opens/adds without them being consolidated/cleared as positions close, it can hit that 20-leg ceiling — at which point ANY subsequent SL amend request for that symbol fails outright and `order_monitor` leaves the DB (and the live stop) UNCHANGED. This is a protection-integrity risk: a stop-loss that should move (e.g., a breakeven trail or a tightening update) silently fails to update on the exchange while the DB may or may not reflect the intended level, for as long as the leg count stays saturated. Not yet confirmed whether this is a one-off (a stale/orphaned leg never cleaned up) or a structural risk of the partial-brackets design at higher trade frequency/leg turnover on one symbol. NOT investigated further this session (incidental discovery during unrelated deploy-verification read) — flagging per the standing 'if you see something, say something' directive rather than walking past it.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review or order-path session. items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) confirmed one-off/stale-leg artifact, cleaned up, and a monitor added so a future saturation is caught before it silently blocks SL amends; or (b) a structural fix (consolidation/fallback) ships so an SL amend on a saturated symbol never silently fails to protect the position — order_monitor's `errors=1` counter for this cause should trend to zero going forward.

updates.by: claude (operator-flagged, live screenshot of Bybit Open Orders showing 23 TP/SL entries for XRPUSDT)
updates.note: CONFIRMED STILL ACTIVE AND WORSE, ~3h after the 05:27Z discovery. Operator screenshot of the Bybit Open Orders → TP/SL tab shows 23 open conditional orders for XRPUSDT, all `Sell / Close Long / qty 165.5`, most sharing an identical `SL 1.0756`, timestamped every ~4-5 min (07:03:39, 07:07:36, 07:11:53, 07:16:48, 07:21:04 as of the screenshot). Cross-checked live: `GET /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=bybit_2` shows exactly ONE XRPUSDT position (side=Buy, size=165.5, entry=1.091) — confirming these 23 orders are NOT 23 separate positions/entries, they are duplicate/stale Partial-tpsl legs stacked on the SAME single position, now past Bybit's 20-leg cap (matches the 05:27Z ErrCode 110061 already logged). This is the trigger_condition's check (a) — DONE, confirmed pinned past the ceiling, not a one-off. Not yet root-caused WHICH call keeps adding legs at ~4-5min cadence (targeted 60s-window journalctl pulls around 07:07:36 and a 30min window around 07:00-07:25Z did not land on the exact XRP-strategy sub-tick before hitting the diag-relay's 55KB comment truncation — the per-symbol pipeline rotation + tick volume made a blind journalctl pull impractical; a future session should either request `/api/diag/log_file?name=audit` scoped tighter, or add a temporary XRPUSDT-specific grep/filter server-side) — but the mechanism (BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial's per-order leg accumulation, no consolidation on rollover) and the live impact (legitimate SL amends now silently failing per the 05:27Z error) are both confirmed. Escalated to the operator in-session as a live, real-money protection-integrity risk (not a UI/DB hallucination) with two candidate immediate mitigations presented: (1) Tier-3 rollback `BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full` on the live VM (restores single position-level bracket, the pre-2026-07-20 stable behavior, at the cost of reintroducing the netted-position bracket-sharing issue PR #7115 was built to fix); (2) a Tier-2 one-off cancel of the stale/duplicate XRPUSDT legs on bybit_2 to relieve the cap without reverting the mode (no existing tooling found for this in this session — would need scripting, e.g. via `set_trading_stop` idempotent leg replacement or Bybit's cancel-order API for specific TP/SL order IDs).

RESOLVED. Both halves shipped this session: (1) stopgap — PR #7315 (`scripts/ops/cancel_stale_tpsl_legs.py`, the `cancel-stale-tpsl-legs` Tier-2 system-action) merged + run `--apply` on bybit_2 XRPUSDT: cancelled the stale/duplicate legs, live-verified afterward exactly 1 SL + 1 TP leg remain (well under the 20-leg cap), operator notified. (2) structural fix — PR #7321 merged (sha e3203aff675adb3b48c6173c353099b3554c0326) and deployed to the live VM (`ict-trader-live.service` confirmed active post-restart, `xrp_pullback_2h` evaluating fresh prices): `execute_pkg` now captures each trade's Bybit leg id at entry via a before/after snapshot diff (`trades.sl_order_id`/`.tp_order_id`), and `modify_open_order` amends that SPECIFIC leg in place via `amend_order` when a tracked id exists, instead of re-adding via `set_trading_stop` — so a trade opened after the fix deployed cannot accumulate duplicate legs the way the old add-only path did. `close_open_position` also best-effort cancels the closing trade's own tracked leg(s) on exit. resolution_criteria (b) is satisfied: an SL amend on a trade with a tracked leg id now amends in place rather than adding a new leg, so the `errors=1` ErrCode-110061 failure mode cannot recur for trades opened post-fix. Full detail: docs/sprint-logs/S-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP-2026-07-21.md. NON-BLOCKING open follow-up (tracked in that sprint log, not re-opening this item): the structural fix's live entry-time leg-capture has not yet been observed against a real fresh entry (all validation so far is via the local test suite — 344 tests incl. the new `test_bybit_partial_tpsl.py` coverage — plus code review); a future session should confirm on the demo account (bybit_1) that a fresh partial-mode entry populates `sl_order_id`/`tp_order_id` and that a subsequent SL move amends in place rather than adding a leg. Also: legs from trades opened BEFORE the fix deployed have no tracked id and still fall back to the legacy add-a-leg path — the `cancel-stale-tpsl-legs` action remains available for that pre-existing minority and any other stranding this class of bug could still produce (see the updated docs/claude/system-actions.md entry).

updates.by: claude (same session, continued — operator caught the gap live via Telegram screenshot)
updates.note: The 'non-blocking follow-up' noted above turned out to bite immediately: the operator flagged (screenshot of repeated `TRADE UPDATED — XRPUSDT, SL → 1.0855` Telegram pings at 13:34/13:39/13:43Z, same ~4-5min cadence as the original bug) that the bybit_2 XRPUSDT position — open since BEFORE PR #7321 deployed — kept re-accumulating legs on the legacy add-a-leg path, because entry-time capture only fires for NEW orders and has no retroactive path for already-open trades. Confirmed via diag (`journal?table=trades`): the open XRPUSDT row (id 3577) had `sl_order_id`/`tp_order_id` both NULL. Fix shipped THIS session as PR #7336 (`backfill-tpsl-leg-ids`, merged sha 132df8d1b128ef920f85ef560d8134c00dbf391f, deployed — live VM HEAD confirmed via the pull-and-deploy audit trail): a new Tier-2 system-action that reads a symbol's CURRENT live SL/TP leg ids and retroactively writes them onto the one matching open/untracked trade row (refusing on ambiguity — more than one live leg of a type, or more than one candidate trade row). Applied to bybit_2/XRPUSDT: took 2 cancel→backfill race retries (legs kept forming on their own ~5min cadence faster than the ambiguity-safe write could land — issues #7338/#7340 both correctly refused rather than mis-attributing) before landing clean on the 3rd attempt (issue #7342): trade 3577 now carries `sl_order_id=67bc78e1-a8b6-4a7b-86bb-a4419937aa0c` / `tp_order_id=ff2dd38b-b9ee-40b9-bcfc-db98a1a052ea`. **LIVE-VERIFIED** (issue #7343, dry-run read 7 minutes later, past the next expected ~5min tick): still exactly 1 SL + 1 TP leg, SAME order id as when tagged — no new leg was added, confirming `modify_open_order` is now amending this specific leg in place rather than re-adding. The structural fix is now genuinely complete for this position, and `backfill-tpsl-leg-ids` is available for any other pre-existing open trade that needs the same retroactive tag. This item stays `resolved` — no further action needed on bybit_2/XRPUSDT specifically; the general capability (`backfill-tpsl-leg-ids`) is documented in `docs/claude/system-actions.md` for future use.

items.source: Direct follow-up to the now-`resolved` `BL-20260721-BYBIT2-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP` item. Everything live-verified for that incident (issue #7343: the same tracked leg id held across the position's own ~5min SL-recompute cadence) exercised the BACKFILL-then-amend path (`backfill-tpsl-leg-ids`, PR #7336) on a pre-existing trade — never the entry-time capture path itself (`execute_pkg`'s before/after conditional-order snapshot diff, PR #7321) against a real, freshly-placed Bybit Partial-tpsl order.
items.title: [verify] live-confirm PR #7321's ENTRY-TIME leg-id capture on a genuinely fresh Bybit Partial-tpsl order (not just the backfill-then-amend path already verified)
items.description: PR #7321 added `_partial_tpsl_leg_ids`/`_classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs` to `execute_pkg`: before placing an order it snapshots the symbol's live conditional (StopOrder) legs, places the order, snapshots again, and diffs to find the newly-created SL/TP leg id(s) — writing them onto `trades.sl_order_id`/`.tp_order_id` at insert time. This before/after diff logic has 344 local unit/integration tests plus full CI (7961 passed) exercising it against MOCKED `get_open_orders` responses, but has never been observed against the REAL Bybit API response shape for a freshly-placed Partial leg. The two failure modes that would matter in practice: (1) the diff finds 0 or >1 new legs of a type (e.g. a concurrent same-symbol entry from another strategy lands in the same poll window) and deliberately leaves the id untracked — expected/safe per the fix's own design, but the FREQUENCY of this in real trading conditions is unknown; (2) some subtle mismatch between the mocked test fixtures and Bybit's actual `get_open_orders(orderFilter="StopOrder")` payload shape (field names, `stopOrderType` values, timing of when a just-placed leg becomes visible in a follow-up list call) could cause the live diff to silently misfire in a way no test would catch. Today's incident only ever exercised the SEPARATE `backfill-tpsl-leg-ids` retroactive-tag path (PR #7336) — that proved the AMEND-IN-PLACE half of the fix works once a leg id is tracked, but said nothing about whether entry-time capture itself reliably populates that id for a brand-new order.

If entry-time capture is found to silently fail or mis-fire under real conditions, that's a new Tier-2/3 finding to raise with the operator, not something to fix quietly in a health-review session.

items.opened_by: claude (M27 Batch-4 XAUUSD session — discovered while dispatching a config-exact backtest+kfold run)
items.source: Direct repro across three consecutive trainer-vm-diag-request dispatches this session (issues #7297, #7300, #7301): a foreground command that runs silently (no stdout) for longer than roughly a minute or two reliably kills the SSH session with `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, before ANY output — including a partially-written result file — is captured or reported back on the issue. This happened identically whether the heavy command was plain foreground, backgrounded with `nohup ... &` + a foreground poll loop, or gated with a `timeout 480` wrapper; only fully detaching the process with `setsid nohup ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown -a` (returning from the SSH command almost immediately, well inside the drop window) reliably avoided it (issue #7302, confirmed working). The underlying compute was NOT actually slow — a 178k-bar XAUUSD 15m backtest that appeared to hang for 8+ minutes under the broken foreground pattern actually completed in under 3 minutes once run detached (confirmed via a follow-up log-tail dispatch).
items.title: [trainer-vm-diag] long-silent (no-stdout) foreground commands reliably drop the SSH channel before completion, independent of workflow job timeout-minutes
items.description: `.github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml` runs the requested `cmd:` over an SSH session with `timeout-minutes: 10` at the JOB level. That job-level timeout is NOT what's firing here — the failures happened at 2–8 minutes in, well under the 10-minute budget, and manifested as a client-side `Broken pipe` rather than a graceful cancellation (the workflow's own `if: cancelled()` handler, which correctly posts a comment on a genuine concurrency-preemption cancel, never fires for this failure mode — the run just dies with no comment at all, which is worse: a requester sees silence and has no way to distinguish 'still running' from 'already dead'). Likely cause: the SSH action/client (or an intermediate proxy) has an inactivity/keepalive timeout shorter than a few minutes that isn't being satisfied by a command producing zero stdout. This wasted significant session time across three consecutive dispatch/diagnose/retry cycles before the detached-launch pattern was discovered empirically. Composes with BL-20260720-TRAINERDIAG-FENCE (same workflow, different failure class) — not fixed this session because the fix (likely a `ServerAliveInterval`/keepalive setting on the SSH step, or a documented requirement that any command expected to run >1min must self-detach) touches a shared workflow other sessions rely on. A secondary, related observation: the issue body's free-text prose AFTER the `cmd:` YAML block is also being fed to bash as part of the same script (confirmed repeatedly — e.g. a sentence beginning 'M27 Batch-4 (XAUUSD...' produced `bash: line N: syntax error near unexpected token '('`, and one beginning 'Retry of #7294...' produced `bash: line N: Retry: command not found`). These are currently harmless because the prose reliably fails as shell syntax, but it is latent — a future issue body whose free-text portion happens to parse as valid (and unintended) shell would silently execute it on the trainer VM.

items.title: [infra] Trainer's own ML cycle saturates 6 GB into deep swap (promotion-readiness ~3.2 GB) -> chronic OOM/wedge risk; external research jobs merely tip an already-saturated box
items.description: REFRAME (the key insight from the research session): the trainer's own cycle already pushes 6 GB deep into swap BEFORE any external research load — so this is a footprint/serialization problem on the box itself, not just 'don't run big sweeps'. ROOT CAUSE (verified in code this review, Tier-1 read): `ml/promotion/attribution.py` streams the shadow log via inspector.iter_records (a generator) but then MATERIALIZES it whole — `records = list(records)` (attribution.py:192; load path load_shadow_records -> aggregate at ~L322-327). So `ml promotion-readiness` loads the ENTIRE runtime_logs/shadow_predictions.jsonl (+ _backfill.jsonl) into RAM as ShadowRecord objects; that log has grown large since per-bar regime scoring went live (REGIME_BAR_SCORING) — hence 3.2 GB / ~99 min. FIX OPTIONS (Tier-2/3, operator-gated — NOT enacted here): (1) DON'T materialize: window/bound the shadow-log read to the relevant lookback before list(), or aggregate incrementally over iter_records without a full in-memory list (streaming reduce) — the single highest-leverage fix. (2) SERIALIZE the heavy ML stages within a cycle (promotion-readiness + `ml train` were overlapping) so a cycle can't swap-thrash itself; +nice/ionice. (3) CONTAINMENT: systemd MemoryMax / MemorySwapMax on the trainer service units so a runaway OOM-kills ONE job instead of wedging the whole box (a wedge currently needs an out-of-band reset-instance). CAPACITY NOTE: the Always-Free Ampere pool is FULL (4/24 OCPU-GB) so 'add RAM' is not free — this must be a footprint/serialization fix, not a resize. Cross-links: BL-20260712-TRAINER-JOB-SERIALIZATION (same health backlog — the SSH-starvation serialization ask; this is its concrete recurrence + root cause) and MB-20260705-TRAINER-OOM (ml-review backlog — the ML-lifecycle OOM signature). Full incident write-up: docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-REFINEMENT-2026-07-12.md (section 'M20-X sweep INCIDENT'). Coordination: the research session owns the M20-X sweep re-run and has gated it (won't launch unless available > 2 GB and swap < 500 MB), so no collision there; this item is the trainer's own memory-pressure fix.

items.source: PERF-20260601-001 root-cause (docs/research/trend-donchian-live-anomaly-rootcause-2026-07-11.md; trainer-vm-diag #6136). trend_donchian bybit_1 rows 2604/2607/2610 are setup_type='intent_reduce', exit_reason='reconciler_filled', entry_price==exit_price, yet carry a large non-NULL positive pnl (+$561/+620/+898).
items.title: Reconciler books an intent_reduce leg with a phantom non-NULL pnl (entry==exit) — contradicts apply_intent_reduce_partial_close's NULL-pnl design
items.description: A reduce leg is meant to carry NULL pnl (src/units/accounts/execute.py::apply_intent_reduce_partial_close leaves pnl/pnl_percent NULL, pnl_source='deferred_intent_reduce'), and order_monitor already treats reduce legs specially (is_reduce_leg). But some intent_reduce rows get closed via the reconciler_filled path with entry_price==exit_price AND a large fabricated positive pnl (trend_donchian demo 2604 +$561.28 / 2607 +$620.17 / 2610 +$898.60 — all entry==exit). That phantom pnl inflates any analytics that don't explicitly exclude reduce legs. Observed on DEMO here so no real-money impact, and the new exclude_reduce_leg_predicate (src/web/api/_clean_trades.py, applied in /strategy/attribution) now MASKS it in the read path — but the WRITE path should not book the phantom pnl at all (a real-money intent_reduce reconciler-flip would otherwise inject a fabricated win/loss upstream of any single reader). ROOT-CAUSE belongs to the reconciler close path (order_monitor.py _reconcile_open_trades / the reconciler_filled pnl computation for a row whose setup_type='intent_reduce'): it should defer/NULL the pnl for a reduce leg the same way the open-time path does, or skip pnl computation when entry==exit on a reduce leg. Cross-ref: the exclude_reduce_leg guard is defense-in-depth in the analytics layer; this item is the upstream write-path fix.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review touching the reconciler close path, OR a real-money intent_reduce leg appears with a non-NULL reconciler pnl.
items.resolution_criteria: The reconciler close path leaves pnl NULL (or a deferred marker) for an intent_reduce reduce leg instead of booking a phantom entry==exit pnl; a test covers a reduce-leg reconciler close asserting NULL pnl.

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid, Tier-2 code (reconciler books intent_reduce leg with phantom non-NULL pnl entry==exit, contradicts apply_intent_reduce_partial_close NULL-pnl design). Not independently re-triggered this window. Blocker: Tier-2 reconciler fix.

Write-path fix, 2 sites in order_monitor.py: (1) _close_trade_from_order_status now gates the pnl write on `not is_reduce_leg` + stamps pnl_source='deferred_intent_reduce' (a reduce leg's qty-matched closed_pnl on a netting account is the PARENT's realized close, so booking it fabricated the entry==exit +$561/+620/+898 rows); (2) _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced scan now excludes intent_reduce rows so the universal fallback can't re-fabricate the NULL. Reverses the #2974 attribution (which the read-path exclude_reduce_leg_predicate masked anyway); updated its test. Regression tests added (test_order_monitor_close_pnl reduce-leg assertion flipped + test_reconciler_reduce_and_shadow). Latent real-money PnL-integrity fix (bybit_2 netting).

items.source: Live incident 2026-07-09 ~22:14-22:37Z: an ib_paper MGC short (mgc_pullback_1d, pkg-a4a957610253455e, order 188, -9 @ 4128.91) tripped MONITOR BLIND (candles_unavailable 3 ticks) because the IB exec client's circuit breaker was open (gateway wedge). The alert reads 'Broker SL/TP backstop (if any) still holds' — but there is NO way to VERIFY that: _check_naked_positions is journal-driven (MGC's journal had sl/tp -> never flagged), and the broker-side resting-order verification (_check_broker_naked_equity_positions via AlpacaClient.has_protective_orders) is ALPACA-ONLY. items.title: No IB broker-side protection VERIFICATION — an IB futures position with journal SL/TP but no RESTING broker bracket is invisible to every naked check
items.description: GUARDRAIL GAP (operator asked for a guardrail on the MGC monitor-blind trade). For Alpaca, _check_broker_naked_equity_positions asks the broker whether a resting protective leg exists (has_protective_orders) and re-arms a GTC OCO if none; for IB there is no equivalent, so an IB position whose broker OCA bracket was never placed / got cancelled / failed during a breaker flap stays silently naked while the monitor is also blind. PROPOSED FIX (held for operator/supervised build): add IBClient.has_protective_orders(symbol) (account-wide reqAllOpenOrders read, fail-safe None on read failure) + an IB analogue of the broker-naked sweep that re-arms via the EXISTING _attempt_naked_autoprotect on a confirmed-clean 'no resting bracket' read. CRITICAL BUILD CONSTRAINTS: (1) do NOT add a per-monitor-tick account-wide IB order read — that risks re-triggering the tick-latency/pacing wedge class (BL-20260609); cadence-gate it. (2) IB order visibility is per-client-session — ib.openTrades() only sees THIS client's orders, so a readonly client would false-read 'naked'; must use reqAllOpenOrders (account-wide) and validate against the live gateway before trusting it to PLACE orders. (3) fail-safe: read failure/ambiguity -> skip, never place. Deliberately NOT shipped unsupervised overnight (order-placing path needs live IB cross-client validation).

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED. Root-caused from the trader journal: the ~18-min wedge was (a) a clean Error 326 clientId-in-use on the base id 498 (the gateway/socat side still holds the pre-restart session as active, so a fresh connect on 498 times out until reaped) AND (b) the freshly-rotated clientId's cold-socat-relay liveness probe repeatedly condemning a genuinely-healthy session (BL-20260610-009 cold-flow class, but at the probe). Fix shipped in two PRs: #6100 (teardown-before-reconnect + clientId rotation after N connect/probe failures + reset-window awareness) and #6114 (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER default 3->1 so rotation engages on the FIRST reconnect failure, + new IB_PROBE_TRUST_FRESH_HANDSHAKE default true so a probe timeout on a completed fresh handshake is best-effort, not a breaker-tripping condemnation; IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S still bounds each real fetch). items.source: src/prop/prop_journal.py::insert_fill — plain INSERT, no dedup. Live evidence: breakout_1 prop_fills id 15 (buy) + id 16 (long) are the SAME ETH trade (external_order_id 500139412) logged twice (the buy/long direction-synonym correction saga, BL-20260705-PROP-DIRECTION-SYNONYM-MATCH).
items.title: [prop] insert_fill is a blind append (no idempotency) — a re-reported / duplicate fill creates a second prop_fills row
items.description: prop_journal.insert_fill does a straight INSERT with no dedup guard, so re-posting the same fill (operator re-report, corrective re-report, or a relay retry) creates a duplicate prop_fills row. This is the SECONDARY double-log vector behind BL-20260706-PROP-CLOSE-MISLINK (the primary — a close linking to the wrong ticket — was fixed in #5744). Concrete residue: prop_fills 15/16 are the same trade (ext order 500139412) as two rows. FIX (Tier-2, prop DB write path): make insert_fill idempotent/upsert-ish on a natural key — (account_id, external_order_id, status) when external_order_id is present, else (account_id, ticket_id, status, qty, exit_price) — updating the existing row instead of inserting a duplicate; or at minimum flag/supersede the older duplicate in raw/notes. Prop journal is isolated from real-money/paper KPIs so this is data-hygiene, not money-at-risk. Verify with a re-post of an existing fill producing no new row.

updates.note: RESOLVED. insert_fill is now idempotent — it computes the natural key ((account_id, external_order_id, status) when external_order_id is present, else (account_id, ticket_id, status, qty, exit_price)), SELECTs any existing matching row, and UPDATEs it in place rather than inserting a duplicate; direction synonyms (buy->long / sell->short) are normalized so a corrective re-report under the canonical direction dedupes against the original. Shipped in #6079 (ae5dc3b), deployed to the live VM (#6082), covered by tests/test_prop_journal_idempotency.py (5 tests: re-report updates in place, buy/long synonym dedupe, distinct-status separate row, no-ext fallback-key dedupe, keyless append). This prevents ALL future duplicate prop fills. The single pre-existing historical duplicate (prop_fills id 15, a stale buy-direction row superseded by the canonical ticket-linked id 16 for ETH ext-order 500139412) is intentionally left uncleaned per operator decision (2026-07-09 "skip it"): it is cosmetic, on an already-closed trade, prop-only and isolated from all real-money/paper KPIs, and cleaning one row would require standing up a new allowlisted maintenance system-action for no material benefit.

items.source: journalctl -u ict-git-sync.service on the live VM: every fetch succeeded cleanly through 07:08:59Z (pulled 200a536c fine), then EVERY run since 07:14:18Z fails identically: 'fatal: could not read Username for "https://github.com": No such device or address' (exit 128). Confirmed via two independent pull-and-deploy system-action dispatches (issues #5659, #5661) at 07:55Z and 07:59Z, both hitting the exact same error — not transient.
items.title: ict-git-sync auto-deploy broken VM-wide since ~07:14Z today — git fetch can't authenticate to GitHub
items.description: Auto-deploy (`ict-git-sync.timer`, fires every ~5min) has been failing on EVERY run for the last ~50+ minutes as of this writing — this blocks ALL merged PRs from reaching the live VM, not just one. The live trader process itself (`ict-trader-live.service`) is unaffected and healthy (confirmed via the liveness-watchdog journal + /api/diag/services) — this is purely the deploy pipeline. `/api/diag/version` still reports git_sha=200a536c, the last commit that landed before the failure started. This directly blocked deploying the operator-approved IB liveness-probe fix (PR #5654, merged as ee522ca) for verification. Root cause is unknown from the diag surface available (no dispatchable action exists to inspect/fix a VM-side git credential — unlike the trainer VM's full-SSH relay, the live VM only has the fixed `system-actions.yml` allowlist + GET-only diag). The 'could not read Username' signature is the canonical symptom of an HTTPS git remote with no working credential (expired/revoked PAT, or a credential helper that stopped resolving) — git falls back to an interactive username prompt, which fails headless. Timing note: this VM has an open, known pattern of an OCI host-side agent silently mutating filesystem state without warning (BL-20260629-DEVNULL-CLOBBERED-LIVE-VM / BL-20260629-DEVNULL-OCI-SOURCE-KILL) — worth checking whether the same class of interference touched `~/.git-credentials` / the git credential helper around 07:09-07:14Z, though this is unconfirmed.
items.trigger_condition: Needs VM-side inspection this repo's current tooling can't do read-only (no arbitrary-shell relay for the live VM). Likely needs either (a) the operator to check/refresh whatever git credential the VM's origin remote relies on, or (b) a system-action addition (mirroring the gateway VM's unrestricted diag pattern, scoped read-only) if this needs to be self-diagnosable going forward.
items.resolution_criteria: ict-git-sync.service fetch succeeds again; a subsequent pull-and-deploy lands ee522ca (or later) and /api/diag/version reflects it.

check_log.note: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (operator): the repo was flipped from public to private this session, right around the failure window — the VM's anonymous HTTPS `git fetch` had never needed a credential before and now does. Fix prepared (PR TBD): deploy_pull_restart.sh now authenticates via an inline Basic-auth header built from a new optional VM_GIT_DEPLOY_TOKEN (fine-grained, Contents:Read-only PAT), read from .env (systemd EnvironmentFile= already exports it; a targeted single-line grep fallback covers a direct SSH/pull-and-deploy invocation). Falls back to the current plain fetch when unset, so this is a no-op until the token exists. Wired into the existing sync-vm-secrets.yml OPTIONAL_SECRETS propagation path (same mechanism as DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN). Operator is creating the token now. KNOWN GAP not yet addressed: the dedicated IB-Gateway VM has no .env by design and also does a plain `git clone`/fetch from this same repo (deploy/ib-gateway-cloud-init.yaml + the gateway branch of deploy_pull_restart.sh) — unverified whether it's currently affected; needs a separate propagation step if so. Filed as a standalone follow-up rather than blocking this fix.

RESOLVED. See resolution_note for the full two-recurrence history. Final state: global git credential set on ict-bot-arm, on-disk deploy_pull_restart.sh current (no duplicate-header bug), ict-trader-live.service restarted onto d5276f74, /api/diag/version confirms git_sha=d5276f74. Deploy pipeline is unblocked — other concurrent sessions were told they could resume.

items.resolution_note: Recurred twice after the initial fix before landing clean. (1) The per-invocation http.extraheader approach (first fix attempt) caused a duplicate-Authorization-header 400 once a global git credential was also set — http.extraheader is multi-valued, confirmed experimentally, not just assumed. Fixed by reverting deploy_pull_restart.sh to a plain fetch and relying solely on the global credential set by vm-git-credential-bootstrap.yml (PR #5678). (2) Even after that merged, pull-and-deploy failed identically again because the ON-DISK deploy_pull_restart.sh was itself still the old, broken pre-fix copy — same deadlock shape one level deeper. Fixed by extending vm-git-credential-bootstrap.yml to git reset --hard origin/main + invoke the deploy script directly when the worktree reads behind origin/main (PR #5681). Live-verified end to end: dispatched the bootstrap (issue #5682, exit 0, correctly reported the worktree behind origin/main + did the reset + ran the deploy script), caught that the deploy script itself skipped the service restart (zero diff after the outer reset) and explicitly dispatched restart-bot-service (issue #5683) to actually load the new code, then confirmed /api/diag/version reports git_sha=d5276f74 (the merged commit). ict-git-sync.timer now authenticates on every scheduled fetch.

updates.note: Gateway restart fired 2026-07-05T22:12Z via vm-ib-gateway-recover — succeeded cleanly (IBC login_completed=yes, api reachable, 22:12:34Z). Re-probed /api/diag/exchange_positions well after the ~2min circuit-breaker clear window: ib_paper STILL reads positions:null. BUT cross-checked the trader's OWN persistent connection: mgc_trend_1h has been evaluating MGC every ~3 min with live real-time prices through 06:28Z (close 4162.3->4157.7->...), including an actionable sell signal dispatched at 06:05:49Z (confidence 0.0539, correctly below threshold to execute) and another eval at 06:08:56Z (confidence 0.3476). /api/bot/accounts/balances confirms ib_paper api_ok:true, balance stable at $1,271,418.77, open_positions:0 (genuinely flat, not stale-masked). CONCLUSION: the live trading connection is fully healthy — this was never a real wedge. The diag relay's exchange_positions endpoint opens a SEPARATE short-lived read-only IB client per the diag-relay design, and that specific connection path appears to hit the same cross-host socat-relay quirk CLAUDE.md documents for IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S (reqCurrentTime doesn't resolve over the relayed gateway even when the persistent connection is healthy). Reclassified from 'operational IB issue' to 'diag-tooling limitation, no live impact' — closing. Do NOT burn another gateway restart on a future null exchange_positions read for ib_paper without first cross-checking live *_eval activity + accounts/balances api_ok, per this note.

STRUCTURAL FIX LANDED, superseding the diag-tooling-limitation reclassification above (PR #5789, branch claude/intelligent-dijkstra-hs2271). Root-caused the actual mechanism (not just the symptom): IBClient.connect() verified liveness (reqCurrentTime) but never guaranteed the FIRST real accountSummary()/portfolio() data had landed before declaring success — ib_insync's accountSummary() only populates from an explicit reqAccountSummary() subscription (never called anywhere in this repo) and, per ib_insync's own RequestTimeout defaulting to 0 (unbounded), that lazy first call had NO timeout of its own; portfolio() similarly depends on reqAccountUpdates(), which connect()'s own init requests race with a silently-swallowed timeout that never fails connect(). So account_open_positions()'s net_liquidation disambiguation (this item's title) could misreport 'not logged in' on a perfectly healthy gateway whenever the diag read client's cache was cold (first use, or a fresh reconnect after a silent idle-timeout drop) — exactly this item's symptom, and it recurred again in the 2026-07-06 weekly /system-review. Fix: IBClient.connect() now runs a bounded account/portfolio WARM-UP (subscribe + wait for real data, retry-once-then-condemn — same shape as the existing liveness probe) right after the liveness probe succeeds, gated to run once per underlying connection (a still-open cached handle skips it; a fresh connect or a reconnect after an idle drop re-runs it). New env var IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S (default 8.0s; <=0 opts out). By the time connect() returns success, balance()/positions() are always served from an already-warm cache — no cold race left to lose. Regression-tested (delayed data still succeeds; a genuinely wedged gateway is still bounded + trips the breaker; reconnect-after-idle-drop re-warms); full existing IB/accounts/reconciler suite (217+ tests) still green. NOT YET DEPLOYED to the live VM — this is Tier-2 (live IB connection/read behaviour); needs an explicit operator OK before restart-bot-service/pull-and-deploy is dispatched. This item stays 'resolved' (its own symptom was benign that day); tracking the deploy-and-verify follow-through as a NEW item is the correct next step if the operator wants a dedicated tracker, but the fix itself is code-complete and PR-linked here.

The 2026-07-06T20:00 warm-up fix above was deployed to the live VM and the concurrency bug it uncovered (MB-20260706-IBCONCURRENCY, separate PR #5809) was also fixed and deployed — but a clean single-request retest of /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper AFTER both fixes still returned positions:null, with the web-api journal showing 'account/portfolio warm-up timed out twice (8s + 8s retry)' for the diag read client specifically, while the trader's own persistent connection (different clientId) kept evaluating mgc_trend_1h on fresh real-time prices the entire time. Root-caused a SECOND, deeper mechanism: reqAccountUpdates (the call portfolio()/positions() depends on) is a persistent PER-ACCOUNT subscription. The trader's own execution connection (clientId 496/497) already holds it for ib_paper; the diag/reconciler read client (ib_read_client_for, a distinct PID-salted clientId, e.g. 9585) opening a SECOND concurrent reqAccountUpdates subscription for the SAME account is a documented IB-API multi-client collision — the Gateway does not reliably deliver a fresh accountDownloadEnd to the second subscriber. Structural fix (not a longer timeout): a readonly client's warm-up never subscribes to reqAccountUpdates at all, and IBClient.positions() now routes readonly reads through reqPositions() instead of portfolio() — a stateless, one-shot request IBKR documents as safe for any number of concurrent clients against the same account. Cost: no unrealizedPNL on this path (unrealised_pnl is None for an IB readonly read, the same 'not measured' contract dashboard.py::_broker_unrealised_for_trade already handles). The trader's own non-readonly connection is completely untouched — still portfolio()/reqAccountUpdates, unchanged. New tests added (TestReadonlyAccountUpdatesCollision in tests/test_ib_integration.py) proving the readonly warm-up never calls reqAccountUpdates even when it would hang, and that positions() uses reqPositions() not portfolio() for a readonly client. Full IB/accounts/reconciler/diag suite green. NOT YET DEPLOYED — Tier-2, needs operator OK before restart-bot-service/pull-and-deploy, then a clean re-verify of exchange_positions for ib_paper.

items.source: src/prop/ line-by-line audit (docs/audits/s-audit-f/prop-bridge.md F3). Three call sites independently classify 'is this a prop account' with DIFFERENT predicates: prop_journal._prop_scope (exchange==breakout OR account_class==prop OR type==prop OR backtest_ruleset!=standard), telegram_report_handler.default_prop_account (exchange==breakout OR account_class==prop only), account_rulesets.unit_for_account (backtest_ruleset!=standard OR exchange==breakout).
items.title: Three divergent is_prop_account predicates across src/prop/ — consolidate to one helper
items.description: Latent multi-account drift. Today the single prop account (breakout_1) matches all three predicates so they agree, but a future prop account declared by account_class:prop WITHOUT exchange:breakout would be invisible to default_prop_account's disambiguation, and one declared only by backtest_ruleset would be invisible to both default_prop_account and the journal-side reconcile scope. Fix: extract one canonical is_prop_account(acct: dict)->bool and have _prop_scope, default_prop_account, and unit_for_account all call it. Tier-1 refactor, no behaviour change under the current single account.

items.description: The intraday ETF cells (gld/slv/spy/qqq/tlt _1h) route to alpaca_options_paper and are being closed en masse by the reconciler (closeReason 'other') at a single instant with mark prices that are wildly wrong (underlying-vs-option pricing mismatch suspected: qty is treated as shares, e.g. SLV 95 × (58.82-53.29)=525.35, yet the exit price 53.29 is not a real SLV print). Net effects: (1) paper analytics/-/performance are contaminated by fabricated PnL — the -$845.65 window figure is meaningless; (2) the same reconciler path closed a REAL-money trade (bybit_2 ict_scalp #2995) with closeReason 'reconciler' rather than tp/sl, so the artifact mechanism is not paper-isolated. Investigate _reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions / _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced for alpaca_options_paper: why 6 positions read absent and were closed at one tick, and why the close-side mark price is implausible. Likely related to the options-expression overlay pricing ETF legs as the underlying.

updates.note: ROOT-CAUSED + already fixed in code. Mechanism: alpaca_options_paper holds us_option legs for its ETF debit-vertical expressions. Pre-fix, the reverse reconciler's account_open_positions returned those legs as adoptable positions and — not recognising the account as options-expressing — adopted them as equity `adopted_orphan` trades (entry = underlying spot), which the local-PnL sweep then priced with the EQUITY formula (local_markprice x qty x contract_value_usd=1.0) -> fabricated +/-$ hundreds (the -$845 paper figure). Trades 2999-3006 were adopted 18:47-18:56 and closed 19:05:48. FIXES (both live in deployed sha 5a2db1f2 since the ~20:08 restart): #4858 (19:01Z) made account_open_positions options-aware (options account -> returns ONLY us_option, so the reconciler no longer adopts the legs as equity orphans); #4867 (20:04Z) added the _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced options-defer guard (account_expresses_options -> skip the equity formula). The 18:47 adoptions PREDATE the ~20:08 deploy. Post-deploy trades (3007-3014, all >=21:42Z) show ZERO new alpaca_options_paper adoptions -> fix holding. RESIDUAL (no new code): (a) verify clean over 24-48h; (b) Tier-2 DB writeback to mark the ~8 pre-fix phantom paper rows reconcile_status='superseded' so they stop polluting paper KPIs (currently 'reconciled' = still counted). items.title: OPERATOR DECISION TO REVISIT: give alpaca_options_paper its OWN Alpaca paper login (separate keys) instead of sharing alpaca_paper's
items.description: SURFACE THIS TO THE OPERATOR at the next /system-review. The options-expression account `alpaca_options_paper` currently runs on the SAME Alpaca paper API keys as the equity account `alpaca_paper` (ALPACA_API_KEY_ID / ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY). Correctness now rests on TWO asset-class filters keeping the two bot-accounts' positions from colliding: (1) account_open_positions' `_alpaca_pos_in_scope` (us_option for the options account, non-us_option for the equity account) and (2) account_expresses_options resolving the `options` block from canonical accounts.yaml even when handed a stripped cfg (#4858). This is FRAGILE BY DESIGN — the 2026-06-27 orphan-adoption incident is exactly what happens when one of those filters sees an incomplete cfg. A dedicated second Alpaca paper login (its own key pair at e.g. ALPACA_API_KEY_ID_OPTIONS / ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY_OPTIONS, wired via accounts.yaml api_key_env/api_secret_env + sync-vm-secrets.yml) would make the isolation STRUCTURAL (two brokers never see each other's positions) instead of filter-dependent, removing the shared-login failure mode entirely. TRADE-OFF the operator weighed: a 2nd account is more setup (new Alpaca paper account + keys + secret propagation) vs. the shared login which 'just works' but needs the two guards to stay correct forever. RECOMMENDATION (mine, for the operator to decide): move to a dedicated paper login before this pattern is reused on alpaca_live (real money) — a shared real-money login with this same filter-dependent isolation is a materially worse place to discover a stripped-cfg regression. items.source: PR #4441 (merged to main as squash 5830136c, deployed via ict-git-sync) fixed the perpetual MHG/ib_paper adopt→sl_cross→re-orphan flap. Root cause: IBClient.close returned retCode 0 the moment the opposing market order was ACCEPTED (or still pending) — it never confirmed the position reached flat — so an accepted-but-unfilled close marked the DB row closed (sl_cross) while the real IB position stayed open and (because close() Step 1 cancels the protective bracket) naked, then got re-orphaned. Fix: (1) IBClient.close now re-reads the live position and requires flat within IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S (default 6s, <=0 disables) else returns retCode 1 so the monitor leaves the DB row open + retries; (2) order_monitor._apply_update arms a per-(account,symbol,direction) close-retry cooldown (IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S, default 300s, 0 disables) on a 'not confirmed flat' close so it doesn't churn the re-armed bracket every tick. Post-deploy verification (2026-06-24 ~13:00) was POSITIVE: trader restarted (new PID), trade 2832 closed exchange_flat_reconciled, NO new MHG adopted_orphan rows for ~80 min, no sl_cross/adopt/orphan churn lines.

Healthy state: an IB sl_cross close either CONFIRMS flat (DB closes once, exchange_flat_reconciled or a real exit) or, when the venue can't fill (market closed / gateway mid-reset), the row stays OPEN with the bracket armed and a 'close retry cooling down' log — NOT a new orphan per cycle. Also sanity-check the two knobs are still at sane values on the VM (IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S>0, IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S>0; a stray 0 in .env disables the guard — same failure-mode class as the dropped POSITION_NETTING_GUARD env on the Ampere migration). The automated recovery path (scripts/ops/backfill_orphan_pnl.py + the new in-line watchdog recovery in PR #4058) can only reconstruct a real exit/PnL from Bybit's /v5/position/closed-pnl, which Bybit retains for ONLY ~7 days. But the 2026-06-21 backfill run found 15 OLD orphans (trade ids 990-1000, 1046-1048, 1454) that ALL returned account_closed_pnl=None — i.e. they are past Bybit's 7-day window and are PERMANENTLY unrecoverable via the exchange API. items.source: Observed in the live-VM deploy log during the 2026-06-16 #3844 pull-and-deploy (and again in passing this session): a candle/market fetch raised 'bybit does not have market symbol MHGN6'. MHGN6 is the IBKR contract-month-qualified symbol for MHG (micro copper, June-2026 expiry). The fetch was routed to Bybit, which has no such market.
items.title: Candle/market fetch for IBKR contract-month symbols (e.g. MHGN6) misroutes to Bybit — connector_for_symbol profile lookup is keyed by root, not the contract-qualified symbol
items.description: src/runtime/market_data.py::connector_for_symbol looks up the instrument profile by EXACT symbol (load_instrument_profiles().get(symbol)). config/instruments.yaml keys metals/index futures by ROOT (MHG/MES/MGC), so a contract-month-qualified symbol like 'MHGN6' misses the profile, exchange stays None, and it falls back to the process default EXCHANGE (bybit) → 'bybit does not have market symbol MHGN6'. The qualified symbol most likely enters the fetch path via an adopted-orphan IB position / order-monitor mark-price lookup (the reverse_reconciler adopts IB positions under their contract-qualified symbol, cf. trade #2540's MHGN6 in BL-20260612-001). Best-effort path (fetch_candles logs + returns None), so no crash — but it means no candle/mark data for that position and a noisy error per attempt. FIX (Tier-1/2): in connector_for_symbol, when the exact-symbol profile lookup misses, fall back to a futures-root normalization (strip the contract-month suffix, e.g. MHGN6→MHG) before defaulting to the process EXCHANGE — mirror the base-futures-root resolution already used in order_monitor._resolve_protective_levels / positions symbol-or-base-futures-root matching. Verify MHGN6/MESM6/etc. route to IBKR.

items.title: vm-diag-snapshot burst requests silently cancelled despite cancel-in-progress:false — GitHub keeps only ONE pending run per concurrency group
items.description: The 2026-05-16 comment in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml ('requests queue and each completes in turn — no silent cancellations') is wrong for bursts: GitHub Actions allows at most one PENDING run per concurrency group regardless of cancel-in-progress, so each newly-queued diag-request cancels the previously queued one; only the running + newest-pending survive. The cancelled-run commenter never fires for queued-cancelled runs (same gap the 2026-05-16 note described), so the requesting session sees an open issue with no reply. diag-data SKILL.md pitfall text fixed this session (space requests ~90s / confirm previous result before filing the next). REMAINING (Tier-1 CI): fix the stale workflow comment; optionally drop the concurrency group (runs are read-only and cheap) or key the group on the issue number so concurrent requests don't share one lane.

items.description: Fix 3 (IB decoupling): src/exchange/ib_connector.py's IBMarketData.get_ohlcv does NOT consult the IBClient circuit breaker, so a wedged gateway costs ~5s probe + 8s fetch per MES symbol PER TICK on the main loop (heartbeat starvation). Watchdog state machine (the deeper half of Fix 2): scripts/check_ib_gateway.py treats 'gateway down' (restart helps) and 'gateway up but can't authenticate' (restart just churns) identically; with the container now capped the churn is harmless, but a smarter watchdog could distinguish them and back off harder / probe-only on persistent auth-failure (without the --exhaustion-reset-min re-churn) while still auto-recovering when IBKR returns. PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1 tooling): in gate-check, when the manifest's evaluator is multiclass, default the baseline trainer to RegimeClassifierTrainer (or have compute_oos_edge auto-pick an evaluator-compatible baseline) so oos_edge 'just works' for regime heads and the gate is not silently un-evaluable. items.source: 2026-06-05 live-trader restart-loop incident (issues #2793-#2813). Root mechanism confirmed from scripts/check_heartbeat.py + the live journal.
items.title: Liveness-watchdog autoheal can run a PERPETUAL restart loop — last_autoheal_streak only rate-limits (~3 min), it never caps; and it kills a trader still inside a slow first tick
items.description: INCIDENT ROOT MECHANISM. ict-liveness-watchdog (scripts/check_heartbeat.py --auto-restart-after 3 --interval 60) restarts ict-trader-live every ~3 min when the heartbeat is stale. _maybe_autoheal fires when stale_streak - last_autoheal_streak >= 3, then sets last_autoheal_streak = stale_streak; but stale_streak resets to 0 ONLY when the heartbeat goes fresh (check_heartbeat.py:390). When the trader is killed mid-first-tick BEFORE it ever writes a heartbeat (the heartbeat is written in src/main.py's sleep loop, AFTER the first run_pipeline tick completes), the heartbeat never goes fresh -> stale_streak climbs forever -> the gate re-opens every 3 checks -> the watchdog autoheals every ~3 min INDEFINITELY. On 2026-06-05 the trader's first tick was slow/hung (clock-skew Bybit failures + logged-out IB Gateway MES timeouts; see BL-20260605-002/003/004), so every restarted instance was killed before heartbeating -> a self-perpetuating loop that ran ~4.5h (from ~04:23Z). The CLAUDE.md claim that 'last_autoheal_streak gates re-fires so we won't get a restart-loop on a persistently broken trader' is FALSE — it only spaces restarts by threshold, it does not cap them. boot-grace (--boot-grace-seconds 600) also did not help post-reboot: the slow first tick exceeded the 10-min grace. FIX (Tier-2 code): (a) cap consecutive autoheal restarts + cooldown then alert-only, mirroring scripts/check_ib_gateway.py (--max-restarts 3 --cooldown-min 20); (b) do NOT autoheal a trader that was (re)started very recently / is still completing startup+first-tick (gate on unit ActiveEnterTimestamp or a 'started but no first heartbeat yet' grace scaled to worst-case first-tick time); (c) fix the CLAUDE.md text. MITIGATION IN PLACE: autoheal is currently PAUSED via the new pause-autoheal system-action (PR #2806) — see BL-20260605-006; resume only once the trader can complete a tick AND this hardening ships.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review; prioritise — this is the mechanism that turned a slow first tick into a 4.5h outage. Also confirm autoheal has been resumed once the trader is healthy (BL-20260605-006).
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/check_heartbeat.py caps consecutive autoheal restarts with a cooldown (then alert-only) AND does not kill a trader still completing its first post-restart tick; verified by inducing a slow-first-tick and confirming no unbounded restart loop. CLAUDE.md liveness-watchdog note corrected. Operator-approved PR (live-VM-consumed unit + script).
items.triage_note: 2026-06-06 /health-review: ROOT TRIGGER eliminated + verified, but the requested WATCHDOG-SIDE hardening is still unshipped. The 06-05 fixes (PRs #2814/#2827) attacked the cause — a hung IB gateway can no longer stall a tick (circuit breaker fail-fast, verified live in journal #2853) and the heartbeat now writes at tick-START — so a slow-first-tick can no longer feed the autoheal-every-3-min loop. Confirmed live: trader uptime stable 87+min (a loop would reset it every ~3min), autoheal re-armed (ict-liveness-watchdog.timer active, #2852). HOWEVER scripts/check_heartbeat.py still has NO consecutive-restart cap and CLAUDE.md's text is not confirmed corrected — the defense-in-depth the resolution_criteria asks for is pending a Tier-2 operator PR. Keep OPEN; loop is materially de-risked, not structurally capped.

check_log.note: CORRECTION (self-retraction): an earlier read of this session inferred '>=2 trader restarts in ~1h' from bot_uptime_s (1666 @06:47Z -> 4008 @08:23Z). The trader JOURNAL (07:14:30-07:18:00Z, issue #2885) DISPROVES it: PID 387659 runs CONTINUOUSLY and ticks normally across the window ('Sleeping 60 seconds', next 'Pipeline start'), no PID change, no restart at ~07:16. So bot_uptime_s is NOT literal process uptime here (reported 4008 vs true ~7440 since the ~06:19 start) -> the 'churn' was a counter artifact, not real restarts. NET: NO restart churn; the trader is STABLE. Moreover the circuit breaker (#2827) is verified WORKING LIVE: at 07:15:51 the trader hit IB ConnectionRefused, tripped the breaker, logged 'Suppressing IB calls so the trader loop is not blocked', and kept ticking on BTCUSDT — exactly the designed isolation. The slow-first-tick autoheal loop this item targets is NOT occurring. The watchdog consecutive-restart CAP is still unshipped (defense-in-depth) but there is no active loop to de-risk right now. Keep OPEN for the cap only; downgraded from 'live concern' to 'latent hardening'. (Minor follow-up: bot_uptime_s under-reporting is a status.json observability nit.)

ESCALATING EVIDENCE — the OTHER failure mode (autoheal does NOT fire when it SHOULD) bit live today. During the 2026-06-09 review the trader hard-wedged 06:18->06:57Z (heartbeat frozen 06:27:45, label=stopped at 14+min; no completed tick since 06:18:12; runtime_status.json + bot_uptime frozen at 06:18:13) under live-VM CPU saturation (95-100%). A >30-min hard hang FAR exceeds the 8-min --auto-restart-after threshold, yet the watchdog did NOT restart the trader — recovery came from an UNRELATED deploy-restart at 06:57 (sha b3370cb6->4cb0405e). So beyond the unbounded-loop hazard this item already tracks, autoheal apparently failed to act on a genuine stall: either it is paused again (BL-20260605-006) or check_heartbeat.py cannot/ did not restart a CPU-starved-but-alive process. Full incident in BL-20260609-001. The watchdog hardening this item asks for must ALSO ensure autoheal reliably fires on a real hang, not just cap runaway restarts. Still OPEN; priority raised.

HARDENING SHIPPED + DEPLOYED + ARMED (PR #3074, merged f65542e, pull-and-deploy #3079). check_heartbeat.py now: per-episode restart cap (--max-restarts 5) -> one-shot [CRITICAL] EXHAUSTED then alert-only; cooldown (--cooldown-min 3); startup-grace (--restart-startup-grace-seconds 180) so a trader mid-first-tick isn't bounced; AND a restart that FAILS TO DISPATCH (systemctl timing out under CPU saturation — the prime suspect for today's non-fire) no longer burns an attempt or starts the cooldown, so it retries next check instead of going silent. 35 tests pass. items.source: 2026-06-05 incident — trader journal for pid 1254/29483/43093 shows the first run_pipeline tick blocking on market-data fetches.
items.title: Per-tick market-data fetches (IBKR/MES + Bybit) block the BTCUSDT pipeline + heartbeat — a down PAPER gateway / a clock-skewed Bybit auth can stall the LIVE-money loop and the liveness signal
items.description: INCIDENT CONTRIBUTOR. The first run_pipeline tick synchronously fetches market data for every tick symbol. With the IB Gateway logged out, each MES/IBKR fetch times out ~10s x 3 timeframes (ib_insync: Connected -> Disconnected -> 'API connection failed: TimeoutError'); and with the VM clock skewed (BL-20260605-003) the Bybit signed market-data fetch fails (ErrCode 10002) and intermittently HARD-HANGS (pid 29483 sat at 'Pipeline start' 29 min consuming ~1 min CPU = blocked on a network call, no enforced timeout). Because the heartbeat is only written AFTER a tick completes, a stalled fetch starves the heartbeat -> the liveness watchdog autoheals (BL-20260605-001) -> restart loop. NET: a secondary/paper data source (IBKR) being down, or a transient Bybit auth failure, can take down the live-money trader. FIX (Tier-2 code): make per-tick market-data fetches non-fatal to the loop + heartbeat — short, enforced timeouts on every connector fetch so none can block indefinitely; skip/short-circuit a symbol whose feed is down rather than blocking the whole tick; and/or write the heartbeat from a path that cannot be starved by a hung fetch (separate liveness thread, or write heartbeat at tick-START as well as tick-end). The dashboard /api/bot/candles already fails best-effort; the trader signal-builder fetch path needs the same discipline.

items.resolution_criteria: A down IBKR gateway and/or a transient Bybit fetch failure no longer prevents the trader from completing a tick + writing a heartbeat within the watchdog window — verified by inducing an IBKR-down condition and confirming BTCUSDT keeps ticking + heartbeating. Tier-2 code (src/runtime market-data path + src/main heartbeat) — operator-approved PR.

items.source: /health-review — operator-flagged squeeze_breakout_4h Telegram sequence (2026-05-31 16:00-16:15 UTC)
items.title: Misleading 'TRADE OPENED — SHORT' ping on an intent_reduce leg (carries parent LONG's entry/SL/TP)
items.description: VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA, NOT A REAL TRADING BUG — notification-only. When the multi-strategy intent layer emits an intent_reduce/close leg, coordinator._delta_to_legs does dataclasses.replace(pkg, direction=delta.side) to flip the leg's direction to the opposite (reduce-only) side, but KEEPS the parent package's entry/sl/tp. execute_pkg then fires enqueue_trade_open(side=pkg.direction) (execute.py:881) for the reduce leg, so the operator sees '🟢 TRADE OPENED — BTCUSDT SHORT' with Entry 73693.8 / SL 72385.78 (BELOW) / TP 80989.49 (ABOVE) — SL/TP levels that are correct for a LONG, not a short. Ground truth (trade 1949, bybit_1): setup_type=intent_reduce, a 0.007 reduce-only SHORT leg trimming the open LONG position (pkg-838fe5ef, dir=long, the squeeze 4h winner), NOT a new short entry. The position was never short. Two sub-issues: (a) a reduce/close leg should not fire the 'TRADE OPENED' lifecycle ping at all (it's a partial close, not an open) — or should be labelled 'POSITION REDUCED'; (b) if it does ping, it must not show the parent's open-side SL/TP on the opposite-side leg. Fix is in the notification path only (execution_diagnostics.enqueue_trade_open call site in execute.py + the reduce-leg branch in coordinator), Tier-2 (touches execute.py / coordinator.py which the live VM consumes) — propose via PR, do not self-merge.

items.description: VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA, NOT A REAL TRADING BUG — alerting false-positive. coordinator.multi_account_execute emits the high-priority 'ALL accounts failed to dispatch' roll-up whenever NO account placed a trade in a round (line 1617: `not any(r.trade_id)`). But under FLIP_POLICY=hold (the live default since PR #2451), an opposite-side signal against an open position is INTENTIONALLY suppressed to a noop (intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy) — zero trades placed is the CORRECT, designed outcome, not a dispatch failure. On 2026-05-31 16:15 the squeeze short signal (id 1951 bybit_1 / 1952 bybit_2) was correctly held (open long present), yet the operator got a 🚨 ALL-accounts-failed alert. The roll-up should treat a round where every account result is an intent_noop (at_target / flip_suppressed_hold_policy / hold) as a benign no-op, NOT a failure — only genuine errors (RiskBreach, exchange_rejected, missing creds) should trip the 🚨 alarm. Fix in coordinator.py:1617 guard (exclude intent_noop reasons) + possibly execution_diagnostics.enqueue_all_accounts_failed_dispatch. Tier-2 (live-path file) — propose via PR.

items.title: ib_paper account has no ib_port — MES order client cannot reach IB Gateway
items.description: The live trader logs `ib_client_for(ib_paper): no ib_port set (config or IB_PORT env) — cannot reach IB Gateway.` on every tick that routes to ib_paper. IB *market data* works (the gateway is up after the 2026-05-25 restart and MES candle fetches succeed via IBMarketData on 127.0.0.1:4002), so MES ticks complete fast and the heartbeat is stable. But the ib_paper account's ORDER client (src/units/accounts/clients.py::ib_client_for) has no ib_port configured, so it cannot place orders on MES — the account effectively collects signals/data but can't execute. If MES is intended to trade (paper), config/accounts.yaml::ib_paper needs `ib_port: 4002` (or the IB_PORT env on the trader unit). Pre-existing (predates this session); surfaced during post-deploy verification. Operator was informed in chat 2026-05-25 and chose to log it rather than fix immediately.

If yes, set ib_port (4002) on the ib_paper account in config/accounts.yaml (Tier-3 change, operator-approved) and confirm the trader log no longer emits 'no ib_port set' + a smoke order reaches IB Gateway. If MES is data-only by design, document that and close.

Status snapshot shows ib_paper live=true on sha 6a7aef4; no journalctl pull this review (relay queue wedged after 13 min — 3 of 6 issues never returned). The order-client gap (separate from IB market-data which works) would still emit the per-tick warning. Remains operator-gated (Tier-3); no change.
items.resolution: PR #2167 (squashed as 288d9bf) forwarded ib_host/ib_port/ib_account/ib_client_id through _load_account_cfgs_for_reconcile in src/runtime/order_monitor.py. The original diagnosis attributed the warning to the ORDER client (coordinator.py::multi_account_execute calling ib_client_for(account_cfg)), but that path's account_cfg already carries ib_port via getattr(account, 'ib_port', None) at coordinator.py:1045 — confirmed by reading the code. The actual emitter was the MONITOR RECONCILER path: _load_account_cfgs_for_reconcile() built an account_cfg dict that only forwarded a subset of fields and dropped the IB connection keys, so account_open_positions(cfg) → ib_read_client_for(account) → ib_client_for(...) → account.get('ib_port') = None → warning + return None. Fired from 4 call sites in order_monitor.py (1523, 1877, 2491, 3463), each on a 60s monitor tick — hence the per-tick spam. Post-deploy verification on diag-request #2169 confirmed: 'ib_client_for warning count: 0' across 300 lines / ~5 ticks; reconciler successfully opened the IB read socket (clientId 9731 visible at 17:57:38). MES order dispatch was never actually blocked — the data-collection-only framing in the original description was incorrect.

items.title: MES regime models (mes-regime-5m/15m) collapse to one class (f1_volatile=0) — model/feature limitation, NOT data-blocked
items.description: mes-regime-5m-baseline-v1 + mes-regime-15m-baseline-v1 never predict 'volatile' (recall_volatile=precision_volatile=f1_volatile=0; acc ~0.49-0.53). IMPORTANTLY this is NOT the missing-MES-trade-data blocker: these train on MES market_features (price history), which IS present and BALANCED — 5m: 60957 range / 25916 volatile (~70/30); 15m: 17694/11278 (~61/39). So it will NOT self-resolve when IBKR is approved + MES starts trading. Root cause: RegimeClassifierTrainer is a per-bucket MODAL-class classifier (ml/trainers/regime_classifier.py) keyed on the backward-looking vol_bucket; on MES that backward vol_bucket does not separate the (forward-vol-based) regime_label, so every bucket is range-majority and argmax always picks 'range'. BTC works because BTC vol is autocorrelated; MES intraday isn't. Operator decision 2026-05-25: LEAVE manifests as-is for now (do NOT demote to research_only); revisit in a dedicated model-training session.

items.source: operator flagged a live BTCUSDT trade whose TP (~143,210) sat ~2x the BTC price / above the all-time high
items.title: EXPECTED, NOT A BUG: trend_donchian (+ fade/squeeze) place a far ~50R 'unreachable sentinel' TP — don't re-flag it as a broken take-profit
items.description: A live trend_donchian BTCUSDT long showed TP=143,210.10 with SL=76,355.40 (entry ~77,666; current ~77,300). This is the DESIGNED 50R sentinel, not a malfunction. trend_donchian/fade_breakout_4h/squeeze_breakout_4h have NO fixed profit target (matches their backtests, which have no TP) — the Chandelier ATR trailing stop is the sole profit exit. But the pipeline's dispatch gate requires every order to carry BOTH an SL and a TP, so the TP is parked tp_r*risk away (tp_r=50.0 in config/strategies.yaml:153/216/259) where it can't realistically fill (max single-trade excursion in 3yr backtest ~11R). Signature to recognize it: reward:risk ~= 50:1. Math check on this trade: TP = entry + 50*(entry - SL) => 77,666.27 + 50*1,310.87 = 143,209.8 ~= 143,210.10. Formula lives at src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:190/195 (order_package) and the trade is protected by the live ratcheting trail in monitor() at trend_donchian.py:285 (moves SL up only, never loosens). The TP-cross close at trend_donchian.py:342 exists only for completeness. A far TP carries no margin/liquidation risk; if BTC ever printed 143k the trade would simply close at +50R. The only live strategy that emits this is trend_donchian (turtle_soup uses tp1_at_r 1.0 / tp2_at_r 3.0, ict_scalp tp_at_r 1.5, vwap a VWAP-anchored TP) — fade/squeeze share the 50R sentinel and (as of 2026-05-25) also run execution: live, so their 50R TPs now appear on real bybit_2 order packages too — still the intended sentinel (see BL-20260525-008).
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run that scores a trend_donchian / fade_breakout_4h / squeeze_breakout_4h order package and sees a TP far from price (~50R / ~2x BTC). Recognize it as the intended sentinel — do NOT score it as a TP defect.

items.source: Investigating the trend_donchian stuck-watchdog alert (trade 1722 / pkg-ac6bb4b3b33f4339); fixed the alert symptom in PR #2002
items.title: Zero-sized same-direction reinforcement signals persist as open order_packages (clutter + watchdog churn)
items.description: trend_donchian (and any breakout strategy) re-fires a same-direction signal on each new bar while the breakout persists. The intent multiplexer correctly refuses to pyramid onto an already-open position — it sizes the reinforcement to target_qty=0.0 (aggregation_reason 'same_direction_reinforcement: ... max target_qty=0.0', sized_qty_by_account={}) — but the zero-qty package is STILL persisted as status='open' with linked_trade_id set, even though no exchange order was placed. These ghost packages never close on their own; their updated_at goes stale and they accumulate in order_packages, and they are what trips the stuck-strategy watchdog (the live snapshot for trade 1722 showed pkg-ac6bb4b3b33f4339 and earlier ones already watchdog_released_alive). PR #2002 made the watchdog timeframe-aware so it no longer false-alerts on these, but the underlying clutter remains. Root fix: a reinforcement that sizes to 0 (no order to monitor) should NOT create a lingering open order_packages row — either skip persisting it, persist it with a terminal status (e.g. status='skipped'/'no_order' + close_reason), or auto-close it so it's never gated/monitored/watchdog'd. Verify the strategy_monocle gate (pipeline.py::_has_open_package_for_strategy) and the per-strategy gates still behave correctly afterward.

items.resolution_criteria: A same-direction reinforcement that aggregates to target_qty=0 no longer leaves a lingering status='open' order_packages row (it is skipped or persisted terminal), so ghost packages stop accumulating and the stuck-watchdog has nothing benign to flag. items.source: /health-review 2026-05-27 — three of six diag-relay issues opened back-to-back never returned a comment
items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay: subset of issues opened in quick succession never comment+close (stuck OPEN; 38 stale opens accumulated since 2026-05-17)
items.description: This review opened six diag issues at 2026-05-27T07:19:28..54Z. Three returned comments within 30s and auto-closed normally (#2125 status, #2128 order_packages, #2130 trainer-vm). Three never returned a comment in 16+ min and stayed OPEN (#2126 services, #2127 audit, #2129 trades). Cross-check: there are now 38 open vm-diag-request issues going back to #1327 (2026-05-17) — a chronic accumulation. Hypothesis: when issues open within seconds of each other, the concurrency-group serializer (`group: vm-diag-snapshot, cancel-in-progress: false`) starts them but a subset of runs fail/timeout SSH or curl in a way that the post-step `if: cancelled()` / `if: failure()` comment-back step doesn't fire — so the issue is left open with no comment. The 2026-05-16 commentary in vm-diag-snapshot.yml already flagged this exact failure mode (#1278/#1281/#1284). Effect: /health-review can't reliably pull a full state set in one fire; chronic open-issue clutter on the repo. Code-level fix needed in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml: add an always() post-step that drops a 'workflow ran but produced no output / failed at step X' comment so the issue stops looking 'in flight'.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or any session that opens >2 diag issues in quick succession and notices subsequent ones never return.
items.resolution_criteria: vm-diag-snapshot.yml carries an `if: always()` (or `if: cancelled()` + `if: failure()`) closing-comment step that ALWAYS posts a result-or-error comment + closes the issue, so no diag issue can be left silently OPEN. Then sweep the 38 stale open issues — close as 'workflow run silently failed; re-open if you need the data'. Code change (Tier-1 observability); not editable from /health-review.
items.resolution: ROOT-CAUSE refined 2026-05-27: vm-diag-snapshot.yml ALREADY carries `if: cancelled()` + `if: failure()` + an implicit-success handler that together cover every terminal job state. The remaining gap is when GitHub's webhook layer batches rapidly-filed `issues.opened` events and silently drops some — the workflow never starts, so none of the handlers fire. There's no in-workflow fix for that. Instead, a SEPARATE sweeper workflow `.github/workflows/diag-relay-sweep.yml` was shipped (PR #2144, merged 2026-05-27 ~09:50Z): daily cron at 06:00 UTC + on-demand workflow_dispatch; finds open `vm-diag-request` / `trainer-vm-diag-request` issues >30 min old with no `github-actions[bot]` reply, comments + closes them. VERIFIED 2026-05-28: the first 06:00 UTC cron ran and cleared the entire stale backlog — `list_issues(label=vm-diag-request, state=OPEN)` returned 0 (the ~38 issues going back to #1327 are all closed). The webhook-drop wedge still recurs (this review's #2173/#2174/#2175 never returned and were closed manually), but that is now an accepted condition: the sweeper cleans up any silently-dropped issue within ≤24h, so no diag-request stays OPEN indefinitely. Mitigation confirmed working end-to-end.

items.source: Today's IB Gateway wedge — Up 21h, upstream IB session dead.
items.title: IBC nightly auto-restart doesn't reliably recover the upstream IB session
items.description: IBC's `Auto restart time` is configured to 11:59 PM on the ib-gateway container (verified in the IBC log on issue #2165 post-recovery: `Auto restart time already set to 11:59 PM`). Yet today the container was 'Up 21 hours' with its upstream IB session entirely dead (Warning 2103 usfarm / 2105 ushmds / 2157 secdefnj all 'broken'; every API call timed out at 10s; 200/200 log lines were `remove Client <id>` with no upstream activity). Either IBC's nightly restart didn't fire, or it fired and didn't successfully re-authenticate to IB's data farms. The autonomous `vm-ib-gateway-recover` workflow is the current mitigation (Claude can dispatch it whenever the symptom recurs), but the root cause needs investigating. Candidates: 2FA timing on the nightly relogin, stale Java/Gateway state on Auto-restart that needs a hard container restart, or IB-side throttling on rapid reconnects. Probable scope: inspect IBC config (jts.ini, ibc.ini) + the docker entrypoint + gateway startup logs around the 11:59 PM window over multiple days to see if the restart fires at all.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; investigate via gateway-logs + provision_ib_gateway.sh on the next 12-24h MES outage.
items.resolution_criteria: Either IBC's nightly auto-restart reliably re-establishes the upstream IB session (verifiable by 7 consecutive days with no `Up >20h with broken farm connections` state), or a sanctioned scheduled job replaces it (e.g. systemd timer triggering vm-ib-gateway-recover at 11:55 PM UTC, before IB's reset window).
items.resolution: ROOT CAUSE REFINED 2026-05-28 (corrects the original 2FA/nightly-restart hypotheses). gateway-logs (issue #2184) showed the container 'Up 13h' but logged OUT of IBKR since `2026-05-28 04:30:50 IBC: detected dialog entitled: Unrecognized Username or Password` — i.e. during IBKR's overnight server-reset window the Gateway's in-place re-login hit a TRANSIENT bad-credential dialog and IBC parked on it, never retrying. NOT 2FA (the paper account DUQ325724 logs in with no 2FA — confirmed by the #2185 recover log: 'Click button: Paper Log In' → 'Login has completed', no Mobile prompt). NOT a real bad password (a full container restart re-logins cleanly — that's why vm-ib-gateway-recover works). NOT `restart: unless-stopped` (the process hangs on the dialog, it never dies, so Docker never restarts it). The gap: nothing auto-recovers a stuck login-failure dialog (`TWOFA_TIMEOUT_ACTION=restart` only covers 2FA timeouts, which never fire for paper). FIX (operator-approved 2026-05-28, branch claude/health-check-CjAWV, draft PR #2183): a symptom-driven auto-heal watchdog — scripts/check_ib_gateway.py + deploy/ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.{service,timer}, firing every 5 min: probes ib_paper via ib_connect_check (healthy ⇔ connected AND net_liquidation populated — a logged-out gateway reports connected=true but net_liquidation=None), and after 2 consecutive wedged checks runs scripts/ops/restart_ib_gateway.sh, with max-restarts=3 + 20-min cooldown so a genuine bad-cred/lockout can never become a restart loop (then it alert-only escalates). The fixed daily scheduled-restart option was considered and DROPPED as non-structural per operator — the watchdog self-heals any wedge within ~5-10 min, fine for delayed paper data. REMAINING: operator merge + pull-and-deploy, then verify the watchdog auto-heals across a few overnight IBKR resets (target: no manual vm-ib-gateway-recover needed).

items.source: Post-deploy journal during PR #2167 ship — first signal emitted after deploy triggered FCM push attempts that all 404'd.
items.title: FCM mobile-push notifier hits Firebase with stale / unregistered device tokens (404 NOT_FOUND)
items.description: When the trader emitted a fresh BTCUSDT VWAP signal at 2026-05-27T17:57:30Z, the M12 mobile-push notifier (src/runtime/mobile_push/notifier.py) fired FCM push attempts that came back `status=404 body={"error":{"code":404, "message":"Requested entity was not found.","status":"NOT_FOUND","details":[...FcmEr...]}}` — Google saying the device registration tokens FCM is targeting don't exist. Visible in the post-deploy journalctl on issue #2168. Means notifications aren't reaching the Android app. Either the dashboard/Android app never registered tokens after FCM init, or the tokens stored in the bot's token store are stale (device uninstall / FCM revocation / token rotation). Notifier should be marking these tokens as dead on 404 and stop retrying them; investigate whether notifier.py implements the FCM `UNREGISTERED` cleanup (remove-on-404) or silently retries. Pre-existing (the FCM key leak earlier today is unrelated — that was about the credential shape in .env, not the device tokens).

items.source: Today's FCM-credential bleed incident (issue #2157).
items.title: Operator-only follow-ups from the FCM private-key bleed
items.description:
The 2026-05-27 systemd-EnvironmentFile bleed dumped the FCM service-account PEM private key into the journalctl tail on TWO pull-and-deploy issue comments. PR #2158 shipped the scrub-env-noncompliant system-action and it ran successfully (12 lines stripped, journal warning is now gone — verified on issue #2161). What's left is operator-only because the MCP tools I have can neither delete issue comments (no delete_issue_comment) nor vacuum the journal (no journalctl vacuum system-action) nor rotate the FCM key (that's Google Cloud Console). Three steps:
  1. Delete the comments containing the leaked key (one-click `...` → Delete on each):
     - https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/issues/2157#issuecomment-4555473441
     - https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/issues/2159#issuecomment-4555811974
  2. Rotate the FCM service-account key at Google Cloud Console (only step that actually neutralizes the exposure — the journal copies on the VM, webhook archives, and any third-party GitHub mirror still hold the old key). After rotation, re-dispatch `set-mobile-push-secrets` with the new JSON in the FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret to update the on-disk file at ${DATA_DIR}/fcm_service_account.json.
  3. Optional: `sudo journalctl --rotate && sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=1s` on the live VM to wipe historical journal copies containing the key. Reduces forensic surface; the scrub already stops future bleeds at source.
items.trigger_condition: Operator-only — no autonomous action possible. Surface every /health-review run until resolved.
items.resolution_criteria: Both leaked issue comments deleted (404 on the comment URLs); FCM service-account key rotated at Google Cloud Console; ${DATA_DIR}/fcm_service_account.json updated to the new credential and a fresh push test succeeds (kicks the notifier and confirms no 404 NOT_FOUND).

items.title: Verify the ict-ib-gateway-watchdog RESTART path fires end-to-end on a real overnight IBKR-reset wedge
items.description: The auto-heal watchdog (the BL-20260527-003 fix, PR #2183) went live on the trader VM on 2026-05-28 (main 6972a9f, deployed as 4d4d0c3 via pull-and-deploy #2196). Its HEALTHY path is confirmed — the #2196 post-restart systemd dump shows `probe: healthy=True reason=net_liquidation=1000600.6 action=none` and the timer active (TriggeredBy). What is NOT yet observed in production is the RESTART path: that on a genuine wedge (a logged-out Gateway reports `connected=true` but `net_liquidation=None`) the watchdog actually runs `scripts/ops/restart_ib_gateway.sh` and brings `ib_paper`/MES back with no human in the loop. The natural test is IBKR's overnight server-reset window (~04:30 UTC), the same window that produced the 2026-05-28 wedge. The watchdog journal is now readable from the diag surface — `ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.{service,timer}` was added to diag.py `_CANONICAL_UNITS` in #2192, so `/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.service` works.

If MES instead stayed healthy through the reset (no wedge to heal), record that and keep watching — absence of a wedge is not yet proof the restart path works.
