items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay rejects multi-param diag paths (the & query separator)
items.description: Issue-driven diag requests whose title carries a & failed this session (#2251 `journal?table=order_packages&limit=40`, #2252 `journal?table=trades&limit=40`) while single-param paths (`journal?table=order_packages`, `db_info`) and the broad `snapshot?limit=200` succeeded. Suspected cause: GitHub stores the title's & as the HTML entity &; the workflow decodes it (${raw//&/&}) but the path-validation regex ^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.:%-]+$ in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml rejects the ; if any entity slips through un-decoded, so the run exits 1 with 'Rejected diag_path'. Workaround in use: single-param paths or the broad snapshot. Low priority — the relay works for the common cases.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run, or the next time a session needs a multi-param diag pull.
items.resolution_criteria: A multi-param diag request (e.g. journal?table=trades&limit=40) completes and posts JSON back, OR the workflow title decode/validation is fixed (fully decode & before the regex, or URL-decode) and verified with a multi-param pull.
items.resolution: VERIFIED FIXED EMPIRICALLY 2026-05-29: a fresh multi-param pull `journal?table=trades&limit=5` (issue #2315) returned JSON (5 rows) and auto-closed — the resolution criteria's first clause is met. vm-diag-snapshot.yml already carries the `${raw//&/&}` entity-decode (lines ~123) and the path-validation regex already allows `&` (`^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.:%-]+$`), so the multi-param path now decodes and validates correctly. The prior-session failures (#2251/#2252) were not reproduced; no code change required. NOTE: the EARLIER multi-param failures observed in THIS session's first half (#2293/#2294 etc.) were the ict-web-api deploy-bounce outage (~09:45-09:52Z), not the & decode — single-param paths failed in that same window too.

items.source: /health-review 2026-05-29 — a docs-only commit deploy bounced the live trader + web-api mid-review, and the (unnecessary) recover dispatches were all webhook-dropped.
items.title: git-sync deploy restarts the LIVE TRADER for docs-only commits (brief trading + read-surface interruption); web-api has no VM-side self-heal and the GitHub recover dispatch is webhook-flaky
items.description: OBSERVED this review: between status #2286 (09:44:05Z, uptime 36577s, git_sha b149b15) and status #2302 (09:52:15Z, uptime 405s, git_sha 22e2cf0) the live trader RESTARTED and HEAD advanced b149b15 -> 22e2cf0. The only commit in that range is 22e2cf0 (#2284, a DOCS-ONLY 'docs(health-review): recurring carry-forward item' change). So the ict-git-sync timer pulled the new commit and ran the full deploy_pull_restart path, which restarts ALL ict-* units (trader + web-api) regardless of whether the diff touches any runtime code. Two consequences: (1) the live money-path trader was bounced (~7 min, 09:45-09:52Z) for a pure documentation change — an unnecessary trading interruption; (2) during that window ict-web-api was down so the diag/dashboard READ surface was blinded (diag pulls #2293-#2296,#2298 failed 09:45:44-09:48:03Z). I misread (2) as a crash and fired three vm-web-api-recover dispatches (#2297/#2299/#2300) — ALL webhook-dropped (issue OPEN, updated_at==created_at, no run), same GitHub issues.opened batching as the resolved BL-20260527-001. They turned out UNNECESSARY (the deploy completed and both services self-recovered by 09:52Z). Net: no real outage, but two genuine gaps surfaced. PRIMARY GAP: deploy_pull_restart restarts the live trader for non-runtime (docs/comms) commits — consider gating the trader restart on whether the diff touches runtime paths (src/, config/, deploy/, requirements). SECONDARY GAP: ict-web-api has no VM-side self-heal and the only autonomous recover lever (GitHub-dispatched vm-web-api-recover) is webhook-flaky exactly when needed.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or whenever a deploy of a docs/comms-only commit is observed to bounce the live trader, or a vm-web-api-recover dispatch is webhook-dropped.
items.resolution_criteria: PRIMARY: deploy_pull_restart.sh (or the git-sync path) skips the ict-trader-live restart when the pulled diff touches no runtime path (docs/comms-only) — verify a docs-only commit deploys without a trader uptime reset. SECONDARY: ict-web-api gets a VM-side auto-restart-on-unhealthy guard (systemd watchdog/timer probing local :8001 /api/health) so the read surface self-heals without a webhook-dependent dispatch. Both are Tier-2 deploy/runtime changes; not editable from /health-review — surface to the operator.

items.resolution_note: FIXED + DEPLOYED — the item was stale-open. PR #2595 (commit 4a8594d, 2026-06-01 21:21Z, a later same-day /health-review session) added the runtime-path gate to scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh (lines ~142-181): it diffs PRE_SYNC_HEAD..POST_SYNC_HEAD and, when every changed path matches the safe set ^(docs/|tests/|\.claude/|[^/]+\.md$), SKIPS dependency-install + unit-refresh + service restart (exit 0) — so a docs/backlog/sprint-log commit no longer bounces the live trader. Fail-safe: empty/uncomputable diff OR any other path (src/ ml/ config/ deploy/ scripts/ comms/ requirements*/pyproject) falls through to the normal restart; DEPLOY_FORCE_RESTART=1 overrides. Confirmed in deployed HEAD e97991f (git merge-base --is-ancestor 4a8594d e97991f = true). The 2026-06-01 'reproduced 3rd time' triage note (16:57Z) predates the 21:21Z fix. SECONDARY gap (web-api has no VM-side self-heal; the GitHub vm-web-api-recover dispatch is webhook-flaky) is NOT addressed by #2595 — re-logging it as BL-20260604-003 so it isn't lost.

items.title: INVESTIGATE: M13 template-analyst vwap strategy insight self-contradicts — summary_md says 'Trades 89/0 closed, WR n/a (0W/0L)' while the same row's row_counts says trades_closed=10, wins=1, losses=9
items.description: insights_history row id=1469 (endpoint=strategy, strategy_name=vwap, model_id=template:v1, generated_at 2026-05-29T20:35:17Z): summary_md renders 'Trades (total / closed): 89 / 0 ... Win rate: n/a (0W / 0L)', but the SAME row's row_counts_json is {trades:89, trades_closed:10, wins:1, losses:9, order_packages:20} and net PnL is rendered -$2.98 (which is non-zero, implying closed trades exist). So the markdown 'closed=0 / 0W-0L' disagrees with the structured 'closed=10 / 1W-9L / -$2.98'. The goal is NOT just to confirm the discrepancy but to ROOT-CAUSE it in the template analyst (src/runtime/insights/template_analyst.py + generator.py): likely two different closed-trade definitions feeding the same card — e.g. the prose 'closed' counts rows with a terminal close timestamp while row_counts 'trades_closed' counts a different status, OR a shadow-vs-live filter applied to one path but not the other (vwap is execution:shadow, 89 trades / mostly unfilled), OR a window/symbol-join mismatch. Whichever it is, the two numbers should be reconciled so the operator-facing prose matches the structured counts. Cosmetic-but-misleading: a reader sees 'vwap: 0 closed, WR n/a' in the narrative while the data says 1W/9L -$2.98.

items.resolution_note: Root-caused + FIXED. recent_data() (src/runtime/insights/data_sources.py) filters WHERE t.status='closed' but does NOT select the status column, so recent_template's `[t for t in rows if t.get('status')=='closed']` matched NOTHING (key absent) and zeroed the header to 'Net $0.00 — 0W/0L' over a table of real closed trades. Extended test_template_recent_endpoint_table_rendering to assert header==table (1W/0L/$7.00). Pure code fix (Tier-1); live on the M13 card after the next deploy restarts ict-insights-generator.

items.title: High order_package ORPHAN rates across strategies — positions go DB-open / exchange-flat without a clean fill record
items.description: While auditing whether strategies exit properly, found high orphan rates in order_packages: trend_donchian 22/38 (58%), vwap 917/1460 (63%), squeeze 24/83 (29%), ict_scalp 4/13 (31%). 'Orphaned' = the reconciler found the DB-open package flat on the exchange but could not record a clean fill/PnL (vs reconciler_filled where it could). This loses PnL attribution and inflates the 'rejected'/'orphaned' noise in the journal, which can skew per-strategy performance stats and therefore the research/demotion evidence. Likely contributors: (a) the re-entry storm (fixed separately by the bar-close debounce) creating packages that never stabilise into real positions; (b) entry orders that fill-then-immediately-exchange-SL vs orders that never fill (the 341 exchange_rejected + intent_noop rejections suggest a mix); (c) the reconciler/orphan-handler not querying Bybit get_closed_pnl to attribute the realised PnL on a derivatives SL/TP fire (see order_monitor._classify_orphan_close — derivatives orphans are left 'unknown'). NOTE the exit machinery itself works (fade + ict_scalp win normally through reconciler_filled; the Chandelier trail ratchets) — this is a reconciliation/attribution + order-stabilisation issue, not a broken-exit issue.

Live re-measure via /api/diag/journal (issue #7657, git_sha 08154e3a): the two most-recent orphaned order_packages — pkg-07d51e1d986447b3 + pkg-da56584ddd114439 (both ict_scalp_avax_5m, bybit_1 demo) — carry status='orphaned' + meta.orphaned_reason='BUG-049 — no linked_trade_id after 5 min; package was never executed', YET each HAS a real trade back-referencing it via trades.order_package_id: pkg-07d51e1d986447b3 ← trade #4022 (setup_type=intent_reduce, status=closed), pkg-da56584ddd114439 ← trade #4021 (status=OPEN, a live position). So these packages DID execute; they were falsely stamped 'orphaned — never executed'. ROOT CAUSE: order_packages.linked_trade_id is a ONE-SLOT 'primary entry trade' pointer (database._migrate_add_order_package_id docstring) — when a decision fans out into several trade rows (real entry + demo mirror + intent_reduce leg + multi-account), only the LAST update_order_package(linked_trade_id=...) survives, so the slot is often left NULL even though the package filled. order_monitor._sweep_unlinked_packages keys the BUG-049 orphan stamp SOLELY on linked_trade_id IS NULL and only consults the newer trades.order_package_id back-reference for REJECTION rows (stage 1) and shadow strategies (stage 1.5) — there was NO stage recognizing a package whose linked trade actually EXECUTED (open/closed). This both (a) pollutes per-strategy orphan-rate stats with executed packages (the resolution_criteria) and (b) when the linked trade is still OPEN, wrongly terminalises a package whose position is LIVE, clearing the strategy-monocle open gate on a live position. FIX (order_monitor.py::_sweep_unlinked_packages, new stage 0 run BEFORE the rejection relabel): reconcile any status='open'+linked_trade_id-NULL+>=5min package that has a non-backtest trade with status IN ('open','closed') back-referencing it via trades.order_package_id — back-fill linked_trade_id from that trade (prefer an open leg, else newest closed) and set the package status to match (open→'open', else 'closed') instead of orphaning. Precedence executed>rejected>shadow>orphaned. Pure link/label reconciliation — NO order placed/modified; self-healing (repairs already-affected rows next monitor tick). Tests: tests/test_reconciler_reduce_and_shadow.py::test_sweep_unlinked_packages_reconciles_executed_trade (executed-closed + executed-open reconcile, genuine-orphan still orphans); full reconciler/monocle/order-packages-log/prop-shadow suites green locally (141 tests; pandas-dependent monocle-gate import skipped in-sandbox, runs in CI). Branch claude/orphan-rate-investigation-ags4xs. Does NOT close this item — the closed-pnl-attribution / executed-then-exchange-flat class (BL-20260622-CLOSEDPNL-AGGREGATE-SOAK) remains its own soak-verify item; this fix addresses the false-orphan pollution half.

FALSE-ORPHAN / split-attribution class RESOLVED + LIVE-VERIFIED. Shipped in two operator-approved PRs: #7658 (prevent — stage-0 reconcile at status='open') then #7665 (heal — widened to status IN ('open','orphaned') so it also repairs the already-orphaned backlog; the #7658 self-healing claim was wrong, caught by live post-deploy check and corrected). Deployed to the live trader (git_sha 6eaeae5a, ict-trader-live restarted 13:09Z). LIVE PROOF (issue #7670, first healing sweep 13:11:43Z): orphaned order_packages 1744 -> 1687 (the 57 executed-but-unlinked false-orphans healed in one sweep; the correlated UPDATE has no LIMIT so a single tick heals all matching). Both known targets healed: pkg-07d51e1d986447b3 orphaned->CLOSED linked_trade_id=4022 (its intent_reduce leg); pkg-da56584ddd114439 orphaned->OPEN linked_trade_id=4021 (live position restored, monocle gate un-cleared). Heal spans strategies/venues, not just the AVAX targets: sampled reconciled rows incl. trend_donchian_ada_4h (bybit_1, ->closed, tid 3142) + mgc_pullback_1d (IB ib_paper, ->open, tid 3341), each carrying meta.executed_reconciled_reason. The residual 1687 orphaned are GENUINE never-executed orphans (correctly untouched — the EXISTS filter fails for them), dominated by historical killed-vwap SHADOW leftovers from May 2026 (the sampled oldest is a 2026-05-02 vwap pkg; vwap was M7-killed, ~917/1460 orphan rate in the original audit) plus dead-end-routed/refused packages — those are historical noise, not the split-attribution bug, and the go-forward flow is covered by the shadow_expired relabel (PR #4339/#4342) + the emit-then-orphan post-dispatch backstop (2026-06-25). NET: the specific false-orphan driver that was actively mis-attributing EXECUTED trades (incl. wrongly orphaning LIVE positions + clearing their monocle gate) is fixed, self-healing every tick, and verified on live data. REMAINING OPEN scope on THIS item is now ONLY the closed-pnl-attribution / executed-then-exchange-flat class tracked as the soak BL-20260622-CLOSEDPNL-AGGREGATE-SOAK (which this session separately re-verified clean on bybit_2 — see that item's 2026-07-26 update).

items.source: While pulling live orphan data for BL-20260601-001 via the vm-diag-snapshot relay, EVERY /api/bot/* and db/table/* path returned {"error":"fetch_failed"} while /api/diag/* paths in the SAME batched SSH run succeeded.
items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay returns fetch_failed for ALL /api/bot/* + db/table/* paths while /api/diag/* works (blocks review pulls of decision-level + filtered-count endpoints)
items.description: Isolated across 3 relay runs: issue #7654 (batch of /api/bot + db/table, all fetch_failed), issue #7656 (version → OK with git_sha 08154e3a; stats + all /api/bot/db/table → fetch_failed in the same run), issue #7657 (/api/diag db_info + status + services + journal all OK). The web-api is UP and serving (db_info: error_per_table {}, order_packages=3290, trades=4022 rows; recovery-log journal shows the dashboard getting /api/bot/stats 200s), and the DB is healthy — so this is NOT a web-api/DB outage. It is a relay-side handling issue specific to the /api/bot/ upstream_prefix in the batched issues path (.github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml resolve_one/curl loop), OR the /api/bot GETs 5xx specifically to the localhost curl (note the relay sends 'Authorization: Bearer DIAG_READ_TOKEN' to /api/bot Tier-1 GETs, which are unauthenticated — a stray bearer + curl --fail could interact; and /api/bot/stats returns HTTP 503 on structural DB failure per S-067, but db_info shows the DB is fine, so that path is not it). Impact: future health/system reviews cannot pull the /api/bot decision-level view (/order-packages) OR the filtered-count endpoints (/db/table/<t>?filter_col=status&...&limit=1 → total) through the relay — the cleanest way to MEASURE the orphan rate (per resolution_criteria of BL-20260601-001). This session worked around it with /api/diag/journal + db_info. NOTE (honesty): on the first all-fetch_failed batch (#7654, before /api/diag/version was tested) this session fired a vm-web-api-recover (#7655) diagnosing a web-api outage; the recovery log showed the service was already active and serving — the restart was a harmless ~2s no-op (health 200 after), and the true cause is this relay/endpoint /api/bot handling, not a down service.
items.trigger_condition: Next session touching .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml or any review that needs /api/bot/* or db/table/* data via the relay. Repro: open a vm-diag-request issue with any /api/bot path (e.g. 'stats' or 'db/table/order_packages?limit=1') and observe fetch_failed while a sibling /api/diag path (e.g. 'version') returns 200.
items.resolution_criteria: The relay returns real JSON for allowlisted /api/bot/* + db/table/* GETs (verify 'stats' and 'db/table/order_packages?filter_col=status&filter_op=eq&filter_val=orphaned&limit=1' both return a body, not fetch_failed). Root-cause whether it is the curl --fail/Bearer handling for the /api/bot prefix in the batched loop, or a genuine localhost 5xx on those endpoints.
items.resolution_note: NOT A BUG — misdiagnosis, corrected honestly. The relay's default upstream_prefix is /api/diag/ and a /api/bot route MUST be namespaced as 'api/bot/<path>' by the caller (resolve_one in vm-diag-snapshot.yml only rewrites the prefix to /api/bot/ when the path starts with 'api/bot/'). I passed the bare basenames ('stats', 'db/table/...', 'order-packages', 'notifications') without the 'api/bot/' prefix, so the relay resolved them under /api/diag/ → 404 → the curl --fail fallback wrote {"error":"fetch_failed"}. Proven via issue #7659: the ict-web-api journal shows 'GET /api/diag/stats 404', 'GET /api/diag/notifications 404', 'GET /api/diag/db/table/... 404' at 12:03:55Z — the relay had prefixed them /api/diag/. Re-fired with the correct 'api/bot/' prefix (issue #7660) and the same endpoints return real JSON. The /api/diag/* paths I passed bare (version/db_info/status/journal) worked because they ARE diag paths. Lesson for future sessions: diag paths are bare (e.g. 'snapshot?limit=200'); /api/bot paths MUST be prefixed 'api/bot/' (e.g. 'api/bot/db/table/order_packages?filter_col=status&filter_op=eq&filter_val=orphaned&limit=1'). No workflow change needed; the calling convention is by design (diag is the default surface, /api/bot is explicitly namespaced). Also for the record: the vm-web-api-recover (#7655) fired on the first all-fetch_failed batch was an unnecessary (harmless) no-op driven by the same misread — the service was up the whole time.
items.notes: Optional low-value follow-up for a future session: add a one-line 'api/bot/ paths must be prefixed; diag paths are bare' reminder to docs/claude/diag-relay.md so the next PM-side session doesn't repeat this. Not blocking.

items.source: Noticed while investigating the MES (mes_trend_long_1d) IBKR-paper pipeline (PR #2626): order_packages + signal-audit pulls show htf_pullback_trend_2h producing MES order packages even though its config declares symbols:[BTCUSDT] and it routes only to bybit_1.
items.title: Per-strategy `symbols:` does not gate EVALUATION — the multi-symbol tick loop runs every enabled builder on the union of all account symbols, producing cross-product packages no account routes (ORPHANED)
items.description: The tick loop (src/main.py::_resolve_tick_symbols) unions every configured account's symbols ({BTCUSDT, MES}) and evaluates each enabled strategy's signal builder on every symbol in the union, regardless of the strategy's own `symbols:` field in config/strategies.yaml. Observed 2026-06-02: htf_pullback_trend_2h (symbols:[BTCUSDT], routed to bybit_1 only) emitted MES order packages (status 'orphaned'); conversely mes_trend_long_1d (symbols:[MES]) is evaluated on BTCUSDT (the signal audit shows symbol=BTCUSDT eval rows for it, reason 'short_suppressed_long_only'). These cross-product packages are dropped/orphaned because no account routes that (strategy x symbol) combo — the symbol->exchange dispatch gate (coordinator._eligible_for_dispatch) + the account.strategies filter correctly prevent execution, so this is HARMLESS to trading (no wrong-symbol order can fire). But it is wasted per-tick evaluation + journal noise: the orphaned cross-product rows pollute per-strategy orphan-rate stats (cf. BL-20260601-001, whose triage_note already saw these htf_pullback_trend_2h-on-MES orphans). Fix: gate EVALUATION by the strategy's own declared `symbols:` (intersected with its routed accounts' symbols) so a BTCUSDT-only strategy is never run on MES and vice-versa.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review or any session touching src/main.py::_resolve_tick_symbols or the per-tick strategy-evaluation loop. Re-pull order_packages and confirm orphaned cross-product packages (htf_pullback_trend_2h on MES, mes_trend_long_1d on BTCUSDT) still appear.
items.resolution_criteria: Strategy signal builders are evaluated only on the symbols the strategy declares in config/strategies.yaml (intersected with account routing), so no cross-product (strategy x non-declared-symbol) order packages are produced. Verify htf_pullback_trend_2h no longer emits MES packages and mes_trend_long_1d no longer emits BTCUSDT packages, with no loss of legitimate signals.
items.resolution_note: Fixed by the per-strategy symbol-scope gate (PR #2643, merged + deployed 2026-06-02, HEAD 3d35e24). intent_multiplexer._collect_intents now skips a strategy whose declared config/strategies.yaml symbols: do not include the current tick symbol (permissive on no-symbols/unknown/config-error), so a strategy is evaluated/emits ONLY on its declared instrument(s) — no cross-product (strategy x non-declared-symbol) packages are produced. Gated at intent EMISSION (not dispatch) so a higher-priority off-symbol strategy can't win a symbol's per-symbol aggregation and starve the legitimate owner. Verified live post-deploy via audit_query: mgc_pullback_1d evaluates MGC-only (zero MES/MHG/BTCUSDT rows) where pre-deploy it ran on all four. Crypto strategies (symbols:[BTCUSDT]) no longer evaluate on MES. Tests: tests/test_intent_symbol_scope.py (4) + 324 intent/coordinator/pipeline regression green. NOTE: the gate lives in the production intent-multiplexer path (STRATEGY=multiplexed_intents); the legacy first-wins pipeline path is not gated but is not the production path.

items.title: Add an alert for 'mes_trend_long_1d_eval rows stop appearing' (catches MES going actually dark, vs side=none being normal)
items.description: MES currently produces a per-tick mes_trend_long_1d_eval row with side=none and reason='no breakout on the latest bar' — that's the strategy doing its job (Donchian-30 long-only on the daily, waiting for a breakout above the prior-30d high; today 7607 vs prior-high 7632.75). Composes with the existing liveness watchdog (process-level) — this is strategy-level coverage. items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay hardcodes /api/diag/ — perf-review's /api/bot/{performance,trades/closed,insights/*} pulls are unreachable from a Trusted-network (relay-only) session
items.description: .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml strips a leading /api/diag/ (line ~134) and curls a hardcoded 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/diag/<path>' (line ~185), so the relay can ONLY hit /api/diag/* endpoints. The performance-review SKILL.md § 'Fetching trade data' documents pulling /api/bot/trades/closed?since=&limit=500, /api/bot/order-packages?since=, /api/bot/performance?window=, and /api/bot/insights/{summary,recent,strategy,health} — NONE of which the relay can reach. A relay-only (default Trusted-network) review session therefore cannot get the clean windowed aggregates (/api/bot/performance) or the closed-trade list (/api/bot/trades/closed); it must fall back to /api/diag/journal?table=trades (reject-dominated, 55KB-truncated ~46 rows) + /api/diag/journal?table=insights_history (the M13 'recent' card, which DOES surface the last-20 closed trades — the practical workaround this review used). Net: per-strategy realized-PnL aggregation is hampered relay-only. Fix options: (a) extend vm-diag-snapshot.yml to allow an /api/bot/ prefix passthrough for the read-only GET aggregate endpoints (performance, trades/closed, order-packages); or (b) add /api/diag/performance + /api/diag/trades_closed mirrors; or (c) document insights_history as the canonical relay-only closed-trade source in the perf-review skill. Mirrors the BL-20260529-004 insights-relay-reach fix (which added insights_history/insights_usage to _JOURNAL_TABLES).
items.trigger_condition: Any /performance-review or /health-review run from a relay-only session that needs /api/bot/ aggregate data; or next time someone extends the diag relay.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the vm-diag relay can return /api/bot/performance + /api/bot/trades/closed (passthrough or /api/diag mirror), verified by a relay pull; OR the perf-review SKILL.md is updated to use the relay-reachable substitutes (journal?table=trades + insights_history) as the canonical relay-only path so a future session doesn't assume the /api/bot/ pulls work.
items.resolution_note: FIXED — extended .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml so the relay can reach an ALLOWLISTED set of read-only /api/bot/* Tier-1 GET endpoints (performance, trades/closed, order-packages, insights/*, health/*, shadow/*, etc.) in addition to /api/diag/*. Default upstream stays /api/diag/; an api/bot/* path is routed to /api/bot/ only if its base (query stripped) is in the explicit allowlist, else rejected. curl URL switched to ${diag_upstream_prefix}${diag_path_safe}. Verified the routing logic + YAML parse locally (diag unchanged; allowlisted bot paths route correctly; non-allowlisted bot paths reject). A future /performance-review can now pull /api/bot/performance + /api/bot/trades/closed cleanly relay-only. Pending merge.

items.title: ict-web-api has no VM-side self-heal; the only autonomous recover lever (GitHub vm-web-api-recover) is webhook-flaky exactly when needed
items.description: BL-20260529-002's PRIMARY gap (docs-commit trader bounce) was fixed by PR #2595. Its SECONDARY gap remains: ict-web-api.service has no on-VM auto-restart-on-unhealthy guard, and the only autonomous recovery path (the GitHub-dispatched vm-web-api-recover workflow) is subject to the issues.opened webhook batch-drop (BL-20260527-001) precisely during a deploy bounce when the read surface is down — observed 2026-05-29 (#2297/#2299/#2300 all dropped) and the #2373 recover that ran mid-bounce failed. With the PRIMARY gap closed the read-surface blind windows are now rarer (docs commits no longer bounce anything), but a genuine web-api crash still has no VM-side self-heal. Fix: add a systemd watchdog/timer (mirror ict-liveness-watchdog / ict-ib-gateway-watchdog) that probes local 127.0.0.1:8001/api/health every ~2 min and restarts ict-web-api.service on N consecutive failures, with restart-cap + cooldown so a genuine crashloop alert-escalates rather than loops. Removes the webhook dependency for read-surface recovery.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or next time a vm-web-api-recover dispatch is webhook-dropped or ict-web-api is observed down with no autonomous recovery.
items.resolution_criteria: ict-web-api gets a VM-side auto-restart-on-unhealthy guard (systemd timer probing local /api/health) that self-heals the read surface without a webhook-dependent GitHub dispatch; verified by inducing/observing one web-api outage that the watchdog recovers autonomously. Tier-2 deploy/runtime change — operator-approved PR.

check_log.note: FIX BUILT (pending merge+deploy+verify). scripts/check_web_api.py — stdlib-only watchdog probing http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health every 2 min (ict-web-api-watchdog.{service,timer}); after 2 consecutive failures runs scripts/ops/restart_web_api.sh, guard-railed --max-restarts 3 + --cooldown-min 10 (crashloop -> alert-escalate, not loop). Decision state machine is byte-identical to the proven check_ib_gateway.py::decide. --auto-restart enabled in the unit (read-only API = low blast radius). Registered in test_s012 EXPECTED_SERVICES + deployment-ops.md; timer auto-enabled by install_systemd_units.sh. Tests: tests/test_check_web_api.py (9). POST-DEPLOY VERIFY: confirm the timer is active + a healthy probe in journalctl (healthy path); the restart path proves out on a real/induced wedge. Closes the gap where the only web-api recovery lever (GitHub vm-web-api-recover) is webhook-flaky.

NEW EVIDENCE of the gap this item targets: this session, /api/bot/order-packages + /api/bot/config returned HTTP 500 transiently around the ~06:19/07:16 trader restarts (the heavier bot routes erroring while /api/diag/*, the Streamlit routine-poll set, and the insights cache stayed 200). They SELF-RECOVERED (config 200 + 8 Streamlit routes 200 OK by 08:06-08:20, same web-api PID 386690 = no restart) — so no recovery lever was needed THIS time, but it confirms the heavier endpoints wobble around restarts and the only autonomous recover (vm-web-api-recover) is still webhook-flaky. The scripts/check_web_api.py VM-side watchdog this item proposes is still pending merge+deploy. Status unchanged (open).

updates.note: RESOLVED (already built, 2026-06-04+) — the ict-web-api-watchdog.{service,timer} exists and the timer was ACTIVE in the 06-25 snapshot: every 2 min it runs scripts/check_web_api.py --auto-restart --restart-after 2 --max-restarts 3 --cooldown-min 10, which probes :8001/api/health and runs scripts/ops/restart_web_api.sh (systemctl restart + health probe) on sustained failure — a VM-side autonomous self-heal independent of the GitHub vm-web-api-recover webhook lever. The item's premise ('no VM-side self-heal') is obsolete.

items.title: check_accounts_api fails in the standalone health-snapshot writer context (account_balance() returns None without the trader's live exchange clients) — card shows a perpetual accounts_api 'watch'
items.description: src/runtime/health.py::check_accounts_api reuses src.bot.data_loaders.account_balance() per account and WARNs on any None. In the trader PROCESS this works (it holds the live exchange/IB clients). But ict-health-snapshot.service runs write_health_snapshot.py as a SEPARATE oneshot that has no such clients (e.g. the local smoke logged 'account_balance(ib_paper): ib_insync is not installed' and Bybit balance needs a live socket), so account_balance() returns None -> accounts_api WARN -> the M13 health card sits at 6/7 'watch' with accounts_api failing even though the live trader's accounts are fine. This is a CONTEXT artifact of running the check outside the trader, not a real outage (verified: the trader dispatched real trade 2428 + is healthy). Net effect: the card never shows fully-green when it should. Fix options: (a) point check_accounts_api at the CONNECTION-FREE balance snapshot (runtime_logs/balance_snapshots.json — the same source /api/bot/accounts/balances uses, 'never opens an exchange socket'), so it reflects the last recorded balance instead of trying to connect; or (b) have the standalone writer skip/soften the accounts_api check (env flag) when not in-process; or (c) accept the warn as a known standalone limitation and document it. (a) is the cleanest — it makes the check connection-free + context-independent. Tier-1 code (observability); not a money-path change.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or whenever the dashboard health card shows accounts_api failing while the live trader is confirmed healthy.
items.resolution_criteria: check_accounts_api reports ok in the standalone ict-health-snapshot writer context when the trader's accounts are healthy (e.g. by reading the connection-free balance snapshot), so the M13 health card grades `good`/ok on a healthy system instead of a perpetual accounts_api `watch`. Verify via insights_history (endpoint=health) after the fix deploys.

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid — check_accounts_api fails in the standalone health-snapshot writer context (no live exchange clients). The cron health snapshot this review reported accounts_api ok (runs in-process), so not currently blinding. Blocker: Tier-1 code.

Not independently re-checked this window (would need to inspect the standalone health-snapshot writer's accounts_api behavior specifically); the live trader's own accounts_api check reads 'ok' (7/7) via health/latest this window, consistent with prior 'watch only in the standalone writer context' framing.
Re-validated 07-26: still soaking / awaiting more live data; no regression in this window's pull. Carried.

RESOLVED — src/runtime/health.py::check_accounts_api now reads the connection-free balance_snapshots DB (get_db().get_latest_balance_snapshots(), the same DB-authoritative source /api/bot/accounts/balances uses) instead of a live account_balance() probe. In the standalone health-snapshot writer there are no live broker clients, so the live probe returned None for every account and pinned this check at a permanent WARN; the per-tick account_reachability_alert latch already owns real-time down detection. Now: a snapshot with api_ok (or a balance) = healthy; api_ok=false + no balance = real down; no snapshot yet = 'no data' (not an outage). Updated tests/test_health.py (8 accounts-api tests, incl. a new no-snapshot-is-not-an-outage case) — all pass.

items.source: /health-review 2026-06-06: /api/diag/journalctl relay calls for ict-trader-live.service (lines=90) AND ict-liveness-watchdog.service (lines=70) both failed (run failed / curl --fail/--max-time), while journalctl?unit=ict-web-api.service (lines=120), status, config, journal, and log_file all succeeded.
items.title: Observability gap: /api/diag/journalctl fails for high-volume units (ict-trader-live) under the relay's curl --max-time, blocking restart-cause root-cause exactly when needed
items.description: When investigating the 2026-06-06 trader restart churn (BL-20260605-001), the diag journalctl pulls for ict-trader-live.service and ict-liveness-watchdog.service both returned 'run failed' via the vm-diag relay, while the lighter ict-web-api.service journalctl (and status/config/journal/log_file) succeeded. The trader logs a large volume per tick, so a journalctl tail of 70-120 lines likely exceeds the relay's `curl -sS --fail --max-time 40` budget (slow/large response -> curl exit 28/timeout -> workflow reports failure), OR the response byte size trips the same ~414KB cap noted elsewhere. Net effect: the single most useful pull for diagnosing a restart loop (the trader + watchdog journals) is the one that fails, so the autoheal-vs-crash-vs-IB-wedge trigger could not be captured this session. Candidate fixes (Tier-1/2): (a) raise the journalctl curl --max-time in vm-diag-snapshot.yml for journalctl paths; (b) add `since=`/`until=` narrowing support guidance so callers pull a small time-window instead of N lines; (c) add a dedicated lightweight 'restart-cause' diag (e.g. systemctl show --property=NRestarts,ActiveEnterTimestamp + the last N ExecStart lines) that returns small output; (d) gzip/cap journalctl output server-side. Until fixed, restart-cause investigation must use systemctl show timestamps + smaller line counts.

items.source: Session 2026-06-07: built the cancel-queued-runs workflow (#2935/#2938) to clear 23 stale 'queued' Actions runs dated 2026-05-15. The runner (with actions:write) found all 23 but cancelled 0 — both `gh run cancel` and the force-cancel endpoint return HTTP 500 for every one.
items.title: 23 zombie 'queued' Actions runs (2026-05-15) are un-cancellable — GitHub returns HTTP 500 on both cancel and force-cancel
items.description: 23 workflow runs have been stuck in 'queued' since 2026-05-15 (ids 25906694928..25907269254). They never got a runner and consume no compute, but clutter the Actions list. The cancel-queued-runs workflow added this session (runner-path, since the PM-side MCP token lacks actions:write) lists them correctly and attempts normal cancel then force-cancel (POST repos/.../actions/runs/{id}/force-cancel) — both return `HTTP 500` for all 23, so the workflow cancels 0. A 500 (not 403/422) means it is a GitHub server-side failure on these specific orphaned runs; nothing a runner or the Actions UI (same endpoints) can do. The cancel-queued-runs workflow itself is sound and reusable for any FUTURE cancellable queued backlog — these particular runs are the exception. Resolution is GitHub-side: GitHub may garbage-collect them eventually, or GitHub Support can purge zombie runs. No code change in this repo will clear them. Note runs can't be DELETED either (the delete-run endpoint only accepts completed runs, not queued). Tracked here only so a future health-review doesn't re-investigate the same inert clutter.
items.trigger_condition: A future health-review or session notices the 23 stale queued runs and considers re-attempting cancellation, or wonders whether cancel-queued-runs is broken.
items.resolution_criteria: The 23 stale 2026-05-15 queued runs no longer appear in the Actions list (GitHub-side GC or Support purge). No repo change is expected to satisfy this; close when the runs are gone or the operator decides to leave them.

updates.note: Confirmed STILL PRESENT 2026-07-11 via actions_list(status=queued): exactly 23 runs, ALL dated 2026-05-15 (Health Snapshot / vm-web-api-recover / vwap-backtest / vm-cloud-fix etc.), stuck ~2 months. Not autonomously closable: the available GitHub MCP toolset exposes no workflow-run cancel/delete method, and GitHub historically 500s on cancelling these. BENIGN — they are queued (never scheduled), so they consume ZERO Actions minutes and don't block the runner. Downgrading urgency: leave open as a known cosmetic nuisance; a real fix needs `gh run delete`/API DELETE from a non-MCP context (desktop CLI or a one-shot workflow), not worth prioritising.

Attempted a real clear via the runner-path cancel-queued-runs workflow (#6131) — which has actions:write AND a force-cancel fallback (repos/.../actions/runs/<id>/force-cancel), i.e. more power than the MCP token. Result: cancelled 0 of 23 — BOTH `gh run cancel` and the force-cancel endpoint failed on every one of the 23 stuck 2026-05-15 runs. So these are genuinely un-cancellable at GitHub's side (a terminal stuck-queued state GitHub's own API refuses to clear), not just an MCP-permission limitation. Confirmed benign (queued → 0 minutes) and NOT fixable from here — stop retrying the canceller. Only a GitHub-support action or natural GC would clear them; not worth pursuing. Downgraded/parked.
Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid — 23 zombie 'queued' Actions runs (2026-05-15) un-cancellable (GitHub 500). Cosmetic/GitHub-side. Blocker: GitHub support / wait-out.
Zombie queued Actions runs from 2026-05-15 not re-checked this window; low priority, cosmetic.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

items.source: backfill-monitor-closed-pnl run #2990 (issue 2990) recovered 0/16 rows.
items.title: backfill-monitor-closed-pnl (and likely sibling backfill/inspect closed-pnl actions) can't reach Bybit creds in the system-action subprocess
items.description: The backfill-monitor-closed-pnl system-action skipped 100% of candidates (16/16, incl. demo bybit_1 rows #2482/#2484/#2490/#2492/#2494 and live rows) with 'account_closed_pnl_for_trade returned None'. The script's own heuristic warns the cause is 'exchange CREDENTIALS NOT REACHABLE from this process's env — silent auth failure'. _lib.sh::load_runtime_secrets sources REPO_DIR/.env; the live ict-trader-live.service reaches Bybit fine (actively trading), so the gap is specific to the system-action subprocess env (likely .env at REPO_DIR missing/incomplete vs the trader's systemd EnvironmentFile, and/or bybit_1 demo creds not present). This blocks any closed-pnl backfill/inspect action regardless of the BL-20260601-001 fix. Pre-existing; surfaced while remediating BL-20260601-001.
items.trigger_condition: Next time a closed-pnl backfill/inspect action is needed, or proactively to unblock BL-20260601-001 demo-row remediation.
items.resolution_criteria: backfill-monitor-closed-pnl (and inspect-closed-pnl) reach Bybit with valid creds from the system-action subprocess and recover/inspect at least the demo rows; root-cause the env mismatch between the wrapper's load_runtime_secrets and the trader's systemd env.
items.triage_note: 2026-06-08: opened from BL-20260601-001 deploy session. Needs VM diagnosis of REPO_DIR/.env contents + how ict-trader-live/ict-web-api load creds (systemd EnvironmentFile vs .env) + whether bybit_1 demo keys are configured.
items.resolution_note: MISDIAGNOSIS — NOT a credential gap. inspect-closed-pnl (Tier-1, read-only) on demo rows #2482 and #2490 (issues #2992, #2994) proved: bybit_client_for(cfg) built the demo client (demo=True → api-demo.bybit.com), get_closed_pnl executed WITHOUT error, and Bybit returned 0 records for each (within the 7-day window). So bybit_1 demo keys ARE configured and reachable from the system-action subprocess (load_runtime_secrets sources the same /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env that ict-trader-live uses). True cause of the backfill 0/16: Bybit DEMO doesn't populate /v5/position/closed-pnl. The 'credentials not reachable' WARNING is a misleading 100%-skip heuristic. Follow-up tracked in BL-20260608-DEMOPNL.

items.source: BL-20260608-CRED diagnosis: Bybit demo /v5/position/closed-pnl returns 0 records (verified #2482/#2490).
items.title: Bybit DEMO realised PnL is unrecoverable from closed-pnl; build a demo-PnL source + fix the misleading backfill warning
items.description: bybit_1 (demo) closed trades carry pnl=NULL because Bybit demo trading does not populate /v5/position/closed-pnl — verified via inspect-closed-pnl on #2482 and #2490 (0 records, creds OK). (1) backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py prints 'credentials not reachable' on any 100%-skip — soften to distinguish client-None/auth-exception from a successful empty response. (2) OPERATOR REQUESTED building a real demo-PnL source: recon shipped (inspect-closed-pnl now also dumps /v5/execution/list + /v5/order/history) to determine which endpoint the demo venue populates; then implement a demo fallback in account_closed_pnl_for_trade (reconstruct exit avg-price + realised PnL from closing executions) + backfill. If demo populates NEITHER endpoint, fall back to computing PnL from entry/exit fills captured at close time.
items.trigger_condition: In progress (operator-requested 2026-06-08). Next: run the enhanced inspect-closed-pnl on a demo trade post-deploy to see execution-list/order-history output.
items.resolution_criteria: Demo closed trades carry non-NULL realised pnl from a working source; AND the backfill warning distinguishes empty-result from auth-failure.
items.triage_note: 2026-06-08: opened from BL-20260608-CRED diagnosis; recon tooling shipped same session. | 2026-06-08 RECON + DEFERRED: enhanced inspect-closed-pnl run on demo #2490 (issue #2997) — /v5/position/closed-pnl=0 rows, BUT /v5/execution/list=6 rows and /v5/order/history=3 rows ARE populated on demo. Key finding: the demo account NETS every strategy fill into a single position (each htf 'trade' is an incremental Sell with closedSize=0; the whole ~0.505 short was flattened by ONE Buy @63483.4), so there is NO per-trade close to attribute — a real demo-PnL source needs a position-accounting/allocation layer (FIFO/avg across constituent opens), not just a different endpoint. Sub-findings: demo opens carry no SL/TP (reduceOnly=False, empty stopOrderType) so positions accumulate vs live bybit_2 which closes per-trade; and the reconciler marked these closed while the net position was still open. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-06-08: DEFER — added to ROADMAP.md 'Items Under Consideration'. Recon tooling (inspect-closed-pnl execution/order dump) is shipped (PR #2996). The backfill false-'creds' warning softening (sub-item 1) also remains open. | 2026-06-08 SL/TP ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATED (operator-requested): root cause confirmed = one-way-mode position-level SL/TP OVERWRITE on same-direction re-entry + reconciler closing on NET-flat (not per-trade) + monocle release → accumulation cycle. SL/TP ARE attached on demo entries (execute.py:659-660) — CORRECTION to the earlier 'demo opens carry no SL/TP' note, which was an over-read (attached position-level SL/TP don't show as separate stop ORDERS in order/history). Evidence: audit_query #3002 (33 sell+28 short htf signals in 9h, only 3 bar_debounce_blocked), inspect #2997 (incremental Sell opens → one Buy 0.505 close), code (no positionIdx/hedge anywhere = one-way; order_monitor.py:2017-2029 net-flat close). Money-relevant on live bybit_2 too (currently masked). Full analysis + Tier-3 remediation proposal (recommend Option A: suppress same-dir re-entry while position open + harden reconciler against transient net-flat; behind a kill-switch + walk-forward) in docs/audits/position-netting-sltp-2026-06-08.md. Awaiting operator decision on the proposal before any Tier-3 code. | 2026-06-08 Option A SHIPPED + LIVE (PRs #3023 guard + #3031 account-scope, deployed f81cf9b): the position-netting / per-trade SL/TP guard is now active on both Bybit accounts (POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED=true, POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ACCOUNTS=bybit_1,bybit_2) after a demo-only soak on bybit_1. Monocle suppresses same-direction netted adds; reconciler requires an extra grace tick before closing on a net-flat snapshot. This restores per-trade=per-position, the prerequisite for closed-pnl to repopulate as positions close discretely. Validated: 36 unit tests + net-vs-suppress walk-forward (real BTCUSDT 5m, 4 windows, no trade-count/win-rate regression + lower max-DD). Kept OPEN because the bybit_1 DEMO venue still does not populate /v5/position/closed-pnl, so demo realised-PnL recovery for already-netted historical rows remains limited — forward demo trades should now close per-trade and attribute. Rollback = unset POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED (or narrow POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ACCOUNTS) + restart, no redeploy.

updates.note: TIER-2 PREP → PROPOSED (awaiting operator OK before ship). Root cause: Bybit's closed-pnl endpoint doesn't return reliable per-trade records for the DEMO account (bybit_1 testnet); _bybit_closed_pnl_lookup returns shared/mismatched records (the sibling BL-20260620-CLOSEDPNL-LOOKUP-MISMATCH-DEMO: two SOL paper trades booked an identical -864.45). PROPOSED FIX (Tier-2, paper-only, real-money untouched): for is_demo Bybit trades, route realised-PnL resolution through the LOCAL compute path (src/runtime/local_pnl.py, multiplier-aware via config/instruments.yaml contract_value_usd) instead of the Bybit closed-pnl lookup — mirroring the local_compute path already used for IBKR/Alpaca/OANDA realised PnL (order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced). Net: demo realised PnL becomes entry/exit/qty-derived (deterministic, no shared-record bleed); the misleading backfill that pulls a wrong Bybit record for demo is bypassed. items.source: Session-end observation: PR #3007 (branch claude/vibrant-babbage-9Wbls, head SHA e286c4ea) shows total_count=0 on get_status for 7+ hours after push. No check runs fired at all.
items.title: PR #3007 CI never triggered after push (0 check runs in 7+ h on SHA e286c4ea)
items.description: After opening PR #3007 against main from claude/vibrant-babbage-9Wbls, mcp__github__pull_request_read method=get_status returned state='pending', total_count=0 across 4+ polls over a 7-hour window. No workflow runs reference the head SHA in the Actions list for the period. Either (a) a path/branch filter excluded this PR's changes, (b) the push event was accepted but didn't fan out to workflow triggers, or (c) the runners were idle/wedged. Worth investigating because the same trigger anomaly would silently let other PRs from claude/* branches merge without CI. First step next session: check Actions for any run referencing e286c4ea; if absent, inspect the workflow trigger filters in .github/workflows/*.yml against the changed paths in #3007. An empty commit on the branch would kick the trigger as a workaround if the configs are correct but state is stale.
items.resolution_note: Not a CI bug. All 11 checks ran green on commit 1 (e286c4ea); commit 2 (61c64816) had 0 runs because the PR was dirty — the backlog-JSON appends conflicted with main, which blocks GitHub from building the merge ref, so the synchronize push triggered nothing. get_status/get_check_runs report only the head SHA, hence total_count=0. The path/branch-filter hypothesis is ruled out (no CI workflow has a path filter). Fixed by resolving the conflict and pushing 61c6481..2be6549; 11 checks re-fired green; #3007 merged. See docs/audits/s9-yz-shadow-promotion-2026-06-09.md §1.

items.title: vm-web-api-recover wrapper's 15 s post-restart health probe is too tight for cold-start of ict-web-api.service
items.description: scripts/ops/restart_web_api.sh probes /api/health for ~15 s after the systemctl restart returns. Observed timeline 16:02:23–16:03:01 UTC: systemd stopped uvicorn cleanly (16:02:23–16:02:41), check_data_dir.sh ran (16:02:43–16:02:44), systemd reported 'Started ICT Trading Bot — dashboard API' at 16:02:44, but uvicorn didn't bind port 8001 within the wrapper's 15 s probe window (curl exit 7 at 16:03:01). items.title: regime_bar_scoring budget can starve later predictor groups (no per-tick rotation)
items.description: emit_regime_bar_predictions (src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py:~348-359) iterates groups in fixed insertion order and breaks when the per-tick wall-clock budget (REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S) is hit; the budget check runs before the fetch-gate skip, so the same groups are always considered first each tick. Pathological case: one group whose single fetch always consumes the whole budget could indefinitely defer the groups after it (low practical risk - an already-fetched group is a cheap continue on most ticks). Fix: rotate the group start index per tick, or order by most-overdue-for-a-fetch. Observe-only path, Tier-1.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1). Added per-tick group rotation to emit_regime_bar_predictions (src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py): a module-level _REGIME_GROUP_ROTATION offset (injectable `rotation` param for tests) advances each call and rotates the scan start, so a group whose fetch always eats the whole REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S can no longer indefinitely starve the groups behind it — over successive ticks every group takes a turn at the front of the budget-bounded scan. Observe-only path, unchanged when budget=0/unset. VERIFIED: 2 new tests (a starved group gets scored when rotated to the front; the counter advances each real call) + the existing budget test pinned to rotation=0 for determinism; tests/runtime/test_regime_bar_scoring.py 35 passed.

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid — regime_bar_scoring budget can starve later predictor groups (no per-tick rotation). REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S bounds it. Blocker: Tier-1 code (rotation).

items.title: _capture_account_context_snapshots opens a fresh read-only SQLite connection per signal
items.description: src/core/coordinator.py:~2376 opens a new mode=ro connection on every order-package decision, then loops daily_state_for + open_trades_count_for per account (an N-account fan-out per signal). Best-effort + shares one connection across the account loop, but the connection is re-established each decision. Fix: cache a ro connection across decisions, or fold the per-account reads into one grouped query. Observe-only writer, Tier-1, minor.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1). _capture_account_context_snapshots (src/core/coordinator.py) no longer does a 2-per-account query fan-out per signal: added daily_state_for_accounts() + open_trades_count_for_accounts() to src/units/accounts/context_snapshot.py (each ONE grouped `... IN (?)` query over the whole account set), and the coordinator now issues exactly two grouped reads per decision instead of 2N. Chose the grouped-query fix over a long-lived cached RO connection deliberately — a persistent ro fd on the live trader could read a stale inode after a DB swap/migration, whereas the per-decision open (microseconds) plus 2 grouped queries removes the real N-fan-out cost with no stale-fd risk. Absent/error entries fall back to (None,None)/None, preserving the exact NULL-storing semantics. VERIFIED: 4 new batch-helper tests (match the scalar helpers, empty/missing-table → {}) + the coordinator hook test (tests/test_account_context_snapshot*.py 17 passed).

items.source: MES restore on the isolated-gateway topology (2026-06-10). Connectivity fixed via the OCI SL rule (#3313); the post-connect liveness probe then false-tripped the breaker. items.title: Re-enable the IB liveness probe: retry-tolerant fix shipped, live env flip (IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=5) still pending
items.description: The IB post-connect liveness probe (IBClient._probe_liveness, src/units/accounts/ib_client.py) runs loop.run_until_complete(asyncio.wait_for(ib.reqCurrentTimeAsync(), IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)) on the persistent loop. Over the isolated gateway (10.0.0.251, socat-relayed cross-host) this never resolves even though the connection is fully healthy (connect + 'Logged on server v176' + 'Market data farm connection is OK' + 'Synchronization complete', and the read-path client which skips the probe works) - verified timing out at BOTH 5s and 15s while sync completes in <1s. As a workaround MES is currently running with the probe DISABLED via IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=0 on the live VM (the <=0 skip added in PR #3318); IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S=8 is the backstop. Proper fix: make the probe resolve over this path - likely use ib_insync's sync wrapper ib.reqCurrentTime() (which drives the loop the way connectAsync does) instead of the manual run_until_complete(reqCurrentTimeAsync()), or otherwise pump the reader during the probe; add a regression test mirroring tests/test_ib_integration.py TestEventLoopResilience. Then set-env IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S back to 5 (restores the cheap dead-session catch on top of the per-fetch timeout). Related: BL-20260610-004 Fix 3 (IBMarketData.get_ohlcv should also consult the breaker). Tier-3 (live IB connection path); PR + verify on the live gateway.
items.resolution_note: IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S set back to 5 on the live VM via the set-env system-action (issue #5685) and live-verified against a real forced cold reconnect (vm-ib-gateway-recover, issue #5686: gateway container restarted 09:14:25, IBC login completed 09:14:48). In the minutes after, the retry-tolerant probe hit four separate cold-TCP-flow misses (MES, MGC x2, MHG) between 09:17:42-09:18:10, each logging "attempt 1/2 timed out ... retrying once after 1.5s" and recovering cleanly on the retry with real candle data fetched right after — zero circuit-breaker trips, zero IBConnectionError/ConnectionError in that window (confirmed via journalctl pulls, issues #5688 + #5689). One genuine breaker trip DID fire at 09:14:26, the moment the gateway container was actually down mid-restart (ConnectionError: Socket disconnect) — correct behavior, not a false trip, since it was not a first-attempt asyncio.TimeoutError.

check_log.by: claude (IB pipeline stability review follow-up, 2026-07-06, operator-requested)
check_log.note: Shipped a code fix (PR TBD): IBClient._probe_liveness now retries the reqCurrentTime round-trip ONCE after IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S (default 1.5s) before condemning the connection, instead of failing on a single timeout. Rationale: the probe fires as the FIRST message on a freshly-established connection, right after connect() — a cold TCP flow over the cross-host socat relay can miss that one round-trip even on a genuinely healthy session (every OTHER call — reqHistoricalData, accountSummary — is proven reliable over this exact relay per today's live selftest + diag pulls). A real wedge still never answers either attempt, so detection is unaffected; only a one-off cold-start miss on a healthy session is absorbed. Added 2 regression tests (tests/test_ib_integration.py: cold-miss-then-recovers stays connected + breaker closed; still-hung-after-retry trips the breaker, bounded). This does NOT yet restore protection on the live VM — IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S is still 0 (disabled) in the live .env. Re-enabling it (set to 5, restart ict-trader-live.service) is a deliberate follow-up step that should be verified against a real cold connect over the relay first, not flipped blind alongside the code merge.

RESOLVED + live-flipped. IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=5 is enabled on ict-bot-arm; the retry-tolerant probe (ee522ca) has been proven against a real cold gateway restart with zero false breaker trips. See resolution_note for the full verification trail.

items.source: Operator pasted live ict-trading-bot ERROR logs: bybit_get_positions_failed / bybit_get_order_status_failed -> 'Unmatched IP, please check your API key's bound IP addresses (ErrCode: 10010)' on account=bybit_2, starting ~18:37 UTC (after the 2026-06-14 live->Ampere cutover).
items.title: Bybit API-key bound-IP allowlist not updated for the new Ampere live VM -> ErrCode 10010 on bybit_2 (real-money money-path outage)
items.description: ROOT CAUSE: the live->Ampere cutover (2026-06-14) moved the trader's egress IP from the micro 158.178.210.252 to the Ampere VM ict-bot-arm 141.145.193.91, but the Bybit API key BYBIT_API_KEY_2 (real money, mainnet api.bybit.com) still has its bound-IP allowlist set to the OLD micro IP. Bybit rejects every authed request from the new IP with ErrCode 10010 'Unmatched IP'. Effect: bybit_2 get_positions + get_order_status (and almost certainly order placement) fail every tick -> the real-money account is blind (cannot reconcile / monitor / open new trades). Native exchange-side SL/TP brackets still protect open positions (they fire on Bybit, not via the client). The cutover checklist in docs/runbooks/live-vm-migration-ampere.md NEVER included 'update the Bybit API-key IP allowlist' -- documented now as follow-up item 6. FIX (operator-only, broker-side, no workflow can do it): on Bybit -> API Management, add 141.145.193.91 to the bound-IP list for BYBIT_API_KEY_2 (keep 158.178.210.252 during the rollback soak; drop it at micro decommission). Also check/repeat for BYBIT_API_KEY_1 (demo, api-demo.bybit.com). NOTE the new VM's egress IP is its OCI public IP (1:1 NAT) = 141.145.193.91; if Bybit still rejects after binding, confirm the exact egress empirically before re-editing. Tier: operator broker-side action + Tier-1 doc fix (this entry + runbook item 6).
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-06-15. The operator bound 141.145.193.91 on the Bybit key, but binding the IP is necessary-not-sufficient: the running ict-trader-live + ict-web-api processes hold BYBIT_API_KEY_2 in os.environ from their last start and never re-read creds at runtime, so they kept failing 10010 until RESTARTED (restart-bot-service + vm-web-api-recover reloaded the corrected .env; new-VM processes then authenticate retCode 0 OK, verified by reproducing the exact call inside the trader's /proc/<pid>/environ). LESSON added to runbook item 6: after rebinding the IP on Bybit, RESTART the trader + web-api. items.title: Live IBKR login blocked: bot user's IB Key 2FA is challenge/response (Seamless Authentication OFF) -> headless gateway can't complete a live login
items.description: Paper logins are 2FA-exempt so ib_paper is unaffected and healthy. LIVE logins require 2FA; the bot user's IB Key is in CHALLENGE/RESPONSE mode (Seamless OFF), so IBKR issues no push and the headless gateway (Xvfb) can neither read the on-screen challenge nor type the response -> hangs at 'Authenticating...' and times out. Pinning IBC SecondFactorDevice='IB Key Security via IBKR Mobile' changed nothing (no device-selection dialog ever appeared), confirming the block is upstream of device selection (no push challenge issued). FIX (operator-only, broker-side): enable SEAMLESS (push) authentication for the bot user in IBKR (account-specific; confirm exact steps with IBKR client services -- it is NOT the IBKR-Mobile Security page; involves Client Portal Secure Login + the bot user being registered for IBKR-Mobile push). Seamless push is REQUIRED for live anyway because the gateway re-logs in unattended daily after IBKR's reset; challenge/response cannot be automated. Then re-run via the vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test label and tap the push. NOT URGENT: ib_live is mode:dry_run (not trading); this is a pre-flight for a future capability. Tooling is built + verified. Full runbook: docs/runbooks/ib-live-login-2fa.md. Tier: operator broker-side action + Tier-1 doc (this entry + runbook).

items.source: After BL-20260614-BYBIT-IP was resolved (trader+web-api restarted on the new Ampere VM, key verified), bybit_2 ErrCode 10010 'Unmatched IP' Telegram alerts kept firing every few minutes (fresh ErrTimes, e.g. 13:21:22, 14:21:56). Exhaustive diags proved the NEW VM (141.145.193.91) was clean: every process holds the working key lDRH...CX, reproduce (even inside the trader's exact /proc/<pid>/environ) returns retCode 0 OK, no proxy, and none of the failures appeared in the new VM's outcomes.jsonl.
items.title: Retired x86 micro (158.178.210.252) left running a ZOMBIE bot fleet post-cutover -> spammed bybit_2 ErrCode 10010 from its unbound IP + served stale data to the Android app
items.description: ROOT CAUSE: the 2026-06-14 live->Ampere cutover never actually shut the bot down on the retired micro. ict-trader-live + ict-web-api + a full fleet of TIMERS (ict-hourly-snapshot, ict-insights-generator(-strategies), ict-heartbeat, ict-health-snapshot, ict-web-api-watchdog, ict-git-sync, ict-liveness-watchdog, ...) kept running on the micro with the real bybit_2 key (its .env was unchanged). The micro egresses from 158.178.210.252, which was dropped from the Bybit API-key allowlist at cutover (only 141.145.193.91 is bound), so every authed bybit_2 call (get_positions via the timers' account_snapshots, get_wallet_balance) returned ErrCode 10010 and the micro's outcomes.report fanned it to the SHARED Telegram channel -- indistinguishable from a new-VM failure. The micro's web-api also still answered :8001, so the Android app (default BOT_API_URL = the micro) read live status+MES off it while BTCUSDT came back no_data (micro Bybit-frozen) -- the 'app shows data from the micro' symptom. WHY IT WAS HARD: api_call failures route to outcomes.jsonl + Telegram, NOT stdout, so journalctl was blind; and the new VM always reproduced OK, so the source had to be a different machine. RESOLUTION (operator-approved 'stop services, keep VM for rollback'): built .github/workflows/stop-micro-zombie.yml (issue label stop-micro-zombie) -- SSHes the micro and stop+disables ALL ict-*.timer + ict-*.service units (two passes; the web-api-watchdog + git-sync.timer resurrected the trader through the first two narrow passes -- they MUST be disabled first). Verified fully dark + zero residual python bot processes at 14:45 and again at 14:53 (stable). Micro VM left UP as the rollback target. PROCESS GAP: the cutover/decommission runbook (live-vm-migration-ampere.md Phase 3/4) must STOP+DISABLE the entire ict-* unit fleet on the old VM (or power it off) at cutover -- not just leave it 'stopped'. Rollback = re-enable the micro units + re-add 158.178.210.252 to the Bybit allowlist. Tier: ops action DONE + Tier-1 doc (this entry + runbook Phase 3/4 update).

items.source: Part-2 audit (dashboard code review). In ict-trader-dashboard streamlit_app.py, _lc_candle_data/_lc_ema_data/_lc_volume_data call int(ts.timestamp()) on tz-NAIVE timestamps (host-local epoch), while _lc_markers uses tz-aware UTC. items.title: Dashboard chart timezone divergence (candle/EMA/volume tz-naive vs UTC markers)
items.description: ACTION FOR CLAUDE: localize candle/EMA/volume timestamps to UTC before .timestamp() (pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True) + tz_localize('UTC')) so all series share one epoch basis. This is a UI-rendering change → must go through the dashboard preview-app verification workflow (claude/web-app-preview), NOT straight to main. Low urgency (production runs UTC, masked).

items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1) — fix pushed in ict-trader-dashboard PR #202 (draft, pending CI+merge; UI-render change → verify live on prod app after merge per the repo's single-app workflow). _lc_candle_data/_lc_ema_data/_lc_volume_data called int(ts.timestamp()) on the tz-NAIVE candle timestamp column (host-local epoch), diverging from the tz-aware UTC markers on any non-UTC host. Added _lc_epoch() which localizes a naive Timestamp to UTC (a relabel, not a shift) before .timestamp() so all series share one epoch basis on any host. VERIFIED: recovers the exact epoch (1700000000) from a naive UTC-wallclock ts; aware ts pass through. Masked in prod (Streamlit Cloud runs UTC), so live behaviour there is unchanged.

items.resolution: Investigated + drained 2026-06-19. The '~1100' was a large overcount (stats/perf snapshot mixed already-resolved + paper + pre-account-class-backfill rows). Authoritative live count via the ict-db-integrity checker (INV-2, /api/diag/journalctl): 102 closed pnl-IS-NULL rows, recent=0 (none in the last 48h — the live multiplier-aware sweep keeps current closes clean). PR #4017 hardened scripts/ops/backfill_pnl_nulls.py to delegate to the canonical src.runtime.local_pnl helpers (contract_value_usd multiplier) — it previously undercounted IBKR futures (MGC 10x / MES 5x / MHG 2500x) via a raw (exit-entry)*size formula; real-money bybit_2 (crypto, cvu=1) was unaffected. Ran backfill-pnl-nulls (#4023) -> 0 recomputable candidates (the live sweep had already drained every closed row that has an exit_price), and mark-reconciler-incomplete (#4024) -> 0 reconciler_filled residual. The residual 102 rows all LACK an exit_price (so local compute is impossible and marking to today's price would be wrong) and are old (recent=0); they are correctly NULL and already excluded from /performance + /stats aggregates, so headline totalPnL / expectancy / equity are correct. The sweep's 14-day window is correct as-is (mark-to-market only makes sense for recent closes), so no sweep change is warranted. items.title: Reconciler-filled close writes epoch-ms (not ISO) into trades.closed_at column
items.description: The trades.closed_at column contract is ISO-8601 (every consumer does datetime(closed_at), which returns NULL for a bare ms epoch). The reader-side dashboard endpoint /api/bot/trades/closed was fixed in the trades-closed-reconciler-visibility PR to normalise ms->ISO so buried rows resurface, but that only patches ONE consumer. The TRUE root cause is the writer: order_monitor should normalise the Bybit ms timestamp to ISO before writing the closed_at column (and notes.closed_at), so every consumer (pnl_history, performance, closed_flat_invariant json_extract, the re-adopt flap guard which ORDER BY closed_at DESC, etc.) sees a consistent ISO value and existing ms rows can be one-shot backfilled. This is Tier-2 order-path/monitor code — propose the exact change + a migration for the already-written ms rows; do not merge without operator approval.
items.resolution: Already fixed: order_monitor close paths normalise closed_at via src.utils.closed_at.normalize_closed_at_value at every write site that takes a broker timestamp (lines ~3620, ~4371, ~4430, citing this BL id); other sites write datetime.now().isoformat(). trades.closed_at is ISO going forward. items.source: Live VM diag (issue #4203 journalctl ict-liveness-watchdog.service): the liveness watchdog (Type=oneshot, fires every ~60s) intermittently fails at the systemd STDIN-setup step with `Failed to set up standard input: No such file or directory` / `status=208/STDIN` (~8% of runs; observed 16:08:08 and 16:12:29 UTC), BEFORE check_heartbeat.py runs. Each failure self-heals on the next minute's run, so the unit's `failed` state is transient (the snapshot at 16:12:32 happened to land 3s after a failed run). The repo canonical unit (deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service) sets NO StandardInput (default null -> /dev/null, which cannot ENOENT), so the deployed unit/drop-in has drifted OR a git-sync `git reset --hard` race transiently breaks the spawn.
items.title: VERIFY the liveness-watchdog 208/STDIN intermittent exec failure is gone after the StandardInput=null pin reinstall
items.description: The dead-man switch must spawn reliably on every tick; an ~8% per-run exec failure erodes the 3-strike (~8 min) autoheal margin and a sticky `failed` state masks a genuinely-dead watchdog. Remediation: PR pins `StandardInput=null` explicitly in deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service (BL-20260622-WATCHDOG-STDIN), which on the next runtime git-sync forces install_systemd_units.sh to recopy the (now-differing) unit, reconverging any drift. FOLLOW UP: after the reinstall is confirmed (deployed unit == repo), pull `journalctl?unit=ict-liveness-watchdog.service&lines=200` and confirm ZERO `208/STDIN` occurrences across a >=30-min window. If 208/STDIN PERSISTS after a confirmed reinstall of the explicit-StandardInput unit, the cause is a drop-in (/etc/systemd/system/ict-liveness-watchdog.service.d/*.conf) or a git-sync `git reset --hard` spawn race (NOT main-unit drift) — escalate to a targeted system-action that `systemctl cat`s the deployed unit + drop-ins and purges any rogue drop-in. Note: the `/etc/ict-vm-role: No such file or directory` log line in deploy_pull_restart.sh line 91 is cosmetic/expected on the trader (empty role = not gateway); NOT a drift to fix.
items.resolution: PR #4206 pinned StandardInput=null on deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service; merged 2026-06-22T16:36:59Z (main baeec23e) and deployed via ict-git-sync (full path: install_systemd_units.sh recopied the now-differing unit + one trader bounce; VM confirmed on git_sha baeec23e, trader healthy post-restart). SOAK VERIFIED: watchdog journal 16:41:01-17:17:04 UTC (~36 min, ~36 consecutive per-minute runs, diag issue #4210) shows EVERY run clean (Starting -> Deactivated successfully -> Finished); ZERO 208/STDIN / "Failed to set up standard input" after the reinstall, vs ~8% failure rate before. Root cause confirmed as MAIN-UNIT DRIFT (reconverged by the idempotent reinstall) — NOT a drop-in or git-sync reset --hard race, so no escalation/purge action needed. The /etc/ict-vm-role "No such file" deploy-log line was confirmed cosmetic/expected on the trader.

Investigate the instant-close path (closedAt<=openedAt, null exit) in order_monitor — likely a netting/flat reconcile that booked a close without an exit fill. check_log.note: Fix landed (order_monitor close/sweep path, Tier-2): the gap was the local-compute sweep deferring broker-reader (Bybit) rows the full 7-day _BROKER_PNL_RECOVERY_MS window while the Bybit closed-pnl sweep could never fill them (no realised closed-pnl record exists for a same-instant net-flat). Between the 6h INV-2 grace and day 7 nothing touched the row -> closed/NULL -> INV-2. Fix: new _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS (6h = DEFAULT_PNL_GRACE_HOURS) shortens the local-sweep defer so a broker row the reader still can't price converges to local_compute (pnl~=0 truthful for a same-instant flat) right after the grace. Broker truth still wins within the grace. +3 tests in tests/test_local_pnl.py. The larger 'should it be booked closed at all' question logged for follow-up if instant-flat reconciles recur.

No recurrence of the 06:00Z wedge observed since the retime. Leaving open one more full week before closing outright to be sure — full findings in docs/research/ib-pipeline-stability-review-2026-07-06.md.

RECURRENCE 2026-07-07 ~07:55:14Z: ict-web-api.service journal (diag #5829) shows 'IBClient: account/portfolio warm-up timed out twice (8s+8s retry) for 10.0.0.251:4002 (account=...5724) -- gateway likely logged out' + 'circuit breaker tripped ... consecutive failures=16'; concurrent exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper (diag #5831) reads positions=null (could-not-read). Raised as the mandatory broker-reachability flag for this review (see anomalies/flags). Recommend vm-ib-gateway-recover if not already auto-fired by the reachability-alert latch.

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING: system-actions.yml's gateway-logs action has been silently pointed at the wrong host since the 2026-06-10 gateway-isolation redesign -- it SSHes to VM_SSH_HOST (141.145.193.91, the live trader) and runs 'docker ps/logs ib-gateway' there, but the ib-gateway container has lived on the dedicated gateway VM (10.0.0.251) since that redesign. This means every attempt since 2026-06-10 to use gateway-logs for root-causing a wedge (including the open BL-20260527-003 investigation) silently got no real data. FIXED this session (system-actions.yml): gateway-logs now routes via ProxyJump through the trader to GATEWAY_HOST (10.0.0.251), mirroring the pattern already used by vm-ib-gateway-recover.yml/vm-ib-gateway-selftest.yml. Also confirmed the current wedge self-recovered on its own between 07:56Z and 08:39Z (exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper went from positions:null to positions:[],error:null) without an operator/Claude-triggered recover -- so the reactive watchdog or a passive retry cleared it, timeline TBD once gateway-logs is re-run post-fix.

OPERATOR DECISION: explored two mitigation paths for the recurring IB-gateway instability -- (1) IBKR's own Client Portal Web API (CPAPI) as a same-account transport swap to escape the Xvfb/IBC GUI-automation layer, and (2) migrating futures to a broker with a cleaner native API (Tradovate, Ironbeam direct API, Rithmic via AMP/Ironbeam). CPAPI is closed off: it requires an IBKR Pro account (confirmed via IBKR's own docs -- Lite is unsupported for API access, no SSO-only carve-out), and the operator does not have Pro and cannot get it in a relevant timeframe. On reviewing the broker-migration options (Tradovate/Ironbeam/Rithmic), the operator decided none of them are worth pursuing right now. DECISION: drop both lines of investigation for now -- stay on the current TWS-socket/ib_insync/Xvfb/IBC integration. The gateway-logs system-action routing fix (this session, see the linked PR) remains valuable regardless -- it unblocks root-causing future wedges on the CURRENT integration, which is now the only path being pursued for IB reliability. Revisit CPAPI/broker-migration only if the account tier changes or the wedge frequency/impact gets materially worse.

items.title: [risk] crypto/fx sub-min-lot refusal uses account-default min_qty, not the per-instrument platform lot (ETH 0.01 gap)
items.description: PR #4969 (merged) made a sub-min-lot risk-based size a per-trade REFUSAL on the crypto/fx (non-whole-unit) path instead of bumping it up to min_qty (the over-risk #3910 flagged). It was scoped MINIMALLY: the refusal threshold is the ACCOUNT-configured min_qty (RiskManager.min_qty, default 0.001), NOT the per-instrument platform lot from config/instruments.yaml. For BTCUSDT that's correct (real lot == 0.001), but ETHUSDT's real Bybit lot is 0.01 (instruments.yaml min_qty/qty_step 0.01) — so a risk-based ETH size in [0.001, 0.0099) currently passes the refusal (>= account 0.001) yet the exchange would reject it as sub-lot. Pre-existing (the old bump was equally wrong there) and NOT worsened by #4969 — bybit_2's live ETH position (0.01) sizes legitimately today. items.title: [infra] live trader VM /dev/null clobbered into a regular file — blocks all operator-action wrappers (pull-and-deploy / restart / reboot) and every '>/dev/null' redirect
items.description: DISCOVERED 2026-06-29 while deploying #5061: the pull-and-deploy system-action FAILED with 'ERROR: /dev/null is not writable on this host — it has been clobbered into a regular file, so every ">/dev/null" redirect (and most operator-action wrappers) fail.' On the LIVE trader VM (ict-bot-arm, 141.145.193.91), /dev/null is a regular file instead of the char-special device (1,3). IMPACT: (a) every operator-action wrapper that preflight-checks or redirects to /dev/null aborts — pull-and-deploy, restart-bot-service, reboot-vm are all blocked (so the relay can't even self-repair this), (b) any process doing '>/dev/null' fails, (c) a future systemd restart of ict-trader-live whose ExecStart/redirects touch /dev/null could fail to come up. NOT currently fatal: ict-git-sync still auto-deployed #5061 (trader confirmed on git_sha d661a0ec, uptime ~104s, heartbeat running, ticks healthy) and the trader is alive — but this is a latent live-VM hazard. ROOT FIX (needs root ON the VM; no autonomous path — the action wrappers that would run it are themselves blocked by the same /dev/null breakage, so this is a genuine operator hand-off): `sudo rm -f /dev/null && sudo mknod -m 666 /dev/null c 1 3`. After repair, re-dispatch pull-and-deploy to confirm the operator-action path works again. FOLLOW-UP: find what clobbered /dev/null (a stray '>' to the literal path /dev/null from a process that ran with /dev not mounted, or a script bug writing to '/dev/null' as a file) so it doesn't recur; consider a cheap health-check assertion that /dev/null is char-special (1,3).
