items.title: [infra root-source] stop the OCI host agent clobbering /dev/null on the live VM (the recurring source behind the guard + self-heals)
items.description: The live trader VM's /dev/null is repeatedly clobbered by an OS-level OCI host agent (suspected oracle-cloud-agent oci-wlp / Cloud Guard Workload-Protection FIM 'remediating' world-writable files, incorrectly including /dev/null) — see docs/runbooks/devnull-guard.md. As of 2026-06-29 we now have THREE self-heal layers (ict-devnull-guard.timer 60s, deploy_pull_restart.sh, and _lib.sh::require_systemctl — the last two added this session) plus the guard %-specifier bugfix, so consumers no longer break on a transient clobber. REMAINING: kill it at the source so /dev/null isn't being rm'd/chmod'd at all. AUTONOMOUS path to try first (SSH+sudo via a runner, NOT operator-manual): `sudo auditctl -w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull` then after it next flips `sudo ausearch -k devnull` to positively identify the writing process/agent; if it's a local oracle-cloud-agent plugin, disable that plugin's /dev remediation via its on-VM config. OPERATOR/OCI-CONSOLE path (only if the rule is tenancy-level): exclude /dev from the OCI Cloud Guard / Workload-Protection FIM profile attached to the instance — needs OCI console/tenancy access (a legitimate category-1 operator/external action). OPTIONAL mitigation regardless: tighten ict-devnull-guard.timer OnUnitActiveSec 60s -> ~20-30s to shrink the exposure window for any non-self-healing consumer (e.g. the trader's own >/dev/null subprocess plumbing). | 2026-07-14 ROUND-5/6 FINDINGS (session_01SDLWbfLGV4WYHgC2ugzedf): (1) The strip is a chmod to 644 (NOT 444) — guard journal 'was 644' heals at 14:20:44/14:58:51/15:12:01/15:27:13Z, recurring ~15-40min, NOT restart-correlated. (2) The denied opens ARE captured (key=devnull success=no exit=-13 EACCES; victims bash/git/ld/python/gawk, uid=1001, subj=unconfined) — NOT AppArmor; no shadow mount (findmnt clean); no DELETE/CREATE. (3) DECISIVE: the -w /dev/null -p wa watch does NOT capture chmod on this aarch64 kernel — the guard's own chmod-0666 heals at exact known timestamps produced ZERO attr records, so the culprit's chmod-644 was equally invisible (rounds 3-5 'no mutation events' inferences were artifacts of a blind watch). (4) Round-6 armed: explicit syscall rules -S fchmod,fchmodat (+setxattr family) -F path=/dev/null -k devnullmode via vm-devnull-diagnose arm-audit; with strips recurring ~15-40min the next read-audit should name the culprit exe=/ppid= directly. ausearch remains broken (use journald _TRANSPORT=audit or raw /var/log/audit grep, ~7.5h retention). | 2026-07-14 ROUND-7 CONCLUSION (session_01SDLWbfLGV4WYHgC2ugzedf): a denial window hit at 19:26Z, FOUR MINUTES after the fchmodat2 (#452) rule armed (19:22Z re-arm confirmed in CONFIG_CHANGE rows) — and the devnullmode key STILL captured zero events. Every plausible arch=b64 userspace mutation path is now EXCLUDED by direct observation: fchmod/fchmodat/fchmodat2/setxattr-family (armed syscall rules, silent), node DELETE/CREATE + mounts (clean), AppArmor (subj=unconfined victims, no AVC). Residual hypotheses, in rough likelihood order: (a) kernel-internal attribute change on the devtmpfs inode (no syscall record by construction) — e.g. a snapd/OCI-agent device-cgroup or devtmpfs refresh path; (b) arch=b32 compat process (untested — b32 audit rules may not even load on this Ampere kernel without CONFIG_COMPAT); (c) an eBPF/LSM inode modification. ACTIVE HUNTING PAUSED after 7 rounds: the operational impact is fully mitigated (ict-devnull-guard 60s heal + restart_bot.sh mid-run heal_devnull + ERR_SINK, all live-verified), strips are brief (~15-60s before heal) and harm nothing, and the devnull/devnullmode traps STAY ARMED — if a future capture names the culprit, resume at the source-kill step (Tier-2, operator OK). Empirical facts bank: chmod to 644 (not 444); windows recur in bursts roughly aligned with the ~15-min timer/tick cadence; victims are all uid-1001 + snap_daemon (oracle-cloud-agent unifiedmonitoring appears as a VICTIM, weakening the original oci-wlp-as-culprit theory).

updates.note: Diagnostic tooling BUILT (Tier-1); the mutating step is HELD for one operator OK. The prior hand-off ('sudo auditctl ... then ausearch') is now an owner-gated workflow: .github/workflows/vm-devnull-source-diagnose.yml (label vm-devnull-diagnose, added to bootstrap-labels.yml). Modes: inspect (READ-ONLY — dumps oracle-cloud-agent/oci-wlp units+plugins+config and greps its logs for dev/null|remediat|world-writable + current /dev/null state + any existing auditd rule/events; may name the agent with zero mutation), arm-audit (Tier-2 — installs auditd if absent + persistent /etc/audit/rules.d/devnull.rules '-w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull', survives reboot), read-audit (READ-ONLY — ausearch -k devnull -i; CULPRIT = the SYSCALL setting mode 0444/stripping the write bit; the guard's own 0666 restores are expected noise). Run inspect first; only arm-audit needs the operator ack. Once the writer is identified: reconfigure the on-VM agent plugin's /dev remediation (autonomous via runner+sudo) OR exclude /dev from the tenancy Cloud Guard/Workload-Protection FIM profile (OCI-console operator action if tenancy-level).

Diagnostic pass (vm-devnull-diagnose #6130 read-audit + #6132 inspect). Findings: (1) the auditd watch IS loaded/active — `auditctl -l` → `-w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull`; auditd running. (2) ausearch -k devnull is EMPTY — no /dev/null attr event captured since arming. (3) /dev/null healthy: 666 char(1,3), mtime unmoved ~20h; ict-devnull-guard runs every ~60s but every cycle 'Finished' as a no-op (it only mknod/chmods on a detected problem) — i.e. NO clobber has occurred in ~20h. The clobber is far rarer than the 'recurring' framing (or currently dormant); the guard fully contains the symptom. (4) NO direct attribution in the oracle-cloud-agent logs — the apparent '0444' grep hits are MICROSECOND-TIMESTAMP false positives (e.g. '18:34:10.000444'), not mode-0444 remediation lines; no 'remediated /dev/null' log exists. Prime suspect remains oci-wlp (OCI Workload Protection / FIM plugin — snap.oracle-cloud-agent running; oci-falcon NOT installed) but UNCONFIRMED. FORWARD PATH: leave the watch armed; the NEXT clobber will be captured by `-w -p wa` (attribute-change) with the acting exe/pid → attribution. IF the next confirmed flip ALSO yields an empty ausearch, THEN the -w watch has a blind spot and we add a syscall rule (`-a always,exit -F path=/dev/null -F perm=a -k devnull`). No source-kill is proposable without attribution, and the guard makes this LOW-urgency. No operator action needed now.

Re-validated 2026-07-19: root-source (OCI host agent clobbering /dev/null) NOT eliminated — the recurring source behind the whole devnull cluster. Currently /dev/null is healthy (this session's actions succeeded). Blocker: Tier-2 infra (stop the host agent / durable guard).

NEW CLUE (read-audit re-run, issue #7298, 2026-07-21T07:52Z): the armed audit rules are STILL capturing zero chmod/fchmod/fchmodat/fchmodat2/setxattr/mount events on /dev/null (the mode-strip mechanism remains syscall-invisible to this rule set, as in Rounds 5-7) -- but this pass's DENIED-open sweep (success=no, key=devnull) caught one denial from Oracle's OWN agent, not just our tooling: comm="unifiedmonitori" exe="/snap/oracle-cloud-agent/118/plugins/unifiedmonitoring/unifiedmonitoring" subj=snap.oracle-cloud-agent.oracle-cloud-agent, EACCES on openat, in the same ~07:35Z window as ~30 denied opens from our own unconfined bash/git/python. items.source: The RPT-20260702-061700-since-last /system-review report flagged btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 and btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 as advisory-stage models that had stopped producing shadow_predictions rows since 2026-06-23 / 2026-06-25. Diagnosis (vm-diag-request shadow_stats?model_id=...&stage=shadow on both, 2026-07-02T07:43Z) found both models ACTIVELY logging shadow-stage predictions with last_seen within minutes of the query (630 / 10169 records, healthy non-degenerate score distributions) — not stale at all.
items.title: ml-review staleness check should track a model's CURRENT registry stage, not the stage it was at when first observed
items.description: Root cause of the false alarm: both models were demoted advisory→shadow around 2026-06-23 / 2026-06-25 (MB-20260623-001 / MB-20260625-001, degenerate live-score reasons — the yz vol_bucket-edge calibration gap documented in src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py's own module docstring). ShadowPredictor logs whatever `stage` value it was instantiated with, so predictions before the demotion carry stage="advisory" and predictions after carry stage="shadow" for the SAME model_id. The staleness check that fed the system-review evidently kept querying (or reasoning about) the OLD stage label instead of re-resolving the model's current registry stage before judging it stale — so a clean, expected demotion looked identical to a silent failure. No code fix needed for the models themselves (they are healthy); the fix is in the review methodology: any future staleness/liveness check for a shadow model should look up its CURRENT target_deployment_stage from the registry first, then query shadow_stats for that stage specifically — never assume the stage recorded at first-flagged-stale time is still current.
items.trigger_condition: Next /ml-review or /system-review session that flags a shadow/advisory model as stale or silently dead.
items.resolution_criteria: The staleness-check step in the ml-review / system-review skill (wherever it lives) re-resolves each candidate model's current registry stage before querying shadow_stats, rather than reusing a stage captured earlier in the session or assumed from a prior finding.
items.resolution: Diagnosed as a false alarm, not a bug in the models or the shadow-logging pipeline (Track C of the 2026-07-02 system-review follow-up plan). Both btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 and btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 confirmed actively producing shadow-stage predictions in real time. Logged here as a methodology note for the next /ml-review or /system-review session to avoid re-flagging the same false positive — no code changed.

items.source: gpu-burst-train.yml run 28772601594 (arm-B burst issue #5642) was CANCELLED while queued: the workflow triggers on EVERY issues.opened (non-labeled ones conclude 'skipped'), and its single `concurrency: group: gpu-burst-train` means each new issue's run displaces the previously PENDING run in the group - so an unrelated trainer-diag/diag-request issue opened while one burst runs silently cancels the next queued burst.
items.title: gpu-burst-train concurrency group lets ANY new issue cancel a queued burst
items.description: Queued (pending) gpu-burst runs are silently cancelled by any subsequent issue in the repo because all issues.opened events share the one concurrency group. A cancelled burst looks like 'never ran' unless someone inspects the Actions history. Observed 2026-07-06 (arm B #5642 cancelled by the #5643 trainer-diag issue's skip-run); worked around by firing bursts one at a time.
items.suggested_fix: Gate the concurrency group on the label match (e.g. move the label check to a first job whose output gates the burst job, and key concurrency as gpu-burst-${{ github.event.issue.number }} on the burst job only, or set the group at job level only for labeled issues). Keep spend-gate serialization by having the burst job itself take a repo-level lock (the ledger commit step already serializes on push).
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review / CI-touching session.
items.resolution: Fixed: the concurrency group is now conditional — only gpu-burst-train-labelled runs share the serializing 'gpu-burst-train' group (so two real bursts still can't run at once), while every other issues.opened event (diag-relay, system-action, trainer-diag skip-runs) gets a unique 'gpu-burst-skip-<run_id>' group and can never cancel a queued burst. Root cause was that concurrency is evaluated at the workflow level before the job's label `if`, so all issues entered the one group.

items.source: diag relay issues #5827/#5829/#5831 (2026-07-07): GET /api/bot/health/latest and /api/bot/health/services both returned non-2xx (curl --fail -> 'fetch_failed') on TWO independent pulls this session, and /api/bot/accounts/balances failed the same way once, while every sibling /api/bot/* route in the SAME ssh batch (stats, positions, order-packages, trades/closed, strategies/*/review, candles, config, etc.) succeeded. Code review: src/web/api/routers/accounts.py::get_account_balances is `async def` but calls `_from_db()` -> `Database().get_latest_balance_snapshots()` synchronously (a blocking sqlite3 read against a 433MB trade_journal.db under constant live-trader write load), not wrapped in run_in_threadpool/asyncio.to_thread.
items.title: GET /api/bot/health/{latest,services} and /api/bot/accounts/balances intermittently return non-2xx -- likely a blocking DB call stalling uvicorn's single event loop under load
items.description: Reproduced twice this session (diag #5827 first batch, #5829 targeted retry) for health/latest + health/services; accounts/balances failed once (#5831), succeeded in other pulls. Hypothesis: `accounts.py::_from_db()` runs a synchronous sqlite3 read directly inside an `async def` route with no thread-pool offload -- if that read blocks (WAL lock contention / long fsync under the live trader's constant write volume), it freezes uvicorn's whole single-worker event loop, starving every other in-flight request (which is why health/latest and health/services, both otherwise-trivial file/subprocess reads, failed in the same window). This co-occurred with a live IB-gateway circuit-breaker trip (BL-20260623-002 recurrence) and a burst of ~80 near-simultaneous dashboard/Android requests in the same ~90s window (ict-web-api journalctl, diag #5829) -- consistent with event-loop contention, though not proven without a direct trace. A similar class of bug was just fixed for IB account/position reads in commit 1f286ee (BL-20260706-IBCONCURRENCY, 'offload IB account/position reads off uvicorn's event loop') -- this may be the same pattern in a different router. FIX (Tier-1, API code, no live-trade-path risk): wrap `Database().get_latest_balance_snapshots()` in `asyncio.to_thread(...)` (or equivalent) inside `accounts.py::get_account_balances`; audit `health_snapshots.py::get_services`'s `subprocess.run` similarly (it already has timeout=3 but is still a blocking call inside an async route). Verify by re-pulling health/latest + health/services + accounts/balances via the diag relay several times back-to-back and confirming no repeat 'fetch_failed', ideally during/after a deliberately-induced DB-busy window.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED (RISK-3 Task 1) by PR #6029 (9c3987d, 'web-api: eliminate event-loop-blocking in async routes'), verified on main 2026-07-09. Every blocking read route across 23 routers is now either a plain `def` (FastAPI threadpools sync routes) or an `async def` that offloads via `asyncio.to_thread` (`get_account_balances` is now plain `def`; `prop.post_report` offloads `ingest_report`). `PRAGMA busy_timeout=3000` added to both connect paths (`prop_journal._connect` + `units/db/database.py`). A permanent class-eliminator AST guard `scripts/ci/check_async_route_blocking.py` is wired as the `async-route-blocking-guard` CI merge gate (green) + `tests/test_async_route_blocking_guard.py`.

items.source: journal?table=trades (diag relay #5836), trade id 3224: 2026-07-07T02:15:10Z, mgc_pullback_1d short MGC on ib_paper, status=exchange_rejected. entry_reason: 'RuntimeError: IB _submit_order: IBClient: Gateway at 10.0.0.251:4002 (account=…5724) answered the liveness probe but never delivered account/portfolio data within 8s (likely logged out or no account resolved). Tripping circuit breaker so IB calls do not block the trader loop.'
items.title: IB account/portfolio-warmup timeout recurred on ib_paper the day after BL-20260706-IBWARMUP / BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION landed — confirm the fix is actually deployed + effective
items.description: This is the exact failure signature (`IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S` probe-then-condemn path in `IBClient.connect()`/`_warm_account_data`) that BL-20260706-IBWARMUP and its BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION follow-up were supposed to fix on 2026-07-06. Seeing it trip again on 2026-07-07T02:15Z blocked a legitimate mgc_pullback_1d short (confidence 0.55, trending regime ADX 37.9 — a decent setup that never got a chance to fill; see performance-review scoring for pkg-8d2b5d6cffbc4552). Two possibilities: (a) the fix reduces but does not eliminate cold-TCP-flow misses (the retry-then-condemn design accepts SOME residual failures by construction, per IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S's own docs — in which case this is expected background noise, not a regression); or (b) the fix hasn't actually rolled to the live VM (check `/api/diag/version` git_sha against the PR merge commit) or isn't retrying as designed. FIX: pull `/api/diag/version` + `/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service` around 2026-07-07T02:14-02:16Z to see whether `_warm_account_data` actually attempted its documented retry before condemning the connection; if the retry never fired, the deploy or the retry logic itself needs a second look. If it did retry and still failed, this is within the documented residual-failure envelope and just needs a frequency count over a longer window before deciding whether IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S/IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S need raising.
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review or VM investigation session; also re-check if this recurs multiple times in a short window (would argue for (b) over (a)).
items.resolution_criteria: Either confirmed as expected residual noise within the documented retry-tolerant design (close as won't-fix, cite the retry evidence), or confirmed as a deploy/logic gap and fixed with a follow-up PR.
items.resolution: NOT A REGRESSION — outcome (a): the retry-tolerant warm-up worked exactly as designed and correctly condemned a GENUINELY-WEDGED gateway. Definitive evidence from the narrow journalctl window (diag relay #5847, 2026-07-07T02:13-02:16Z on ict-trader-live.service): the gateway (10.0.0.251:4002, clientId 497) failed the LIVENESS PROBE repeatedly 02:13:05-02:14:47 ('liveness probe attempt 1/2 timed out after 5s ... retrying once'), then on the mgc_pullback_1d dispatch at 02:14:52 the probe passed but the WARM-UP 'timed out TWICE (8s + 8s retry)' at 02:15:10 -> 'gateway likely logged out' -> breaker tripped (consecutive failures=1) -> order rejected. So the documented retry (BL-20260706-IBWARMUP / BL-20260610-009) DID fire on both the probe and the warm-up; the gateway genuinely wasn't answering either attempt. Deploy confirmed current at the time (/api/diag/version git_sha=3690317e, well after the 2026-07-06 fix commits). This was an UNSCHEDULED gateway wedge (02:15Z is before IBKR's ~03:45-05:45 reset window), and the gateway recovered on its own (a live exchange_positions read on ib_paper succeeded at 10:05Z). CONCLUSION: raising IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S / adding retries would be the WRONG fix — the gateway was DOWN, not slow, and a longer timeout would only block the trader loop longer. The warm-up/breaker path is correct: it isolated the dead gateway from the loop, which is its job. The two GENUINE gaps this exposed are NOT in the warmup code: (1) gateway-wedge RECOVERY LATENCY (reactive gateway-VM watchdog ~10-15min + daily 06:05 reset), and (2) DROPPED DAILY SIGNALS — a 1d strategy fires once, so a wedge at the exact fire moment loses the signal entirely with no retry. (2) is the real hardening opportunity (retry a breaker-open-rejected order across the next few ticks) and is surfaced to the operator as a Tier-2/3 design option; if pursued it gets its own item, not this one. Observability for all of this now ships via /api/diag/ib_state (PR #5845, merged e08fe3a).

items.source: journal?table=trades (diag relay #5836), trade ids 3226/3227 (mgc_trend_1h short MGC, ib_paper, 2026-07-07 05:25/06:00Z): `entry_reason` reads 'REJECTED: dry_run_no_order_placed | mgc_trend_1h signal' and `notes.reason` is 'dry_run_no_order_placed' with `notes.is_dry: false` — but the linked order_package's `meta.rejected_reason` says 'risk-refused (no fill placed); reconciled from the journalled rejection row' and `meta.rejected_by: monitor_reconciler`.
items.title: mgc_trend_1h rejections carry a stale/mismatched 'dry_run_no_order_placed' entry_reason text while the order-package meta records the real cause as risk-refused (reconciled)
items.description: Two data points disagree about WHY the same rejected trade happened: the `trades.entry_reason`/`notes.reason` literally say 'dry_run_no_order_placed' (which would imply `is_dry: true`), yet the same row's `notes.is_dry` is `false` and the linked order_package's `meta` says the real cause was a risk-manager refusal later reconciled by `monitor_reconciler`. This is confusing for anyone (human or /performance-review) reading `trades.entry_reason` at face value — it doesn't match the account's actual dry-run state or the order package's own recorded rejection cause. Likely a stale/leftover reason string written at an earlier point in the rejection path that never got updated when the reconciler backfilled the real cause into `meta`. FIX (Tier-1, observability/data-integrity, no live-trade-path change): trace where `entry_reason='dry_run_no_order_placed'` gets written for a `mgc_trend_1h`/ib_paper rejection (likely `src/runtime/orders.py` or the risk-refusal path in `RiskManager`) and confirm it reflects the account's actual `is_dry` state, or have the reconciler backfill the same corrected text into `trades.entry_reason` (not just `order_packages.meta`) so the two never disagree again.
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review or a session touching the risk-refusal/reconciler rejection-reason write path.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the root cause is found and the reason text is corrected (both fields agree), or the discrepancy is explained as intentional (e.g. two independent 'reason' fields with legitimately different meanings) and documented so it stops looking like a bug.

updates.note: ROOT FRAME CLARIFIED (narrows the fix, item stays open): the 'dry_run_no_order_placed' entry_reason is NOT a stale/wrong string — mgc_trend_1h is config execution:shadow (config/strategies.yaml L785), so the STRATEGY-level shadow gate folds into effective_dry in Coordinator.multi_account_execute even though the ACCOUNT (ib_paper) is mode:live and notes.is_dry (the account-level flag) is correctly false. So 'dry_run_no_order_placed' is the CORRECT disposition for a shadow-suppressed package; there is no is_dry contradiction. The ONE genuine inconsistency left is cosmetic: the reconciler backfills order_packages.meta.rejected_reason='risk-refused (no fill placed); reconciled from the journalled rejection row' for these shadow-suppressed packages, which is misleading — they were shadow-suppressed, not risk-refused. FIX (Tier-1, cosmetic): have the reconciler label a shadow/dry-suppressed no-fill as such (e.g. 'shadow_suppressed_no_order' / 'dry_run_no_order_placed') rather than the generic 'risk-refused' when the underlying journal row's reason is dry_run/shadow. Downgraded in practical severity — nothing is mis-executing; a reader just needs to know shadow==effective_dry.

items.resolution: Root cause found + fixed (Tier-1 observability — label-only, no order-path behaviour change). TWO independent bugs made trades.entry_reason disagree with notes.is_dry: (1) log_rejection_to_journal HARDCODED is_dry=False for every rejection row, so even a genuine dry/shadow skip (mgc_trend_1h is execution: shadow — demoted live->shadow 2026-06-18) wrote reason='dry_run_no_order_placed' with notes.is_dry=false, a direct contradiction; and (2) execute_pkg forces is_dry=True when exchange_client is None (a LIVE account with the IB gateway wedged) and journaled it with the SAME 'dry_run_no_order_placed' reason — mislabeling a gateway-down infra skip as an intentional dry-run. Fix: log_rejection_to_journal now takes is_dry (writes notes.is_dry; default False, back-compat) and the dry-branch caller passes the honest value + a cause-specific reason: genuine dry/shadow -> 'dry_run_no_order_placed' + is_dry=True; client-unavailable -> new 'exchange_client_unavailable_no_order_placed' + is_dry=False. Both fields now always AGREE. Verified is_dry writes ONLY notes.is_dry — the is_demo/account_class paper-vs-real column is derived separately from account_cfg and is unaffected (new test asserts this). paper_record_classifier _REFUSAL_MARKERS gained 'exchange_client_unavailable' so the new reason still buckets as a refusal. 2 new tests + full execute/coordinator/classifier sweep (451 passed). Shipped on PR #6302 branch.

items.title: Config-only PRs can merge with a RED full test suite — the filtered pytest-run skips the config-assertion tests
items.description: Twice this session, config/docs-heavy PRs (#5850 turtle_soup demote + ib_paper prune; #5851 pull-ibkr-history system-action) merged GREEN via a fast/filtered pytest-run that did NOT execute the full suite, leaving main's full-suite CI RED: test_strategy_execution_gate (turtle_soup now shadow), test_ib_integration x2 (ib_paper strategy list), test_intent_delta_dispatch (turtle_soup-as-live premise), test_system_actions_workflow + test_notify_run (pull-ibkr-history allowlist/priority). The failures were only exposed when the NEXT PR (#5853) touched real code and triggered the full 7192-test run. A config-only change that breaks a config-assertion test should NOT be able to merge green. Likely the pytest-run job path-filters to changed files/affected tests and a config/yaml/workflow change resolves to 'no affected tests'. FIX OPTIONS: (a) always run the full suite on changes to config/**, .github/workflows/**, docs that back tests; or (b) map config/strategies.yaml + config/accounts.yaml + the workflow allowlist to their assertion tests in the affected-test selector; or (c) a nightly full-suite run on main that alarms on red. All 5+ tests were fixed in #5853, so main is green now — this backlog item is about the PROCESS gap that let it go red.
items.trigger_condition: Next CI/tooling pass, or when a config PR merges green but a later PR's full suite goes red.

items.title: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (bot-caused, not broker-side): a mass reconciler false-close on 2026-07-07T14:15:56Z hid ~$218k of still-open, uncapped concurrent notional exposure on alpaca_paper — see BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE for the mechanism
items.description: Investigated a 'ALL accounts failed to dispatch' alert (spy_pullback_1h/SPY, alpaca_paper + alpaca_live). alpaca_live's risk_refused was plain underfunding — not a bug. alpaca_paper's zero_balance (shared Alpaca paper login with alpaca_options_paper, both ~-$67,946) took several rounds to trace because the trades journal's own pnl was actively misleading (see below). FINAL MECHANISM, confirmed via a fresh diag pull at 2026-07-07T16:19-16:28Z, minutes after it happened: at 2026-07-07T14:15:56.749880Z, `position_snapshot_reconciler` closed MULTIPLE alpaca_paper positions across DIFFERENT symbols simultaneously (same closed_at timestamp on trades 3131 SPY 125sh, 3077 SPY 142sh — wait, distinct order_package_ids but same closed_at batch also covers 3060 SLV 1360sh, 2868 GLD 33.6sh, 2774 TLT 231sh, and more), each stamped `pnl_source: local_compute` / `exit_price_source: local_markprice` (a FABRICATED mark-to-market, not a real fill) — almost certainly because the reconciler's exchange-positions read came back empty/misread at that moment and it concluded every open position was flat (the same failure class as the historical 'AlpacaClient.positions() returning [] instead of None on a read failure' bug this repo has hardened against elsewhere, e.g. RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S). The individual fabricated PnLs looked small/benign (+$805, -$441, +$1706, -$434, -$176, etc.) — which is why an earlier pass through this backlog entry incorrectly concluded the journal 'didn't show a loss anywhere near -$67,946' and pointed the operator at Alpaca's own activity screen instead. ~2 hours later, at 2026-07-07T16:19:38-45Z, the REVERSE reconciler discovered the SAME positions were STILL genuinely open on the broker (they never actually closed) and re-adopted all of them fresh as `adopted_orphan` rows: SPY 125sh (~$92.6k), SLV 1360sh (~$73.5k), TLT 10sh, QQQ 16sh (~$11.9k), IWM 9sh (~$2.7k), IEF 8sh (~$753) — all simultaneously open on the SAME $100k paper account, ~$180k+ of concurrent notional exposure stacked across independently-sized strategies (spy_pullback_1h, slv_trend_1h, qqq_pullback_1h, iwm_trend_long_1d, ief_pullback_1d, tlt_pullback_1d/1h), each individually risk-bounded at trade-open time but with NO portfolio-level aggregate cap across strategies on one account. THIS is genuinely bot-caused: (1) the reconciler bug corrupted the journal's view of reality (false closes with fabricated PnL), which is why searching the journal for 'the loss' kept coming up empty; (2) the real financial exposure was always sitting on the broker the whole time, continuously, as an uncapped multi-strategy stack — exactly the mechanism BL-20260707-ALPACA-PULLBACK-NOTIONAL-SIZING flagged for a single trade, but worse in aggregate across concurrently-open positions. The operator's report that 'the old account reset itself to $100k' does NOT match this diag pull (accounts/balances as_of 2026-07-07T16:01Z still reads -$67,945.12 for both alpaca_paper and alpaca_options_paper) — worth the operator double-checking which account/view showed the reset (possibly the NEW dedicated alpaca_options_paper account, which would legitimately start at $100k when first created).

items.title: position_snapshot_reconciler mass-closed multiple alpaca_paper positions simultaneously with fabricated local-mark PnL, then the reverse reconciler re-adopted them ~2h later still genuinely open on the broker — the positions never actually closed
items.description: At 2026-07-07T14:15:56.749880Z, `position_snapshot_reconciler` closed several alpaca_paper trades across different symbols in the same batch (confirmed same `closed_at` timestamp on at least SPY id 3131 (125sh, pnl local-computed +$805.63), SLV id 3060 (1360sh, +$1706.80), GLD id 2868 (33.6sh, -$434.53), TLT id 2774 (231sh, -$176.77) — likely more not yet enumerated), each with `notes.pnl_source: local_compute` + `exit_price_source: local_markprice` (the '(symbol, side) confirmed absent from the exchange open-positions snapshot across two observations' closed_reason). At 2026-07-07T16:19:38-45Z (~2h5m later), the REVERSE reconciler (`_reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions`) found the exchange reporting the SAME symbols still open with matching or near-matching entry prices/sizes and re-adopted them fresh as `adopted_orphan` rows (SPY 125sh @740.67, SLV 1360sh @54.043, TLT 10sh @85.54, QQQ 16sh @720.63, IWM 9sh @298.53, IEF 8sh @94.14) — i.e. the positions were open continuously the whole time; the 14:15:56 batch-close was WRONG. Hypothesis (not yet confirmed against logs — needs journalctl/audit around 14:15:56Z): the exchange-positions read that fed the close-confirm at that tick returned an empty/degraded snapshot (Alpaca API blip, rate limit, or a client.positions() read failure that returned [] instead of None — the exact failure class RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S and the AlpacaClient/OandaClient None-on-failure hardening were built to prevent, but evidently a gap remains for `position_snapshot_reconciler`'s specific close-confirm path, distinct from the reverse reconciler's orphan-adopt path those fixes covered). CONSEQUENCE: the fabricated small per-trade PnLs from the false-close made the trades journal actively misleading during the -$67,946 root-cause investigation (BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY) — every individual number looked benign while the REAL uncapped multi-position notional exposure sat unaccounted-for on the broker the whole time. FIX (Tier-2, order_monitor.py / position_snapshot_reconciler close-confirm path — needs investigation before a specific patch is proposed): (1) find and harden whatever exchange-positions call feeds this reconciler's close-confirm for Alpaca (does it correctly distinguish 'read failed' from 'genuinely flat', matching the pattern already fixed for AlpacaClient.positions()/account_open_positions elsewhere?); (2) consider whether the 2-observation confirm this path already claims to require was actually satisfied, or whether a single degraded read slipped through; (3) audit `runtime_logs/signal_audit.jsonl` / journalctl around 2026-07-07T14:10-14:20Z for the actual read that triggered this to confirm the failure mode before patching blind.

items.resolution_criteria: Root cause of the 14:15:56Z false-close batch is confirmed from logs (not just inferred from journal state) and a fix lands so the close-confirm path can't mass-close genuinely-open positions on a degraded/empty exchange read. Regression test: a simulated empty/failed positions() read during the close-confirm path must NOT close an open trade.

updates.note: Root cause found by static analysis of src/units/accounts/clients.py::account_open_positions (the single function position_snapshot_reconciler calls for its exchange-truth read), not from logs — journalctl around 14:15:56Z was repeatedly requested via the diag relay but the issue-comment reply is capped at ~55KB and the trader logs too verbosely per tick to fit a usable window; log-level confirmation was not achieved despite 3+ attempts with progressively narrower windows. The code-level bug is nonetheless conclusive: the Alpaca branch's empty-snapshot verification used `if not bal:` to decide whether client.balance() proved the account genuinely reachable before trusting an empty positions() read as flat. A negative float is TRUTHY in Python, so alpaca_paper's ~-$67,946 balance sailed straight through as 'verified live' and the empty read was trusted as [] (flat) — exactly the mechanism this entry hypothesized. FIX LANDED (not yet pushed/deployed): commit bf0c0fe on branch claude/spy-dispatch-failures-ir2ktj changes the guard to `bal is None` (correctly means 'read failed') plus a new explicit `bal < 0` check (anomalous account state — don't trust the empty read even though it's a successful call) — both now return None (skip, no false-close) instead of falling through to return [] (flat). `bal == 0.0` now correctly returns [] where it previously also incorrectly returned None under the old truthiness bug — an intentional, low-risk behavior change (a genuinely-zero-balance account is separately blocked from new orders by the zero_balance gate). Regression tests added in tests/test_accounts_clients_open_positions.py: test_alpaca_empty_balance_negative_returns_none, test_alpaca_empty_balance_zero_returns_flat. Full suite green (20/20 in that file; 218 passed across the broader reconciler test set). Status stays 'open' until this is pushed, PR'd, merged, deployed to the live VM, and verified live.

Deployed and live-verified. PR #5901 merged (squash sha 0297fff) with operator OK in chat. `ict-git-sync` auto-deploy confirmed via `/api/diag/version`: live VM git_sha advanced from b7fcc87f (pre-merge) to 3a41031b (post-merge, includes 0297fff in ancestry, both trader + web-api services active) within ~10 minutes of merge. Closing resolved — the code-level defect is fixed and running; genuinely-open Alpaca positions can no longer be mass-closed on a negative-or-unreadable-balance empty-snapshot read. Note: while investigating a follow-on alert (QQQ close failing with 'insufficient qty available'), confirmed via a fresh /api/diag/exchange_positions pull that alpaca_paper's positions (QQQ, SPY, IWM, IEF, TLT, USO) were never actually flat/reset — they're still genuinely open on the broker, consistent with this fix's diagnosis. A separate, unrelated bug was found in the active-close path (AlpacaClient.close() doesn't cancel resting bracket legs before flattening) — tracked as a new task, not this backlog item.

items.title: spy_pullback_1h / qqq_pullback_1h (etc.) on Alpaca can size a single trade's NOTIONAL to ~100% of account equity because a thin stop-distance-to-price ratio is divided into the risk budget with no independent leverage/notional cap
items.description: While investigating BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY, found alpaca_paper trades id 3077 (142 shares SPY, ~$105,700 notional) and id 3131 (125 shares SPY, ~$92,600 notional) — both from spy_pullback_1h, both DOLLAR-RISK-BOUNDED to ~1.5% of equity at the stop (RiskManager.position_size correctly computed qty = risk_budget / (entry-stop)), but because the 1h pullback stop sits only ~0.6-0.8% away from entry on an expensive instrument (SPY ~$740-750/share), the resulting SHARE COUNT and therefore NOTIONAL is enormous relative to equity (~90-105% of the ~$100k paper account on ONE trade). position_size's only ceiling on this is the margin/buying-power cap (`available_usd * effective_leverage * _MARGIN_SAFETY_BUFFER`), which is large enough on a healthy account to permit it. Dollar-risk-at-the-tracked-stop is correctly bounded, but real-world execution risk (slippage on a 100+ share market order, a fast move that gaps through the stop, or the stop-loss leg not actually resting on the broker as assumed) scales with NOTIONAL, not with the intended risk budget — so a nominally-1.5%-risk trade can realize a loss far larger than 1.5% if the stop doesn't execute cleanly. This is a plausible contributing mechanism to how the shared alpaca_paper/alpaca_options_paper login could have gone deeply negative, though it was NOT confirmed as the literal explanation for the -$67,946 figure (see BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY — the specific trades checked netted near-breakeven; the real loss is earlier in Alpaca's history). PROPOSED FIX (Tier-3, src/units/accounts/risk.py::position_size — order-sizing path, needs operator approval before any change): add an independent max-notional-as-fraction-of-equity clamp (e.g. a `max_position_notional_pct` risk-config knob, applied after the existing risk-budget and margin-cap sizing, floor-rounded like the existing whole-unit clamp) so a thin-stop instrument can never commit near-100% of equity to one position regardless of how the risk-budget/stop-distance division works out. Applies to any account/strategy combination with a tight stop on an expensive instrument, not just alpaca_paper/spy_pullback_1h — worth an account_compat_matrix-style check across the other *_pullback_1h cells (qqq/gld/slv/tlt) once a fix direction is agreed.

Size is bounded only by the risk budget, the daily-loss budget, the margin/buying-power ceiling, and the exchange's lot size.' items.title: AlpacaClient.close() rejected with "insufficient qty available for order" because it never cancels the position's resting bracket SL/TP leg before flattening
items.description: Discovered while investigating a live '🛑 Position CLOSE failing' alert for QQQ/alpaca_paper (12 consecutive close failures, error 'insufficient qty available for order (requested: 16, available: 0)'). A fresh broker-truth pull (`/api/diag/exchange_positions`) confirmed QQQ (and SPY/IWM/IEF/TLT/USO) are genuinely open on the broker — this is NOT another instance of BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE, it's a different bug in the ACTIVE-CLOSE path. Alpaca's exact error phrasing (`available: 0` while `existing_qty` matches the full position) is the documented signature of shares already `held_for_orders` by another resting order. Every Alpaca position here was opened as a bracket order (entry + SL + TP legs placed atomically, per AlpacaClient.place()'s docstring), so the original protective stop leg is still resting on the broker holding the full qty. `AlpacaClient.close()` (src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py) just issued `DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol}` with no cancel-first step, unlike `IBClient.close()` (which explicitly cancels resting protective legs before the opposing order) and `AlpacaClient.place_protective()` (which already calls the same `_cancel_open_orders_for_symbol()` helper before re-arming, to avoid OCO stacking). Since nothing ever cancelled the stale leg, the close retried the identical failing DELETE every monitor tick indefinitely, leaving the DB row permanently open. FIX: `close()` now calls `self._cancel_open_orders_for_symbol(symbol)` before the flatten DELETE, mirroring the IB contract and reusing the helper `place_protective` already relies on. Regression tests added in tests/test_alpaca_wiring.py (`test_client_close_cancels_resting_orders_first`, `test_client_close_no_resting_orders_is_single_call`) pin that cancels happen, target the right order ids, and happen BEFORE the flatten call; existing `test_client_close_idempotent_on_404` still passes unchanged. This is a real-money order-path fix — `close_open_position` → `AlpacaClient.close()` is shared by alpaca_paper AND alpaca_live.

items.title: AlpacaClient.close() treated Alpaca's HTTP-accept as a confirmed flatten — a close accepted right after market close never actually filled, fabricating a phantom-closed row with a made-up PnL, then re-adopted 7 minutes later as a fresh orphan; the re-adopt guard had zero protection for this because it only matched setup_type='adopted_orphan'
items.description: Live incident: `_close_unattributable_orphan` (exit_coverage_resolver) closed an orphaned SLV short (1360sh @ $53.94) at 2026-07-07T20:33:45Z (4:33pm ET, just after the US equity close). `AlpacaClient.close()`'s DELETE /v2/positions/SLV returned HTTP 200 (accepted); the code treated that as confirmed-flat, fabricated a local mark-to-market PnL (-$693.60, pnl_source=local_compute), and marked the trade row closed. The position never actually flattened on the broker. 7 minutes later the reverse reconciler found SLV still fully open (same 1360sh, same $53.94 entry) and bare-adopted it as a brand-new orphan trade row — TWO DB rows now exist for the SAME broker position, the phantom-closed one carrying a fabricated realized PnL that is never corrected. Root cause: `close_open_position`'s Alpaca branch (src/units/accounts/execute.py) and AlpacaClient.close() had no fill-confirmation step, unlike IBClient.close()'s IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S contract (poll the live position, require it to actually reach flat within a bounded window before declaring success). Compounding factor: the just-shipped resting-order-cancel fix (BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-RESTING-ORDER-BLOCK, PR #5918) cancels the protective bracket BEFORE the flatten attempt, so a phantom-closed position is genuinely NAKED on the broker for the entire gap — and invisible to `_check_naked_positions` (which only scans status='open' rows), so there was zero monitoring or alerting on the exposure window either. Separately, the re-adopt flap guard (RECONCILER_READOPT_GUARD_SECONDS, BL-20260618-RECONCILE-DUP) only matched rows with setup_type='adopted_orphan' — a phantom-closed STRATEGY-ATTRIBUTED row (still carrying its original strategy's setup_type) fell through with ZERO flap protection, not even the 300s SLV incidentally got via its own setup_type. Full investigation ordered by the operator ('do a full audit of the entire Alpaca pipeline... I don't want to keep fixing one bug just to create another') — four parallel read-only audit agents covered order placement/sizing, position/balance reads, close/flatten paths, and reconciler/re-adopt-guard logic; this entry captures the three findings judged tightly coupled enough to fix together. FIX (all three parts landed in one PR): (1) AlpacaClient.close() now polls positions() after the DELETE, bounded by new ALPACA_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S (default 6.0s, <=0 restores legacy accept-is-success), mirroring IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S exactly — and deliberately reuses the exact 'not confirmed flat' retMsg substring order_monitor.py's existing IB-built cooldown/retry/consecutive-failure-alert machinery already keys on generically (by account/symbol/direction, not by exchange), so no other file needed to change for that half. (2) _recently_closed_adopted_orphan (src/runtime/order_monitor.py) widened to also match a row closed via exit_reason IN ('exchange_flat_reconciled', 'exit_coverage_no_strategy') regardless of setup_type — deliberately NOT widened to every close reason (a genuine broker-confirmed close like Bybit's reconciler_filled or a normal sl_cross/tp_cross strategy exit must never suppress a legitimate new position). (3) AlpacaClient.balance()/buying_power() truthiness bugs fixed in the same PR (see BL-20260707-ALPACA-BALANCE-TRUTHINESS below) since they surfaced in the same audit pass and are the same bug shape as the original BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE fix.

items.title: AlpacaClient.balance()/buying_power() treated a genuine $0 reading the same as 'could not read' — same truthiness bug shape as the already-fixed account_open_positions bug, one layer up
items.description: balance(): `float(acct.get('equity') or acct.get('cash'))` — a real equity=0.0 is falsy, so the code silently substitutes cash instead, even though equity is the more authoritative figure. buying_power(): `if bp > 0: return bp` inside a fallback loop over (regt_buying_power, buying_power, cash) — a genuine regt_buying_power=0.0 (fully invested / no free margin, a real and common account state) is treated identically to an unparseable value and falls through to a LESS authoritative key; if all three read non-positive, the function returns None. Coordinator.multi_account_execute reads a None buying_power() as 'could not determine' and falls back to a MORE PERMISSIVE sizing basis (total_account_usd/balance_usd x leverage) — exactly backwards: the account has genuinely zero free margin and the sizer should be MOST conservative, not fall back to a laxer basis. Verified safe to fix: Coordinator's caller already does `if _bp is not None: available_usd = _bp`, and RiskManager.position_size's margin cap correctly computes max_qty_by_margin=0 when available_usd=0.0, safely refusing the trade rather than erroring.

items.title: Order ENTRY has the same accept-vs-fill confirmation gap as the close side (BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-NOT-CONFIRMED-FLAT) — a bracket order journals status='open' the instant it's HTTP-accepted, with a fabricated entry price, no fill confirmation
items.description: `_submit_order`'s Alpaca branch (src/units/accounts/execute.py ~line 780) treats any retCode==0 (HTTP 2xx accept) from AlpacaClient.place() as success; execute_pkg then calls `_log_trade_to_journal` synchronously right after, writing status='open' with entry_price=the strategy's DECISION-TIME signal price, not a broker-confirmed fill price — no polling for an actual fill. Lower urgency than the close-side bug fixed today: Alpaca bracket orders are time_in_force:day MARKET orders, which fill almost instantly during RTH, and RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S (BL-20260622-ALPACA-SNAPSHOT-FALSECLOSE) already exists specifically as a grace period for a just-placed order that hasn't propagated to the positions() snapshot yet — i.e. the team already knew entries can sit apparently-unfilled for minutes. NOT yet confirmed whether a genuinely NEVER-filled entry (rejected post-accept, or placed outside RTH) converges to a correct state or fabricates a phantom trade with fake entry+exit+PnL for a position that never existed on the broker — this needs tracing before a fix is designed. Deliberately deferred out of today's close-side fix: the entry path is more sensitive (delaying/blocking a live entry has different risk than delaying a close) and deserves its own careful design, not a bolt-on.

updates.note: Operator directive: 'finish the fix for the entry side as well - I want full pipeline stability.' Fixed the REJECTION half only, deliberately NOT the fill-price half (scoped down from the original description after tracing the actual call path). AlpacaClient.place() (src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py) now polls the order by id after a successful POST, bounded by new ALPACA_PLACE_CONFIRM_S (default 3.0s, matching IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S; <=0 restores legacy behaviour): a terminal rejected/canceled/expired status within the window is surfaced as retCode!=0 so _submit_order raises and _log_trade_to_journal never writes a phantom open trade row for an order the broker never actually executed. Still-pending or filled at the deadline is reported as success unchanged. Deliberately did NOT attempt to capture/backfill the broker's real filled_avg_price into the journal: _submit_order's return contract is a bare str (order_id) shared byte-for-byte across bybit/IB/alpaca/oanda; threading a richer fill-price payload through it would be a materially larger, cross-exchange refactor and a separate design decision, not a bug fix — the decision-time entry price is already the documented, accepted convention for every exchange here (IB's own IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S only checks non-rejection too, never fill price), and RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S remains the existing downstream grace period for a genuinely-slow-but-good fill. Tests: test_client_place_confirms_no_rejection_when_filled, test_client_place_detects_post_accept_rejection, test_client_place_still_pending_at_deadline_is_success, test_client_place_confirm_disabled_restores_legacy_behavior (tests/test_alpaca_wiring.py) — 34/34 in that file, 323 across the broader order-management/reconciler surface.

items.title: Minor / lower-priority findings from the full Alpaca-pipeline audit — logged, not blocking
items.description: Bundle of smaller findings from the four-way parallel audit (order placement/sizing, position/balance reads, close/flatten paths, reconciler/re-adopt-guards), none individually urgent enough to block the main close-confirm fix: (1) OandaClient.close() (src/units/accounts/oanda_client.py) has the IDENTICAL accept-is-success defect as the pre-fix Alpaca close — not live-impactful today since oanda_practice is dry-run-only, but will need the same confirm-flat treatment before any OANDA account goes live. (2) No client_order_id / idempotency key on AlpacaClient.place()/place_protective() — a lost HTTP response to a timeout could leave a real accepted broker order un-journaled; low probability today since there's no retry loop in execute.py/coordinator.py to trigger a double-submit, but worth hardening. (3) The naked-position re-arm paths (_rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery, _check_broker_naked_equity_positions in order_monitor.py) size the re-armed OCO from trades.position_size (the journal column) rather than a fresh broker-side qty read — suspected staleness risk, not confirmed as a live bug, needs a follow-up trace of whether position_size reliably stays broker-truth-synced across partial fills/closes. (4) AlpacaClient.place_protective() duplicates whole_unit_qty's rounding logic inline instead of calling the shared helper place() already uses — cosmetic DRY violation, functionally identical today but a latent drift risk if the rounding rule ever changes. (5) _PENDING_ORPHAN_NOSTRAT_CLOSE (order_monitor.py) is never popped on the 'absent' (closed via disappear-confirm) branch, only the 'recoverable' branch — an unbounded but harmless in-process dict leak (trade ids are never reused). (6) _recover_orphan_order_package searches order packages of ANY status (not just open) for a symbol/direction/entry-price(+-2%) match — theoretical risk of resurrecting an already-closed, unrelated order package on a coincidental price match; not observed live, worth a defensive exclusion (e.g. skip packages whose linked trade closed via exit_coverage_no_strategy/exchange_flat_reconciled within the readopt-guard window) as a follow-up.

items.title: Alpaca close() still races share-release on a re-arming OCO (QQQ #3269) — needs qty_available-gated flatten, not blind retry
items.description: MECHANISM: the position's protective OCO stop-sell leg (stop 708.38, price hovering ~708.7) reserves all 16 shares as held_for_orders. close() cancels the leg + retries the DELETE within a 6s window, but Alpaca's cancel->qty_available release appears to take longer than 6s AND/OR the naked-autoprotect sweep re-arms a fresh OCO on an intervening monitor tick, so every close attempt re-hits available:0. This is a real close-path bug that could also strand a REAL alpaca_live position on a slow cancel, not just this paper orphan. CORRECT FIX (deterministic, not another blind retry): after the cancel pre-pass, POLL the position's qty_available (raw /v2/positions/{sym} field, add to AlpacaClient.positions() or a helper) until it == qty before issuing the DELETE, with a longer bound; and/or make the close a persistent 'closing' latch that suppresses the naked re-arm for that (account,symbol) until confirmed flat (not just the same-tick guard). NEEDS order/qty-level broker visibility — consider adding /api/diag/exchange_orders?account_id (read-only, mirrors exchange_positions) to SEE what holds the shares before the next attempt. LOW URGENCY: QQQ is alpaca_paper (is_demo, no real capital) — the live cost is the 'won't flatten' banner/Telegram noise, bounded to every-Nth-failure. Deprioritized behind real-money work per operator.

items.description: Once INV-6 reports total>0 on the live VM, run scripts/ops/repair_malformed_notes.py --apply (Tier-2 DB write) to rewrite the legacy invalid-JSON blobs into valid envelopes (salvaging intact closed_at). items.resolution_note: RESOLVED. The nonfinite-aware dry-run (issue #6058) found 1085 json_valid=0 rows and classified ALL of them as TRUNCATED (49 trades.notes + 1036 order_packages.signal_logic; nonfinite=0) — i.e. the original char-slice footgun (BL-20260618 class), whose write-side was already eliminated by the dump_capped migration. HONESTY NOTE: an interim hypothesis that the 1036 signal_logic rows were NaN/Infinity serialization was DISPROVED by the classifier (json.loads accepts NaN, so a complete-but-nonfinite blob would parse; all 1085 fail to parse → truncation, confirmed by the mid-string tails). PR #6055 (json_notes.sanitize_nonfinite) still shipped as a valid LATENT-bug fix — dump_capped genuinely must never emit NaN/Infinity — but it was NOT the cause of this population. The one-shot repair (issue #6059, repair_malformed_notes.py --apply, Tier-2 DB writeback) rewrote all 1085 rows into valid JSON (salvage envelope preserving the raw under _original_truncated + recovering closed_at on the trades.notes rows that unblock closed_flat_invariant), verified by the script's post-commit re-scan: 'applied; remaining malformed rows = 0'. INV-6 (ict-db-integrity, hourly at :28, checks trades.notes) will independently re-confirm total=0 on its next run. Repair dispatched via the repair-malformed-notes system-action (added earlier this session).

Locate the reset script (scripts/ops around reset_daily_risk_state) + its system-action/workflow wiring and remove the sqlite3-CLI dependency.

items.source: pairs SOLUSDT/BNBUSDT garbage-order investigation. A live BNBUSDT pairs leg was placed with SL=2x entry / TP=0.5x entry (an exploded/collapsed bracket the venue would reject). Root cause traced to risk_spread ~= 5.4 in LOG-spread units (implausibly large) fed into leg_protective_levels.
items.title: Pairs sleeve: unstable rolling OLS beta on a 15-bar lookback blows up risk_spread -> exploded SL/TP (clamp #6549 band-aids the symptom, not the beta)
items.description: The pairs executor sizes each leg off risk_spread = stop_z * std(log-spread), where the log-spread = log(price_a) - beta*log(price_b) and beta is a rolling OLS hedge ratio. On a SHORT (15-bar) lookback the OLS beta is numerically unstable (a few outlier bars swing it far from 1.0), which inflates the spread std and drives risk_spread to implausible values (~5.4 in log units => a leg backstop of e^5.4 ~ 220x). SYMPTOM FIXED (#6549, src/units/strategies/pairs_sizing.py::leg_protective_levels): the log-move is now clamped to [log(1.02), log(2.0)] so a degenerate risk_spread can never emit an exploded/collapsed bracket the venue rejects — the garbage BNBUSDT order can't recur. The clamp is defensive-in-depth and correct, but it masks rather than fixes the BETA estimation: a clamped-but-wrong risk_spread still mis-sizes the notionals (pair_notionals divides risk_budget by risk_spread), so the sleeve's risk-per-trade is still off when beta is unstable. Pairs is currently execution: shadow on bybit_1 (demoted #6552 after the live-placement break), so this is NOT live-money-at-risk today. REAL FIX (Tier-3, backtest-gated, NOT enacted here): stabilize the hedge-ratio/spread estimation before it reaches sizing — e.g. a longer/robust beta lookback, ridge/Kalman beta, winsorized spread std, or an explicit sanity guard that rejects a pair-tick when |beta| or risk_spread falls outside a plausible band (the honest 'skip this tick' rather than size on garbage). Validate on the pairs backtest harness before re-flipping any pair to live. Cross-ref: pairs SL/TP clamp #6549, pairs shadow demotion #6552, /api/bot/pairs/soak (M22 D2 soak surface).
items.trigger_condition: Next pairs-sleeve work session, OR before any pair is re-flipped from execution: shadow to live.
items.resolution_criteria: Pairs beta/spread estimation is stabilized (robust/longer-lookback beta or a sanity guard that skips a tick with an implausible beta/risk_spread) and validated on the pairs backtest harness; risk_spread stays in a plausible band across the soak; the #6549 clamp becomes a never-triggered backstop rather than a load-bearing fix.

items.title: /dev/null unwritable on live VM breaks pull_and_deploy git-fetch (deploy-tooling hygiene)
items.description: Root cause to confirm: /dev/null on ict-bot-arm likely got replaced by a regular file or chmod'd off 0666 (crw-rw-rw-). Fix is a privileged one-liner `sudo chmod 666 /dev/null` (or recreate: `sudo rm -f /dev/null && sudo mknod /dev/null c 1 3 && sudo chmod 666 /dev/null`), or a VM reboot (devtmpfs recreates /dev). There is no autonomous arbitrary-command wire to the LIVE VM (system-actions is a fixed allowlist; trainer-vm-diag is trainer-only), so this needs either an operator chmod, a new one-shot labelled workflow that SSHes the chmod (Tier-2), or a reboot-vm system-action (Tier-2). Not urgent while git-sync keeps the code current + the trader is healthy, but it must be fixed before a code deploy that requires a restart-with-fetch and to remove the latent risk to /dev/null-redirecting processes (incl. the liveness watchdog's restart path).

items.title: btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1 OOM-thrashes into D-state and wedges the WHOLE trainer ~24h, evading the per-manifest timeout + OOM-kill
items.detail: On 2026-07-19 the trainer was found with run_training_cycle.sh stuck ~24.8h on ml/configs/btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1.yaml: the training python (working set ~4.2-4.8GB RSS) sat in State D (uninterruptible disk-sleep), 0% CPU, wchan=mem_cgroup_handle_over_high. No manifest trained since Jul 18 01:24 (journal) -> ALL trainer work (other manifests, drift-retrain, any gate-check I tried to run) was blocked for a day; every fc-pcv gate-check 'hang' that night was this process starving the 6GB box. ROOT CAUSE: the flow head's ~4.8GB working set sits in the GAP between the unit's MemoryHigh=3G (soft -> kernel keeps reclaiming, pushing pages to the MemorySwapMax=512M swap and faulting them back = perpetual swap-thrash, D-state) and MemoryMax=5G (hard -> never reached at 4.8G RSS, so the kernel OOM-killer never fires). The existing per-manifest `timeout --kill-after=30s 1800s` in run_training_cycle.sh CANNOT reap it because SIGTERM/SIGKILL do not land on a process in uninterruptible D-state until it leaves the mem-cgroup-over-high reclaim path -> the cycle stays blocked at that manifest and the OOM-quarantine (trainer_manifest_health, BL-20260717) never records a timeout so it never quarantines. Cleared manually via pkill -9 (freed 4.4GB); it re-wedged on the same manifest the next cycle -> recurs every cycle.
items.fix: Operator-domain memory tuning (these caps were deliberately iterated - MemoryHigh 4G->3G, MemorySwapMax 512M - so pick values with care). Options, not-yet-applied: (a) MemorySwapMax=0 on ict-trainer.service + ict-trainer-catchup.service (deny cgroup swap) so an over-MemoryHigh manifest can't swap-thrash in D-state - it runs in RAM (throttled) or hits MemoryMax and OOM-kills cleanly (OOMPolicy=continue + run_training_cycle.sh already handle a killed subprocess); risk: a legit manifest relying on the 512M cushion would OOM-kill instead. (b) Lower MemoryMax below the flow head's ~4.8G peak (e.g. 4G) so it OOM-kills; risk: kills other 4-5G-peak manifests too. (c) Memory-bound the 5m flow head specifically (streaming/subsample its market_features load; the unit comment already flags a 'market_features streaming refactor' as the real peak-RSS fix) or exclude it from the cycle until bounded. (d) Add an external D-state-watchdog: a trainer process in State D at 0% CPU for >N min = wedged -> the watchdog lowers memory pressure (e.g. `systemctl set-property ... MemorySwapMax=0`) or pkills it so the cycle's timeout can then proceed. Recommend (a)+(c). NOT applied autonomously - memory-policy change on the running trainer, operator to choose values.

But HIGH severity operationally: one heavy manifest silently blocks the ENTIRE training center for ~24h/cycle - no new heads train, no drift-retrain, gate-checks can't run. Recurs every ict-trainer.timer fire. Backward-impact: any 'trainer looks stuck / no new models' observation since ~2026-07-18 01:24 traces here. Once fixed, re-run whatever training/gate-checks were starved (incl. the fc-pcv oos_edge, already done in a manually-cleared window: oos_edge PASS +0.282).

items.title: FALSE ALARM (corrected same day): 'GitHub Actions outage' was actually an unmergeable (dirty) PR — pull_request workflows silently never run when the merge ref cannot be built
items.detail: ORIGINAL (WRONG) diagnosis: pushes/PR events after ~07:30Z produced zero check runs, so a GitHub-side push/pull_request webhook outage was presumed. REAL root cause (operator pushed back — 'no way it's been down 5h' — forcing proper investigation): the PR branch had a MERGE CONFLICT with main (squash-merge of #7042 vs the branch's original commits diverged in ml/promotion/live_parity.py + tests/ml/test_live_parity.py), so mergeable_state was 'dirty'. GitHub builds pull_request-event workflow runs against the MERGE REF; when the merge ref cannot be built, the workflows are silently skipped — zero check runs, indistinguishable at a glance from an Actions outage. Push-event workflows also only trigger on main in this repo, so branch pushes never fire CI regardless. Fixed by merging origin/main into the branch (conflicts resolved); CI fired instantly on the push, all 26 checks green. LESSON (the durable part): before suspecting an Actions outage, check the PR's mergeable_state — 'dirty' means no merge ref, means no pull_request CI; another session's PRs running CI at the same time is the fastest disproof of an outage.

items.title: Netted-position bracket fires close ONLY the newest journal row — older rows go phantom-open, then get mis-resolved with other trades' closed-pnl records / stale mark prices (root-caused; exchange behaved correctly)
items.detail: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-20 (forensics: trainer relay #7122 full-notes dump + 1h candles #7118/#7117). SUPERSEDES the earlier 'no effective bracket / stop-enforcement failure' framing — the exchange behaved CORRECTLY throughout. Mechanism: on Bybit one-way mode the netted (multi-strategy) position carries ONE position-level tpsl — each new same-symbol open REPLACES it (execute.py attaches stopLoss/takeProfit on every non-reduce Market order). When that bracket fires (Full mode) the ENTIRE position flattens, but the journal/reconciler closes only the NEWEST trade row; older rows stay phantom-'open'. Jun 21-23 bybit_2 BTCUSDT timeline (all verified): TP fire 06-22 11:37 @64729 (journal closed only 2768; 2765's 0.001 share actually exited HERE at a PROFIT), SL fire 06-22 21:23 @64250 (closed only 2797/2769; 2783's real exit, ~-0.9R), SL fire 06-23 06:21 @62724 (closed only 2798/2799). The phantom rows were later mis-resolved: (a) closed-pnl matcher stamped OTHER trades' broker records byte-identically — 2765<-2799 (-1.63903789/62724.0, REAL MONEY), 2764<-2769 (-3350.54/64255.9), 2796<-2798 (-828.847/62725.0); (b) reconcile_orphan_history (Jun 25 06:14) stamped 2757/2762/2770 with local_markprice 62402.2 (Jun-23+ price). The catastrophic per-trade R reads (-7..-14R) that drove the ict_scalp 'lets losses run' narrative are 100% measurement artifact; real losses were bracket-bounded. TWO REAL DEFECTS: (1) [attribution, Tier-1/2] the reconciler's 'position flat' close must cascade to ALL open journal rows on (account,symbol,direction) at that fire, qty-prorating the closed-pnl record, instead of closing only the row it was checking — and the closed-pnl matcher must refuse/flag a record whose close flattened a position that had >1 open journal row (netted_ambiguous), never stamp it verbatim onto one row. (2) [protection semantics, Tier-3] under Full-mode tpsl the NEWEST trade's bracket governs every strategy's share — older trades ride geometry they never chose. Candidate fix: tpslMode=Partial with qty-scoped brackets per order (needs Bybit API validation), or accept position-level semantics and make the journal model it honestly. Also explains part of BL-20260713-BYBIT2-PNL-UNDERRECORD and generalizes BL-20260720-PAPER-PNL-CROSSWRITE (NOT paper-only: 2765 is real money). Analytics impact: per-trade R for netted bybit windows is unreliable until (1) lands + a historical repair pass re-attributes the Jun 21-23 rows. items.title: Merge-serialization protocol lapsed under load: 3 claim-less merges raced 'behind' 3x in one day while claimed merges raced 0x — the protocol needs per-merge framing + a mechanical nudge
items.detail: 2026-07-20 (operator flagged it: 'are we using the merge queue and message board correctly? we added those specifically to prevent this'). Self-audit of board #6927: on 07-19 every merge by this session carried MERGE SLOT CLAIM/RELEASE comments and zero races occurred. On 07-20 the same session merged/attempted #7082, #7155, #7167 WITHOUT claiming first and hit mergeable_state 'behind' THREE times (each costing a branch refresh + a full ~10-min CI rerun + a squash-vs-original conflict in one case); the two merges where a claim WAS posted (reactively) merged cleanly first try. Root causes: (1) the claim step lives in session memory, and under time pressure (racing an approved promotion chain) it was skipped exactly when the repo was busiest; (2) the session also did not READ the board before merging, so even a counterpart's claim would have been missed; (3) docs/claude/session-board.json (the merge-queue file) went untouched all day — the two mechanisms (file queue + live board) have drifted, with the 07-19 note declaring the live board 'the real-time signal', leaving the file's role unclear. PROPOSED FIXES for a review session: (a) reword session-coordination SKILL.md + the SessionStart clause-0 text to frame the claim as a PER-MERGE precondition ('before every merge_pull_request call: read board tail, post CLAIM, merge, post RELEASE'), not a session-start ritual; (b) clarify or retire session-board.json's merge_slot in favor of the board comments (one source of truth); (c) optional mechanical nudge: a tiny helper script sessions are told to run (checks the newest CLAIM/RELEASE comment pair and refuses to proceed on someone else's open claim) — cheap, no branch-protection change. Evidence: board comments 5026296972 (reactive claim #7167), 5025958114 (reactive claim #7155), merge failures at 16:11Z/18:52Z/19:11Z-19:19Z in the session log.

updates.note: Proposed fixes (skill-doc reword, session-board.json clarification, mechanical-nudge helper) not shipped this window. No merges were performed by this review session (health-review makes no code changes needing a merge), so no fresh evidence either way on protocol adherence.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

Shipped proposed fixes (a)+(b): reworded session-coordination/SKILL.md § 2 to frame the merge claim as a PER-MERGE precondition on the merge_pull_request call ('read board tail -> post 🔒 MERGE SLOT CLAIM comment -> sync -> merge on green -> 🔓 RELEASE'), not a session-start ritual, and made the LIVE BOARD COMMENT (#6927) the authoritative claim with session-board.json::merge_slot demoted to a durable mirror (one source of truth) — updated the two-surfaces preamble, § 2 steps, the session-board.json _doc + merge_slot schema, and coordination-board.md's 'complements not replaces' bullet to match. Fix (c) (a mechanical nudge helper script) intentionally deferred as optional — the reframe + one-source-of-truth addresses root causes (1)+(2)+(3) without new tooling; re-log if the lapse recurs after the reword.

items.title: trainer-vm-diag cmd extractor executes markdown-fenced bodies via backtick command substitution
items.detail: A trainer-vm-diag-request issue whose cmd: block is wrapped in markdown ``` fences is passed to bash WITH the backticks intact — triple-backtick acts as nested command substitution, so the request half-executes and stray output is itself executed as a command (issues #7208/#7209: pgrep's PID line ran as a command, '275311: command not found'). The documented `cmd: |` YAML-block form works (#7211). Fix: in .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml's extractor, strip leading/trailing ``` fence lines from cmd_raw (the vm-diag-snapshot relay may share the pattern — check both), or reject fenced bodies with a loud comment instead of executing them mangled. Repro: any fenced cmd body.

updates.note: Fix (strip/reject markdown fences in the cmd extractor) not shipped this window; this session's own trainer-vm-diag dispatch used a clean `cmd: |` block (no fences), so it did not hit the bug, but the extractor is unchanged.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

RESOLVED — the trainer-vm-diag.yml cmd extractor now strips markdown code-fence lines (```/```lang) from the cmd body via a `found && /^[[:space:]]*```/{ next }` awk rule, so a fenced cmd body no longer leaks the fence into bash (an un-stripped ```bash line ran as command ``` + backticks got command-substituted). Verified: valid YAML.

items.title: RESOLVED: pytest-run CI test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run — real glob-order bug in dataset_unchanged_check.py, not test flakiness
items.detail: CI run https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/actions/runs/29948446729/job/89019758539 (PR #7381, a docs/backlog/report-only /system-review PR) failed this ONE test out of 7976 passed/8 skipped: assert duc.decide(...) == 'SKIP' got 'TRAIN'. The test sets a manifest+dataset mtime to 1 day old (_set_old default 86400s) and a registry run_at 0.5 days old (12h) -- a 12h margin that should not be flaky by itself. Confirmed NOT caused by this PR: scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py and tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py are both unchanged since PR #7082 (well before this branch's merge-base 2a21ed5), and running just this test file in isolation (pytest tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py -k test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run) PASSES cleanly. This strongly suggests an order-dependent interaction with another test earlier in the ~8000-test full-suite run (e.g. a time.time()/os.utime patch or monkeypatch that leaks past its own test's teardown) -- the same class of issue the pytest-run workflow's own comments cite as the 2026-05-28 time-bomb-test incident. Needs a full local repro of the full test suite (matching CI exactly, ~6-7 min) with a bisection pass to find the offending earlier test, then either fix its teardown or make this test's time reference injectable/mockable so it can't be perturbed by global state. ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED same session: scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py::decide() called d.get("model_id") on every glob-matched registry JSON file OUTSIDE the try/except that only guarded json.load() -- the test fixture's own "not-an-entry.json" sibling artifact (a JSON list, not a dict) crashes that .get() call with AttributeError when glob.glob() happens to enumerate it before the real dict entry (glob order is filesystem-dependent, not sorted). The AttributeError propagated to the function-level fail-open (except Exception: return "TRAIN"), silently flipping the expected SKIP to TRAIN. Confirmed by forcing both glob orderings locally with a monkeypatch -- reproduces 100% of the time when the non-dict sibling glob-sorts first, regardless of environment. Fixed with a one-line isinstance(d, dict) guard (commit pending on PR #7381) + a new regression test (test_skip_regardless_of_glob_order_with_non_dict_sibling) that forces both orderings explicitly so it can never again depend on ambient filesystem behavior. Not a flake, not order-dependent test pollution from another test -- a real latent bug in production code that happened to only manifest under GitHub Actions runner's particular directory-entry order. (Cross-reference: an independent concurrent session, ml-strategies-workplan-nm3xnx, also hit this exact bug on PR #7379 and logged it as BL-20260722-DATASET-UNCHANGED-CHECK-FLAKE, now marked resolved pointing back here.)

items.recommended_action: Done -- fixed + regression-tested in the same PR that surfaced it.

items.title: CI flake: test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run fail-opens to TRAIN
items.detail: tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py::TestDecide::test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run intermittently fails 'assert TRAIN == SKIP' in CI (seen on PR #7379 run 29948106302, HeadSHA c0235198). The setup is deterministic (dataset/manifest mtime 24h old vs registry run_at 12h old, a 12h margin) and reproduces as SKIP locally, so the TRAIN can only come from decide()'s bare-except fail-open (scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py:77) — i.e. TrainingManifest.from_yaml/path_under raised in CI. The fail-open MASKS the real intermittent exception. Diagnose: replace the bare-except with logging of the exception type, or harden the test to assert no fail-open occurred (distinguish real SKIP from fail-open TRAIN). Not dangerous in prod (fail-open TRAIN = one unnecessary retrain) but it flakes CI and hides an intermittent manifest-load error. Introduced with MB-20260720-FCPCV-RETRAIN-NOOP.

Fixed with an isinstance(d, dict) guard + a regression test that forces both glob orderings explicitly (PR #7381, commit 682efda). See BL-20260722-PYTESTRUN-DATASETCHECK-FLAKE for the full writeup.

items.opened_by: claude (session continuing /system-review 2026-07-22, investigating operator-reported XRPUSDT trade 3577 SL-notification-spam + stale-dashboard report)
items.source: Root-cause investigation of the operator XRP report: diag pull of order_packages showed pkg-395c72c733074358 (linked trade 3577, xrp_pullback_2h, bybit_2 real money) had sl=1.1116 vs trades.stop_loss=1.0655 (the original entry-time stop), with order_packages.updated_at essentially continuous (stamped within the same minute as the diag query, 5 days after entry). Traced the mechanism: htf_pullback_trend_2h.py::monitor() (and trend_donchian.py::monitor, which claims an identical contract) computes current_price = candles_df['close'].iloc[-1] and ext = window['high'].max() off whatever candles_df the ohlcv_fetcher returns; src/runtime/market_data.py::fetch_candles never drops the exchange-returned forming/incomplete final candle. On Bybit, fetch_ohlcv's last row is the live, continuously-updating current-period candle, so current_price/ext (and therefore the ATR trail candidate = ext - trail_mult*atr) update on every tick a live price makes even a fractional new high, not just on bar close. Each such tick that clears 'candidate > sl' triggers order_monitor.py's modify branch: an exchange amend call + (pre-fix) an unconditional Telegram ping, producing the observed near-continuous stream of SL moves the operator correctly perceived as noise (the SL LOOKED static because none of these micro-moves were individually meaningful).
items.title: [order-monitor][strategy] Pullback-family trail (htf_pullback_trend_2h / trend_donchian monitor()) reacts to the live/forming candle instead of closed-bar-only, causing far more exchange SL amends than intended — proposed Tier-2 fix, needs operator sign-off
items.description: Mitigated (shipped, Tier-1/2, no order-path behavior change) this session: order_monitor.py's modify branch now drops any sl/tp key whose new value is not >0.05% different from the package's current value BEFORE any exchange call, DB write, or notification (_MEANINGFUL_MODIFY_REL_TOL gate) — this kills the notification spam and the pure float-noise exchange amends. trades.stop_loss/take_profit_1 are now also synced on every successful modify so the dashboard/API no longer goes stale after the first trail move (both landed together, tests added: test_modify_skips_immaterial_change_no_exchange_call_no_db_write, test_modify_still_fires_on_meaningful_change, test_modify_syncs_trades_stop_loss_after_success in tests/test_s030_pr4_exchange_modify_close.py). Also fixed in the same pass: _fire_trade_opened_event / _fire_trade_updated_event in database.py SELECTed qty/sl/tp — none of which exist on trades (real columns: position_size/stop_loss/take_profit_1) — so TRADE_OPENED push notifications have silently never fired (swallowed by insert_trade's bare except); fixed to use the real column names. NOT fixed (deeper root cause, proposed only): the trail computation itself should arguably use only CLOSED bars (drop candles_df's last row when it is the forming candle) so the trail advances once per bar close like the strategy's own trail_decay_arm_r/trail_decay_tight_mult meta fields imply it was designed to, rather than continuously intrabar. This changes real order-routing cadence (fewer, larger, discrete SL amends instead of many tiny ones) for every strategy sharing this monitor() shape, not just xrp_pullback_2h — meaningful blast radius (any donchian/pullback-family leg). Proposed exact change: in fetch_candles or the ohlcv_fetcher closure in src/main.py::_build_monitor_ohlcv_fetcher, drop the last row when its timestamp indicates the bar has not yet closed (bar_start + timeframe_seconds > now), mirroring the 'closed bars only' principle already codified for ML scorers this session (docs/research/RESEARCH-RIGOR-STANDARD.md). Also worth checking whether _send_modify_to_exchange rate-limits/dedupes on its own — if Bybit's API is still being hit at a materially reduced but still-elevated cadence post-gate, that's worth knowing before deciding whether the closed-bar fix is urgent or can wait. NOT YET INVESTIGATED this session: the operator's separately-reported 'partial close' bookkeeping question on trade 3577 (does a partial close correctly reduce position_size in place, or should it produce a second row?) — flagged for a follow-up, not fabricated an answer to here.
