items.resolution: CLOSED per explicit operator decision (2026-07-23, in chat): the operator does not mind the strategy trailing off the live/forming candle as its designed behavior -- the notification/exchange-amend SPAM was the actual problem, and that is already fixed (the _MEANINGFUL_MODIFY_REL_TOL noise gate in order_monitor.py, shipped/deployed in PR #7402). The closed-bars-only trail change proposed here is NOT being pursued. items.opened_by: claude (session continuing ML/strategies + platform-layering workplan, M0a/M0b architecture pass)
items.source: While standing up the M0a import-linter layer guard I initially reported to the operator (Telegram ping #7456 + chat) that src/units/strategies/vwap.py and src/units/strategies/_base.py 'import execution (strategy-purity violations)'. On verification BOTH direct-import claims were FALSE POSITIVES from a naive grep: vwap.py:976 is a docstring comment that merely NAMES order_monitor.py (not an import), and _base.py:48 is `from src.core.order_contract import OrderPackage` inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block (a type-only import of the CONTRACT type, erased at runtime, and order_contract is the contract seam not Execution). Corrected with the operator. However an authoritative import-linter check (temp forbidden contract on src.units.strategies.vwap vs {units.accounts.risk, units.accounts.execute, exchange}) surfaced a REAL TRANSITIVE coupling: src.units.strategies.vwap -> src.units.db.database (vwap.py:679) -> src.runtime.local_pnl (database.py:841) -> {src.units.accounts.risk (local_pnl.py:151) -> src.core.coordinator -> src.units.accounts.execute; and src.runtime.market_data -> src.exchange.ib_connector/oanda_connector}. The load-bearing seam is database.py:841 importing runtime.local_pnl — that single edge is what drags the entire persistence layer (and therefore every strategy that persists) up into Execution.
items.title: [architecture][M0b] units.db.database imports runtime.local_pnl (database.py:841), transitively coupling the DB/persistence layer — and every strategy that touches it (e.g. vwap) — up into Execution (risk/coordinator/execute + exchange connectors). Correction of an earlier false-positive 'vwap/_base import execution' report: the direct imports were a comment + a TYPE_CHECKING contract import; the real issue is this transitive DB-layer edge.
items.description: Genuine layer-boundary finding for the M0b incremental-drain migration (ROADMAP_MACRO.md §1). ROOT EDGE: src/units/db/database.py line ~841 does `from src.runtime.local_pnl import ...` (a PnL compute helper). runtime.local_pnl in turn imports units.accounts.risk (→ core.coordinator → units.accounts.execute) and runtime.market_data (→ exchange.*_connector). So the persistence layer, which strategies legitimately need for reads, is not itself layer-clean — it reaches into Execution. CONSEQUENCE: no strategy module that imports units.db.database can be added to the import-linter forbidden-vs-Execution contracts yet (vwap, and any strategy sharing that persistence access, would fail transitively even though its own code is pure). This is exactly the kind of edge the M0b drain exists to cut, one seam at a time, without touching live behavior. PROPOSED FIX (non-behavioral refactor, Tier-1/2, NOT done here): move the local_pnl compute helper that database.py needs behind an inversion — either (a) database.py should not import a runtime/Execution PnL helper at all (invert the dependency so local_pnl imports the DB read fn, or pass the computed value in), or (b) extract the pure part of local_pnl that database.py uses into a Signals/Platform-level helper with no risk/exchange imports. Then database.py's only upward reach disappears and vwap (+ siblings) can be locked into the layer guard. VERIFY with `lint-imports` before/after (the temp contract above is the repro). Blast radius must be measured: database.py is load-bearing on the live path, so the refactor ships behind the normal test suite + a green layer-guard, and the equivalence of the moved helper is asserted. This is tracked as an M0b drain candidate, not an urgent bug — nothing is broken at runtime; it is an architecture-debt seam that blocks widening the enforced contract.
items.trigger_condition: Picked up as an M0b incremental-drain unit (ROADMAP_MACRO §1), OR when someone next tries to add a units.db.database-importing strategy to the .importlinter forbidden-Execution contracts and it fails transitively.
items.resolution_criteria: database.py no longer imports runtime.local_pnl (or any Execution/risk/exchange module, directly or transitively); `lint-imports` with a forbidden contract on src.units.strategies.vwap vs {units.accounts.risk, units.accounts.execute, exchange} passes; the vwap purity contract is added to .importlinter and stays green; the change is behavior-preserving (test suite green, no order-path diff).

items.source: The platform-layering plan flagged a 'violation #2': the live intent/coordination layer (src/runtime/intents.py, src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py) 'hardcodes the strategy roster' — proposed fix: decouple it. Investigated before implementing (operator granted option (a): merge behavior-preserving live-path refactors autonomously; operator also asked for disagreement where warranted).
items.title: [architecture][assessment] 'violation #2' (decouple hardcoded roster from live intents.py / intent_multiplexer.py) is largely a MISDIAGNOSIS — DECLINED, with the one safe sub-fix shipped
items.description:
Assessment (disagreeing with the 'decouple the roster' framing, evidence below):
(1) intents.DEFAULT_PRIORITIES is NOT an architecture violation. It is a legitimate CENTRAL conflict-arbitration policy table (which strategy wins when two want the same symbol) — a Platform/coordination concern that is correctly centralized (a strategy self-declaring its own priority would be worse: every strategy claims top priority). Its values are Tier-3 order-routing decisions wrapped in load-bearing safety comments (e.g. '0 = untested-roster floor so a wiring slip can't override the established roster'; 'tune upward only with operator approval after a backtest'). Moving it to config would relocate Tier-3 data and strip that safety context for no behavioral gain.
(2) The two builder rosters are NOT a dup-that-drifted. pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS (16 keys) is a strict SUBSET of intent_multiplexer._default_intent_builders (54 keys, the authoritative live intent-layer roster, MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER default on). pipeline.monitor_unit_for already looks up the legacy dict first then FALLS BACK to the superset (_resolve_builders) for the sleeves the legacy dict omits — a fallback added to fix a naked-orphan money-loss bug (BL-20260615-MGCNAKED). Deduping/refactoring them is a Tier-3-adjacent order-path change with real risk (that fallback exists for a money-loss reason) and ~zero architectural benefit. Under the default config the 54-superset drives everything, so there is no latent gap.
SHIPPED (the one genuinely-safe, valuable fix from this review): corrected the stale/misleading 'Mirrors pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS to keep the rosters in sync' docstring on _default_intent_builders to accurately describe the legacy-subset / authoritative-superset + fallback relationship (PR #7460) — that comment would otherwise lead a future session to wrongly trim the superset and reintroduce the naked-orphan bug (field beats comment).
NOT DONE (declined): the broad 'decouple the hardcoded roster' refactor. Recommend leaving both the priority table and the two builder registries as-is. If the operator still wants the roster made config-driven for the layering story, the correct precedent is how SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS was already made config-driven (supported_symbols() unions accounts.yaml) — but that would move Tier-3 priority VALUES + their safety documentation into YAML, so it is a Tier-3 change needing explicit operator approval + a backtest that the arbitration outcomes are unchanged, not an autonomous refactor.
items.trigger_condition: Operator revisits the 'decouple the roster' idea, OR a future session proposes deduping the two builder rosters / moving DEFAULT_PRIORITIES to config — read this assessment first.
items.resolution_criteria: Operator either (a) accepts the disagreement (leave the roster/priority centralization as-is; this item closes as 'assessed, declined, comment fixed'), or (b) explicitly directs the config-driven priority migration as a Tier-3 change with a backtest gate.
items.resolution: CLOSED per explicit operator decision (2026-07-23, in chat: 'ok, i'll take your rec on violation 2'). The operator ACCEPTED the recommendation: the 'decouple the hardcoded roster' change is a misdiagnosis and is NOT being pursued. DEFAULT_PRIORITIES stays as the central Tier-3 conflict-arbitration policy table; the two builder rosters stay as legacy-subset + authoritative-superset with the existing fallback. The one safe sub-fix (the stale 'keep the rosters in sync' comment) shipped in PR #7460. No config-driven priority migration will be done; if that is ever revisited it is a Tier-3 change requiring a backtest gate that arbitration outcomes are unchanged.

items.source: The M28 valuation-snapshot producer workflow (macro-valuation-snapshot.yml) tried to direct-push its appended comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl to main and was declined with GH006 'Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main - 9 of 9 required status checks are expected' (run 30017310010). Confirmed general: every commit on main is a squash-merged PR, there are ZERO bot direct-pushes on main. This is the SAME wall as BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE (gpu-burst spend-ledger). So it is a GENERAL gap: no GitHub-hosted workflow in this repo can autonomously land committed data on protected main.
items.title: No autonomous workflow path to commit data to protected main (blocks valuation-snapshot producer AND gpu-burst spend ledger)
items.description: main is branch-protected with 9 required status checks and no Actions-bot push-allowance, so a workflow's `git push HEAD:main` is rejected outright (GH006). A GITHUB_TOKEN-opened PR does NOT trigger the on:pull_request required checks (recursive-trigger suppression), so an auto-merge PR from the default token stalls forever. Net: two workflows are affected today - (1) gpu-burst-train's spend-ledger append (BL-20260706, the $10 budget-gate input silently under-counts), and (2) the M28 valuation-snapshot producer. INTERIM WORKAROUND SHIPPED for the valuation producer (this session): it now accrues its append-only log on the UNPROTECTED data branch `automation/valuation-snapshots` (restore-then-append-then-force-push), which the off-VM M28 P4 gate reads via `git show origin/automation/valuation-snapshots:comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl`. That unblocks the P4 research consumer with zero operator dependency; the live macro-thesis sleeve is observe-only (no order path) so deferring the main path strands no live capability. DURABLE FIX (operator/admin-gated, resolves BOTH workflows): choose one of - (a) add a branch-protection push-allowance / bypass scoped to the github-actions[bot] for commits touching only comms/** data files (repo Settings -> branch protection -> allow specified actors to bypass required checks, or a ruleset bypass), so a data-only workflow can direct-push; or (b) provision a write-scoped PAT secret (contents+pull-requests write, on the bypass list) so a workflow can open an auto-merging PR whose required checks actually trigger. (a) is the least-moving-parts option and needs no daily PR/CI. Once (a) or (b) is in place, repoint macro-valuation-snapshot.yml back at main (the reader-fallback in valuation_store.py already prefers comms/macro on main, so the live sleeve lights up automatically) and fix gpu-burst-train.yml the same way.
items.tier: Tier 1 (CI workflow + one operator/admin action: branch-protection setting OR a PAT secret value).
items.trigger_condition: Next CI/infra-touching session, OR when the live macro-thesis sleeve is about to go order-affecting (then the snapshots MUST be on main), OR the next /health-review. Pairs with BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE - fix both together.
items.resolution_criteria: A workflow can land committed data on main autonomously (verified by a green gpu-burst ledger append on main AND the valuation producer repointed at main landing a snapshot commit), OR the operator explicitly accepts the data-branch pattern as permanent for these data feeds.

items.source: ruff 0.16.0 was released 2026-07-23 and the REQUIRED ruff-lint check installs ruff from the unpinned floor `ruff>=0.15.0` in requirements-dev.txt, so CI pulled 0.16.0. Its expanded DEFAULT rule set now flags C4 (flake8-comprehensions, e.g. C408 'unnecessary dict()') + I001 (import-order) among others, surfacing 8228 pre-existing hits across the repo (visualize_all.py, visualize_swings.py, and many more) and turning ruff-lint red on every .py-touching PR (first observed on PR #7500, run 30039827262). Earlier same-day green runs (#7488-#7490 at ~17:45-18:08) used ruff 0.15.x; the repo's ruff.toml sets NO `select` (intended: ruff's default rule set as-of-S-045) so the 0.16 default expansion silently changed the gate. Reproduced locally: `ruff check .` passes on 0.15.22, `Found 8228 errors` on 0.16.0.
items.title: ruff 0.16.0 default-ruleset expansion turned the required ruff-lint check red repo-wide (8228 pre-existing hits); pinned <0.16 as the interim hold
items.description: INTERIM FIX SHIPPED (PR #7500, this session): requirements-dev.txt pinned `ruff>=0.15.0,<0.16` so CI reproduces the S-045-intended 0.15.x default-ruleset behaviour and ruff-lint goes green again on every PR (self-healing: the pin lands in the same tree the workflow installs from). This holds the line but does NOT adopt the newer, stricter rules. DURABLE FOLLOW-UP (deliberate, separate PR): decide whether to adopt ruff 0.16's expanded default set. If yes: bump the pin, then clear the 8228 residuals by fix-or-suppress. Most are mechanical autofixes (`ruff check --fix` handles 6558) but they span operator-hold paths (src/runtime/*, src/units/accounts/*, src/main.py, config/*, deploy/*) which S-045/ruff.toml deliberately keep out of scope for mechanical lint edits without an operator ping-PR - so a blanket --fix is NOT safe; the operator-hold residuals need routing through a ping-PR or a ruff.toml per-file-ignores entry with the tracking comment block. If no: keep the <0.16 pin and periodically re-evaluate as ruff moves. Either way, when ruff eventually drops 0.15.x support the decision is forced.
items.tier: Tier 1 (CI/tooling: a dev-dependency pin already shipped; the adopt-or-hold follow-up is docs/tooling + possibly operator-ping-PRs for operator-hold-path lint fixes).
items.trigger_condition: Next CI/infra-touching session or the next /health-review; also whenever a session wants to adopt newer ruff rules or ruff drops 0.15.x.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the operator/team explicitly accepts staying on the <0.16 pin as the standing policy, OR (b) ruff 0.16+ is adopted with all 8228 residuals fixed-or-suppressed (operator-hold paths routed correctly) and the pin bumped, with ruff-lint green on both paths.

updates.note: Re-validated 07-26 against fresh full-system pull; carried (snoozed/deferred state confirmed still applicable, no regression this window).

OPERATOR DECISION 2026-07-26: BUMP to ruff 0.16 now — adopt the expanded default ruleset, clear the ~8228 residuals (6558 autofixable via `ruff check --fix`), then unpin from `<0.16`. Land as its own focused PR: autofix pass, manual triage of the non-autofixable residuals (likely per-file-ignores or targeted refactors), then remove the version pin in requirements-dev.txt + the CI installs. Kept open until landed.

items.title: [real-money] Bybit positions can go naked (no resting SL/TP leg) with ZERO detection or auto-recovery — no broker-side naked-verification sweep, _attempt_naked_autoprotect no-ops Bybit, and _check_naked_positions trusts journal SL/TP (intent, not broker legs)
items.description:
OBSERVED: a real-money bybit_2 XRPUSDT position with no TP/SL bracket. ROOT-CAUSE CLUSTER (all code-verified):

(1) No Bybit broker-side naked-verification sweep. order_monitor.py has _check_broker_naked_equity_positions (Alpaca, ~6112) and _check_broker_naked_ib_positions (IB, ~6234) that ask the broker 'does a resting protective leg actually exist?' and re-arm if not. There is NO Bybit equivalent. A Bybit position broker-naked-but-journal-protected is invisible to every check in the file.

(2) _attempt_naked_autoprotect (order_monitor.py:6084-6085) hard-returns False for Bybit ('not a re-armable broker (bybit/oanda atomic at entry)'). So even the DB-driven _check_naked_positions, if it flags a Bybit row, can only alert — never re-arm.

(3) _check_naked_positions selects on the JOURNAL row's stop_loss/take_profit_1 being NULL/<=0. Those fields are written from the INTENDED order['sl']/order['tp'] at open (execute._log_trade_to_journal), NOT from a confirmed broker leg — so a broker-naked Bybit position whose journal shows valid SL/TP is never flagged. (The observed XRP rows carry populated journal SL/TP.)

(4) The false assumption threading through all three (comments at order_monitor.py:6049-6050 and execute.py:1053-1056; CLAUDE.md 'Bybit/OANDA/Alpaca attach SL/TP atomically at entry, so a naked orphan can't occur there') is FALSE under two live conditions: (a) BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial (live on bybit_2, PRs #7161/#7162) makes SL/TP separate qty-scoped conditional legs whose lifecycle desyncs from the NETTED one-way exchange position — intent_reduce legs (NULL SL/TP by design) trim net qty without adding legs, and close_open_position cancels a closing trade's own legs (execute.py:2160-2185), so the SUM of resting legs can fall below (or to zero for) the net open qty; (b) the 20-combined-leg-per-symbol cap (BL-20260721) can silently block a leg amend/creation.

(5) Entry does not verify the SL/TP LEG was created. execute._submit_order bybit branch (execute.py:1116-1117) returns the parent orderId without confirming the qty-scoped Partial SL/TP legs exist; _classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs returns (None,None) when zero new legs appear, and that NULL is treated as 'untracked, use legacy path' rather than 'bracket failed — position is naked'. No rejection journal row, no re-arm.

SCOPE/RISK: bybit_2 is real_money (account_class real_money, yaml_mode live), symbols BTC/ETH/XRP/ADA. At audit time (08:01Z) bybit_2 held only ETHUSDT 0.06 (journal-protected; broker-leg existence UNVERIFIABLE by the bot — which is the point). No CURRENT naked real-money position, so not an active fire, but the class is live and recurs on XRP under partial-mode netting churn.

SECONDARY (separate, lower-severity) cracks found in the same audit: (a) order_packages.linked_trade_id frequently not written at execution ('multi-writer fan-out'); reconciler repairs it (live-observed on pairs pkgs 73775/4e4f) — self-heals but the monitor keys on order_packages status='open', so the package<->trade link is a fragile dependency. (b) monitor() is only invoked for strategies with an order_packages row at status='open'; a bare orphan_adopt row (or a package not status='open') is never handed to monitor(). (c) reverse-reconciler ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=close is an unimplemented stub that degrades to detect_only. (d) _MONITOR_BLINDNESS streak is in-process — resets on restart.
items.tier: 3 (order-path: the primary fix PLACES protective orders on a live real-money Bybit account — operator-gated, validate on bybit_1 demo first)
items.trigger_condition: A Bybit open position (esp. bybit_2 real-money) with no resting SL/TP conditional leg at the broker, regardless of journal SL/TP.
items.resolution_criteria: PRIMARY: add _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions(db) mirroring the Alpaca sweep (order_monitor.py:6112) — for each open, past-grace Bybit trade, read resting StopOrders via the existing primitive execute._partial_tpsl_leg_ids(client, category, symbol) (get_open_orders orderFilter=StopOrder); if the net position has no covering SL leg, re-arm via a new Bybit branch in _attempt_naked_autoprotect using set_trading_stop (qty-scoped in partial mode) with journal/resolved levels. Broker order-state is the idempotency (skip if a leg exists); fail-safe on read failure; skip a symbol in _TICK_ACTIVE_CLOSE_SYMBOLS. Wire into run_monitor_tick beside the Alpaca/IB sweeps. SECONDARY: in execute.py, when Partial-mode entry yields zero new SL (or TP) legs from _classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs, treat it as a bracket-placement FAILURE — attempt an immediate qty-scoped set_trading_stop re-arm and, if still absent, journal a rejection/alert instead of silently NULL-ing the id. Validate the re-arm path on bybit_1 (demo) via a dry-run/validation action before enabling on bybit_2. Also run cancel-stale-tpsl-legs (dry-run) on bybit_2 XRPUSDT to clear any stranded pre-fix legs.

updates.note: PRIMARY fix (Bybit broker-naked sweep + re-arm + entry-side verification) MERGED as PR #7874, demo-validated on bybit_1 (#7881), deployed live (git_sha dfd0172, trader restarted). SECONDARY cracks dispositioned: (1) linked_trade_id fan-out — FIXED: paper-only packages now stamp linked_trade_id immediately at execution (NULL-conditional first-writer-wins via Database.update_order_package_linked_trade_if_unset; real-money leg's unconditional write still wins in a mixed fanout), eliminating the 5-min reconciler-backfill NULL window (execute.py + database.py + tests, follow-up PR). (2) bare orphan_adopt not run through monitor() — VERIFIED-COVERED, no code change: _check_naked_positions selects ALL open non-backtest rows with no strategy filter, so a bare adopted orphan (NULL SL/TP) IS naked-swept + re-armed (now incl. Bybit); the reverse reconciler reattaches or closes-on-disappear. monitor() not firing on a strategy-less orphan is by-design. (3) ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=close stub — INTENTIONAL deferral, left as-is: default is 'adopt' (not close); the close branch logs + alerts + safely degrades to detect_only (never silent), and implementing reconciler-driven active flatten needs the integration test the code comment specifies (reduceOnly size/side + alert-before-close ordering) — a separate Tier-3, not requested. (4) monitor-blindness streak resets on restart — INTENTIONAL cold-start grace (a persisted streak would false-alert on the first post-restart tick before candles are fetched; the broker SL/TP backstop protects throughout). cancel-stale-tpsl-legs dry-run on bybit_2 XRPUSDT returned abort_flat (symbol currently flat — no stranded legs on an open position; re-run --apply if it re-accumulates).

items.source: RESEARCH-PROGRAM-2026-07-30 §3. Two producer failure classes exist and only ONE is guarded. Class A STALENESS (producer stops firing, ledger freezes) is covered by check_producer_liveness.py + macro-producer-liveness.yml (daily, Telegram + issue) — but scoped to ONE ledger (valuation_snapshots.jsonl). Class B VACUITY (producer fires, ledger grows, artifact is FRESH, but the measurement inside is empty and a verdict is published anyway) is guarded by NOTHING. The M1 econ event study was a textbook case: snapshots grew daily, the scorecard regenerated weekly, and the verdict came from price_bars:0 — every liveness signal green, the artifact perfectly fresh and completely vacuous (BL-20260730-M1-PRICE-JOIN-DEAD). silent-empty-guard cannot catch it either: it is a diff-scoped Python-`except` scanner over three src/ paths, so it sees neither scripts/macro|research/, nor the shell `|| echo` that actually hid this, nor the output-side contract of a verdict computed from an empty input set. An S-067 audit of this same bug CLASS exists from 2026-05-10 and it recurred anyway — a guard covering three paths against one language's syntax is not a guard against a bug class.
items.title: [tooling] Extend producer liveness from FRESHNESS to VALIDITY — nothing guards the 'green but vacuous' failure class
items.description: Fix has five parts, in leverage order: (1) DECLARED-INPUT ASSERTIONS — every research artifact already reports its input counts (price_bars, releases, n, total_scanned, records, max_n); the monitor reads them and reports VACUOUS when a load-bearing input is 0 or below the artifact's own declared floor, reusing the Telegram + GitHub-issue alerting already wired. (2) REGISTER EVERY SCHEDULED PRODUCER, not one ledger. (3) PRODUCERS FAIL LOUD — a load-bearing fetch may not degrade to a warning (done for econ-event-study in this session; generalize). (4) STANDING VACUITY SWEEP over comms/** scorecards + the soak logs, scheduled. (5) EXTEND silent-empty-guard's path scope to scripts/macro|research/ + add a shell rule for `|| echo` / `|| true` on a load-bearing fetch step.
items.trigger_condition: Any research/producer artifact can publish a verdict computed from zero inputs while its workflow exits 0.
items.resolution_criteria: check_producer_liveness (or a sibling) asserts non-zero declared inputs for every registered producer artifact and alerts VACUOUS; silent-empty-guard covers scripts/macro + scripts/research and flags `|| echo` on load-bearing fetch steps; a scheduled sweep reports any comms/** artifact whose inputs are zero.

If structural: say so explicitly IN the artifact (a `differing_pct: 0` with a declared reason), so a future reader cannot mistake it for a measurement. If broken: fix and re-soak. Either way it should carry a declared-input assertion once BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD lands. Then sweep the remaining soaks (fc-geometry, allocator, pairs, exit-lever) for the same pattern.

items.source: Found by the corrected-cost re-run itself (issue #7955, run 30519435812 on f67df73). Both re-grade tools iterate config/regime_coverage_exemptions.yaml::coverage_debt — and authoring a Tier-3 cell PAYS THE STRATEGY DOWN OUT of coverage_debt. So the moment a cell is authored, the strategy becomes unmeasurable by the tooling that authored it: regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell returned the literal error 'not in coverage_debt roster'. The tools could grade CANDIDATES but never RE-AUDIT a DECISION.
items.title: [regime][governance] Authoring a cell removed the strategy from the debt roster, making the authored cell permanently un-re-auditable by its own tooling
items.description: This bit immediately and exactly where it mattered most: the 2026-07-30 corrected-cost re-run (the whole point of which was to re-check evidence graded under a ~25x fee over-charge) silently DID NOT re-measure `gld_pullback_1h` — the one live Tier-3 cell the fee fix most called into question — because authoring that cell in #7923 had removed it from coverage_debt. The run reported 34 rows and zero errors, so nothing looked wrong: a blind spot precisely at the live gate, presented as a complete re-grade. Same shape as the 'green but vacuous' class (BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD) one level up: the artifact was complete WITH RESPECT TO ITS ROSTER, and the roster was the wrong set. FIXED in this session: regime_debt_matrix.resolve_strategy(name) resolves ANY strategy declared in config/strategies.yaml, and both --only and regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell fall back to it, so an explicitly-named already-celled strategy stays auditable. The DEFAULT roster is unchanged (still the debt list). FOLLOW-UP still open: (a) re-measure gld_pullback_1h + walk-forward it on corrected costs and record the verdict; (b) consider whether every AUTHORED cell should be on a standing re-audit list, so a cell's evidence is periodically re-checked rather than frozen at authoring time — a cell authored on a bug is otherwise permanent.

TWO GAPS FOUND WHILE SCOPING, both filed: BL-20260730-2D-VOL-CELLS-UNAUDITABLE (the six 2-D trend_vol cells cannot be re-measured by ANY tool — no vol-split exists — and ict_scalp_5m carries ONLY 2-D cells, so its entire live gating is unreachable; 6 of 16 live-affecting cells stay un-re-audited even after #7962+#7963) and BL-20260730-AUTHORED-CELL-REAUDIT-REGISTER (the practice, not the tool: nothing re-measures cells on a cadence). Follow-up (2) of this row — 'decide whether authored cells get a standing re-audit list' — is ANSWERED YES by the operator and now tracked in that register row.

RE-AUDIT RESULTS IN (#7962, #7963). gld_pullback_1h: the live cell SURVIVES — trending short -13.88R@37 = -0.375 R/trade (predicted -0.32 to -0.40), long +37.18R@54 confirming the predicted understatement. NO revert needed; that sub-item is CLOSED. htf_pullback_trend_2h: the trending cell looks INVERTED on current data (long -6.85@42 while permitted, short +7.89@54 while gated) — walk-forward dispatched #7968, NOT proposed as a change (#7915 already refuted a full-sample directional read on this family). COVERAGE: only 4 of 16 live-affecting cells are actually re-auditable. Three distinct blockers, two NEW: no vol-split (6 2-D cells), no harness mapping (squeeze_breakout_4h errors unclassifiable -> BL-20260730-SQUEEZE-NO-HARNESS), and approximate-only (trend_donchian -> BL-20260730-DONCHIAN-APPROX-ONLY). items.source: The corrected-cost regime re-grade (issue #7955) cannot cleanly attribute its deltas: the matrix window is a ROLLING 730 days and the baseline run was ~a day earlier, so every delta mixes the fee correction with a window slide. Proof the confound is real: slv_trend_1h chop short moved -0.56R the WRONG way at n=10, which a fee REDUCTION cannot cause.
items.title: [research][method] Run the fixed-window fee A/B — the corrected-cost deltas are inferred, not attributed
items.description: One matrix pass, same candle window, two --fee-bps-roundtrip arms (0 for commission-free vs the flat 7.5), diffed per cell. That isolates the fee effect from window drift and turns 'consistent with the predicted 0.04-0.12 R/trade band' into a measured number. Cheap (a second arm in the same run). Until it exists, no per-cell delta in docs/research/regime-debt-matrix-corrected-cost-2026-07-30.md should be quoted as a fee amount, and the asset-class re-read (whether marginal-negative equity/ETF legs flip positive) stays deferred — the legs that would flip are small-n, which is exactly where drift dominates.
items.trigger_condition: Anyone quoting a corrected-cost delta as a measured fee effect, or re-reading the equity/ETF sleeve off the uncontrolled comparison.
items.resolution_criteria: A fixed-window two-arm fee A/B is run and its per-cell deltas recorded; the findings doc's §1 caveat is replaced with measured attribution.

items.source: regime-debt-matrix run 30519330796: splg_trend_long_1d returned ALL ZEROS (no trades in any regime) with NO error, inside a run reporting '0 errored, 0 skipped'. Found while harvesting, not by any guard.
items.title: [strategy] splg_trend_long_1d produced ZERO trades over 730d — no signals, or a broken feed/params?
items.description: A row that measured nothing, presented as a measured row — the BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD class at row level rather than artifact level. Two possibilities, both worth knowing: (a) the strategy legitimately fired no signals in two years, which is significant for a LIVE-declared strategy (is it stranded?); or (b) its feed/params resolve to nothing in the harness. Diagnose which. If (a), it belongs in the same conversation as strategy-silence detection; if (b), the harness row should ERROR rather than return zeros. Consider whether the matrix should flag an all-zero row rather than emit it silently.
items.trigger_condition: A matrix/backtest row returns zero trades across every regime with no error.
items.resolution_criteria: Root cause identified (no-signal vs broken resolution); if no-signal, the live-strategy implication recorded; the matrix flags all-zero rows explicitly.

items.source: Found while scoping the operator-directed re-audit of authored regime cells (#7962, #7963). regime_debt_matrix measures the 1-D TREND axis only — it has no vol-split — so the six 2-D `trend_vol` cells cannot be re-measured by ANY existing tool. This is a second, independent instance of BL-20260730-REGIME-CELL-UNAUDITABLE: cells that gate live routing with no mechanism to re-check them.
items.title: [regime] the offline harness has NO vol axis — and the obvious fix (the frozen vol_detector) would reproduce the very population-mismatch this row exists to flag
items.description: The 2-D cells and why they matter: trend_donchian (trending/volatile, transitional/calm, chop/calm), squeeze_breakout_4h (trending/calm), ict_scalp_5m (trending/volatile, chop/volatile). All six affect LIVE BTC routing — BTC has an advisory regime head and REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use enforce is live, so these cells drop real intents. Yet regime_debt_matrix has no vol axis, so a matrix re-run cannot see them. ict_scalp_5m is the worst case: it carries NO 1-D cells at all, so its entire live gating rests on two 2-D cells that NOTHING can currently re-measure. After #7962 + #7963 land, 6 of 16 live-affecting cells remain un-re-audited. NEEDED: a vol-split re-run — tag emitted trades with the vol label the router would resolve (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol when an advisory head exists, else the frozen vol_detector edges) and break the matrix down per (trend, vol, direction). The 2026-06-27 Design-A vol-split (docs/research/A-vol-gating-OFFcell-design-2026-06-27.md) did this once by hand; the gap is that it was never turned into repeatable tooling. Until it is, do NOT describe the authored cells as re-checked. || ESCALATED 2026-07-30 (severity medium -> high) after this nearly caused a bad Tier-3 proposal. The scope is worse than 'the 2-D cells cannot be audited': because regime_cell_walkforward / regime_debt_matrix / regime_tag_emitted contain NO vol axis at all (verified by grep: zero hits for trend_vol|vol_regime|calm|volatile), a 1-D cell re-audit POOLS every vol state -- including the vol states a 2-D cell already gates live. The measured trade population therefore differs from the live-traded population, so the verdict is not decision-grade. Same fidelity class as the side_filter bug fixed this morning (BL-20260730 side_filter forwarding): the harness measured legs the strategy never takes. CONCRETE NEAR-MISS: I was about to propose squeeze_breakout_4h trending short -> off on walk-forward #7990 (short_stable_drag TRUE, 3/4 folds, pooled -3.40R n=26, sign holds ex-fold-3). But config/regime_policy.yaml already gates trending/calm squeeze short via a 2-D cell, so an unknown fraction of those 26 shorts are calm trades LIVE ALREADY REFUSES. If the drag sits in the calm shorts, live is already protected and the 1-D change only adds a block on volatile shorts that may be fine; if it sits in the volatile shorts the change is justified -- and the harness cannot tell these apart. Proposal WITHHELD. EXACT CONTAMINATED SET (both 1-D and 2-D cells): squeeze_breakout_4h (trending/calm) and trend_donchian (trending/volatile, transitional/calm, chop/calm). VERIFIED CLEAN, so prior conclusions on them STAND: htf_pullback_trend_2h has NO 2-D cell (the operator-approved long->off merged in #7979 is unaffected -- checked, not assumed) and gld_pullback_1h has none (its SURVIVES verdict is unaffected). FIX: add the vol axis to the harness so a cell is graded on the (trend, vol) population live actually trades; until then NO 1-D cell change may be proposed for a contaminated strategy. || SCOPED 2026-07-30 -- and the fix is NOT 'add a vol indicator to the harness', which is what this row would previously have led a session to build. Verified in intents.py's own docstring: 'BTC has the 15m advisory head, so every BTC cell resolves the ML label regardless of the strategy's timeframe (the live trend_vol cells gate BTC trend_donchian (1h) + squeeze_breakout_4h (4h) and they DO resolve ML, not frozen)'. BOTH contaminated strategies are BTCUSDT, so their LIVE vol label comes from the ADVISORY ML HEAD btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 thresholded at ML_VOL_VERDICT_THRESHOLD (0.5) -- NOT from the frozen vol_detector. Splitting the harness on the frozen detector would therefore NOT reproduce live; it would be a SECOND, different mismatch that looks like a fix. TWO PATHS, and they answer different questions: (A) BACKTEST-BASED CELL GRADING requires replaying the ML vol head offline per bar. The manifest IS in-repo (ml/configs/btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1.yaml) but the trained ARTIFACT is not -- it lives in the trainer registry, pullable via the trainer-vm-diag relay (autonomous territory). Steps: pull the artifact; score it on historical BTC 15m bars using the manifest's feature list via the offline pure fns so live==train; threshold at 0.5 -> calm/volatile per bar; map each emitted trade's entry time to the containing 15m bar's label; then add a --vol-split to regime_tag_emitted / regime_debt_matrix / regime_cell_walkforward so a cell is graded on the (trend, vol) population. This is the real unlock and it is a MULTI-STEP BUILD, not a one-commit change -- do not scope it as one. Same replay class as analyze_exit_head (see BL-20260730-EXITHEAD-REPLAY-SINGLE-THRESHOLD); it is feasible, just not cheap. (B) CHEAPER, COMPLEMENTARY, DIFFERENT QUESTION: for LIVE trades the vol label is ALREADY RECORDED -- the hard gate writes a regime_hard_gate audit row carrying the resolved `cell`, queryable via /api/diag/audit_query?event=regime_hard_gate. That measures what live is actually gating and can be done now with no ML replay, but it CANNOT grade a backtest cell (historical backtest trades have no audit rows) so it does not substitute for (A). UNTIL (A) LANDS: no 1-D cell change may be proposed for squeeze_breakout_4h or trend_donchian. || DESIGN SCOPED 2026-07-30 (operator-directed 'start on the vol axis'). Two facts, both verified in CODE not inferred from docs, that together kill the obvious approach. (1) ALL SIX live 2-D cells are BTCUSDT: trend_donchian 1h (trending/volatile long, transitional/calm long, chop/calm long), ict_scalp_5m 5m (trending/volatile and chop/volatile, both legs), squeeze_breakout_4h 4h (trending/calm short). (2) NONE of those three strategies declares a `vol_spec` in config/strategies.yaml (only ict_scalp_xrp_5m does, and it has no 2-D cell) -- because live does NOT use the frozen detector for them at all. src/runtime/intents.py::_decision_vol_regime resolves the DECISION vol label from the BTC 15m ADVISORY HEAD's ML P(volatile), keyed PER SYMBOL (deliberately not per (symbol,timeframe), so the single 15m head's label drives the 1h and 4h cells too), thresholded at ML_VOL_VERDICT_THRESHOLD. THE KILLER DETAIL, quoted from that function's own docstring: the trend_vol cells 'were authored under the ML label and LOSE money under the frozen label' (docs/research/A-vol-gating-OFFcell-design-2026-06-27.md). So an offline vol axis built on vol_detector would not merely be an approximation -- it would measure a population live does not gate on, whose documented behaviour is OPPOSITE. That is exactly the population-mismatch failure this row was opened for, which is why the frozen-detector shortcut must NOT be taken however cheap it looks (vol_regime_from_spec is pure and injectable, so it is genuinely tempting). THE CORRECT AXIS: replay the BTC 15m advisory head (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1) per bar -> P(volatile) -> threshold -> calm/volatile per SYMBOL, i.e. reproduce _decision_vol_regime offline rather than its frozen fallback. This IS replayable -- the same class of thing scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py already does for the exit head (see BL-20260730 exit-head correction: 'an ML head cannot be replayed offline' was FALSE). It needs the head artifacts + the serve-time feature row, both trainer-side, so the build is a trainer-relay job, not a sandbox job. COVERAGE NOTE for whoever builds it: the only committed frozen specs are docs/research/artifacts/ict_scalp_phase0/btc{5m,15m}_volspec.json and they name btc-regime-{5m,15m}-baseline-v1 -- NOT the current advisory head -- so they are stale for this purpose as well as wrong-mechanism. Do not build on them.
items.trigger_condition: Any claim that the authored regime cells have been re-audited, or any 2-D cell authoring/revocation without a vol-split measurement.
items.resolution_criteria: A repeatable vol-split matrix exists (per (trend, vol, direction) net-R using the router's own vol-label resolution) and all six 2-D cells have a recorded re-audit verdict.

updates.note: TOOL BUILT (path A), NOT YET RUN — this update is the build, not the verdict. Two committed pieces: (1) scripts/research/ml_vol_label_replay.py replays the ADVISORY head offline into per-bar calm/volatile labels, resolving the head + threshold through the ROUTER'S OWN resolvers (discover_advisory_stage_regime_specs / _ml_vol_verdict_threshold) rather than a hardcoded model id — so the 2026-07-20-style head swap is tracked automatically instead of drifting; (2) regime_tag_emitted.py gained --vol-labels / --only-vol, a by_cell 'trending/calm'-keyed breakdown, and an explicit vol_axis: present|absent declaration on EVERY run so a 1-D grade can never again be read as covering the vol axis. 21 new tests (tests/test_regime_vol_axis.py), incl. a PARITY test that drives the real live ml_vol_regime_for_symbol through its per-bar cache and asserts the replay lands on the same label at the >= boundary. TRAINER INVENTORY (#8054/#8055) confirms the replay needs NO Chronos re-run: the registry entry is target_deployment_stage=advisory with model_state_path=.../20260730T012123Z/model_state.json, and the head's own training frame market_features/BTCUSDT/15m/v520 (175,272 rows) already carries the six fc_* columns joined — so scoring reads the built dataset. TWO LIMITS FOUND, both to declare not hide: (a) v520 SPANS 2021-07-01 -> 2026-06-30 ONLY, so any emitted trade after 2026-06-30 gets vol_regime=unknown and lands in a */unknown row (the harness counts + prints this coverage rather than folding it into calm); the fresher forecasts side-stream v002 already runs to 2026-07-29, so closing the gap is a market_features rebuild, not new tooling; (b) the replay is IN-SAMPLE over the head's training window (the production artifact is fit on full history) — stamped into the labels manifest as fidelity.in_sample=true. NOT DONE, and the row STAYS OPEN: nothing has been measured yet. Next, in order: run the replay on the trainer against v520; run `verify` against the live gate's own regime_ml_vol_shadow / regime_hard_gate audit rows (the empirical test of the offline-vs-serve feature-row caveat — an unverified label file must NOT grade a cell, and the tool returns verdict=no_overlap_nothing_verified rather than a pass when nothing was compared); only then grade the six 2-D cells. The withheld squeeze_breakout_4h trending-short proposal stays withheld until that sequence completes.

CROSS-FINDING with the same-day provenance work (#8039, merged 15:55Z) — recording it so a future session grading these cells does not have to rediscover it. #8039 established that on DEMO bybit books `exit_price` is a mark taken 6+ hours after the close, producing FABRICATED `local_markprice` pnl (226 rows / +$247,683 lifetime; fabricated share 0.0% May -> 30.5% Jun -> 64.9% Jul), and that the headline '-$6,358 7d bybit scalp exit leak' is substantially a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT — real-money 7d scalp pnl on bybit_2 is -$1.91. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: the vol-axis cell grading built in this session consumes HARNESS-EMITTED backtest trades (`net_r` computed by the harness itself), so it is NOT contaminated by journal provenance — that is the reason to keep grading on the backtest substrate. But the moment anyone grades a 2-D cell from LIVE/journal rows instead (e.g. joining `regime_hard_gate` audit rows to realised pnl — the tempting path (B) shortcut in this row's own scoping), the `exit_price_source` / provenance split becomes load-bearing: on the demo books the pnl is fabricated and a cell verdict computed from it would be measuring a number nobody observed. Use `src/runtime/provenance.py::is_measured` / `coverage()` (shipped in #8039) to gate any such join, and report the measured share next to the verdict the way `/performance` reports rCoverage. Related rows: BL-20260730-DEMO-MARKPRICE-FABRICATES-PAPER-PNL, BL-20260730-PROVENANCE-RECORDED-THEN-IGNORED.

REPLAY RAN + A REAL TOOL BUG FOUND AND FIXED. (1) fc-pcv-v1 over v520 SUCCEEDED: 175,272 bars labelled, calm 159,324 / volatile 15,948 = 9.1% volatile, P(volatile) over 109,751 distinct values, 15s / 423MB RSS, feature audit ok with vol_bucket parity 5,008 compared / 0 mismatches. (2) THEN the pre-flight EARNED ITS KEEP: replaying btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 over v520, and fc-pcv-v1 over v002, BOTH ABORTED on vol_bucket parity mismatch. ROOT CAUSE — a trap for ANY offline head replay, worth knowing beyond this row: `market_features` RECOMPUTES its vol_bucket quantile edges PER BUILD, over that build's own window. v002 spans 2021-07-30..2026-07-29 vs v520's 2021-07-01..2026-06-30, so its edges differ slightly (observed: rolling_log_return_vol=0.002478 stored as vol_b2 by v002 while the head's frozen upper edge 0.0024927 puts it in vol_b1). So a head scored on ANY build other than the one it trained on silently receives a DIFFERENT categorical — a valid-looking category the head never trained on for that bar. NOT a live bug: the live serve path always buckets from the head's frozen edges. But it would have produced 175k confidently-wrong offline labels, and the resulting live-vs-replay disagreement would have been misread as a serve-path parity failure. (3) THE DEEPER FIX (PR #8077): my replay was reading the dataset's stored vol_bucket, but regime_shadow.feature_row_for_predictor NEVER does — it derives the bucket from the head's own frozen edges via bucket_for_vol on the head's vol_feature_column. So trusting the stored column was LESS faithful to live AND coupled each head to one build. --vol-bucket now defaults to `live` (derive from frozen edges, honouring a yz head's yang_zhang_vol); identical by construction where head and build agree, and the manifest reports how many rows differed where they don't. This unblocks replaying any head against any build. (4) STILL NOT VERIFIED and the row STAYS OPEN — verify has not run, no cell is graded, squeeze_breakout_4h stays withheld.

VERIFY RAN — and it is a FINDING, which is why the tool was built to report rather than bless. Against the 34 live regime_ml_vol_shadow rows for BTCUSDT over 06-28..06-30: 88.24% label agreement (30/34), but median |dP(volatile)| 0.043 / p90 0.209 / max 0.412. Bar-misalignment RULED OUT by a +/-2-bar probe (#8080) including an AGREEING control row that also matches no adjacent replayed bar — so the offline feature row genuinely differs from the served one. Filed as BL-20260730-OFFLINE-VS-SERVE-PVOLATILE-GAP (severity high). CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: the vol axis is USABLE and is still a large improvement on the 1-D pooling it replaces (which measured a population live never trades), but every cell verdict produced from these labels must carry the ~88% live-agreement fidelity, and a verdict that flips on a few near-threshold bars is NOT decision-grade. The six 2-D cells are still UNGRADED and squeeze_breakout_4h stays WITHHELD — now for a better-understood reason than before.

items.source: The general form of BL-20260730-REGIME-CELL-UNAUDITABLE. Operator answered the standing question ('should every authored cell be re-audited?') with yes. #7958 made authored cells MEASURABLE again; nothing yet re-measures them on a cadence, so a cell authored on a bug stays authored indefinitely — which is exactly how the gld_pullback_1h cell survived a ~25x fee over-charge unnoticed.
items.title: [regime][governance] Stand up an authored-cell RE-AUDIT REGISTER — a decision is not permanent evidence
items.description: Eight strategies carry authored cells (5 live: gld_pullback_1h, htf_pullback_trend_2h, ict_scalp_5m, squeeze_breakout_4h, trend_donchian; 3 shadow: fade_breakout_4h, fvg_range_15m, vwap). Most 1-D cells trace to regime-roster-matrix-2026-06-01 and had NEVER been re-measured before 2026-07-30. Build the register: for each authored cell record (a) the evidence run + date it was authored from, (b) its fidelity flag at authoring time, (c) a re-audit due-date, and (d) the last re-audit verdict. Then re-measure on that cadence — the natural home is the /system-review roll-up, which already has a promotion/demotion readiness mandate and a coverage guard that fails when a required assessment is skipped. Two design points learned the hard way: the register must key off config/regime_policy.yaml (the CELLS), never off coverage_debt (a work queue that ERASES an item when it is acted on); and it must record fidelity, because an approximate row cannot sustain a cell. Composes with the binding 'Green is not evidence' rule's corollary — a decision is not permanent evidence.
items.trigger_condition: An authored cell has no recorded re-audit date, or its last re-audit is older than its declared cadence.
items.resolution_criteria: A committed authored-cell register exists covering every cell in regime_policy.yaml with authoring evidence + fidelity + due-date + last verdict, and a review cadence owns re-measuring it.

items.source: The multiline-aware `|| echo` guard found FOUR producer workflows whose candle fetch swallows its own failure and lets the downstream gate report 'the honest n=0': cot-positioning-backfill.yml, m28-value-grade.yml, macro-valuation-backfill.yml, sysdyn-gas-calibrate.yml. All four were INVISIBLE to the first (line-based) version of the guard because the `||` sits on a shell line-continuation.
items.title: [research] Four macro gates degrade a failed candle fetch into an 'honest n=0' verdict — annotated allow-degraded, not resolved
items.description: Each workflow comments that a degraded fetch means the gate 'will report the honest n=0 / insufficient_data'. That framing is exactly the class BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD exists to kill: a gate publishing a verdict computed from zero inputs, on a green run. 'Honest n=0' is honest about the COUNT but not about the CAUSE — a reader cannot tell 'no data exists' from 'the fetch broke'. Annotated with `# allow-degraded: <this id>` so the guard passes and the debt is attributed rather than silent; NOT fixed, because changing four producers' failure semantics is a real behaviour change that deserves its own reviewed pass. THE FIX for each: let the fetch fail (set -e), or keep it tolerant but have the DOWNSTREAM gate distinguish 'no candles fetched' from 'candles fetched, no signal' and refuse to emit a verdict in the former case (register those artifacts in check_artifact_validity.CHECKS). NOTE the annotation has no expiry mechanism — unlike KNOWN_VACUOUS, which fails once its date passes; consider giving allow-degraded the same treatment so these cannot become permanent.
items.trigger_condition: A macro gate reports n=0 / insufficient_data and nobody checks whether its inputs were fetched at all.
items.resolution_criteria: Each of the four either fails on a degraded fetch, or its downstream gate distinguishes unfetched from no-signal and is registered in check_artifact_validity; the allow-degraded annotations are then removed.

items.opened_by: claude (self-review of the guard I just shipped)
items.source: Self-review. KNOWN_VACUOUS in check_artifact_validity.py requires a backlog owner AND an `until` date, and the guard FAILS once the date passes — so tracked debt cannot become permanent. The sibling override for swallowed fetches, the inline `# allow-degraded: <reason>` comment, has NEITHER requirement enforced: any string satisfies it, forever. I shipped the weaker override in the same PR as the stronger one.
items.title: [tooling] `# allow-degraded:` has no owner/expiry enforcement — the weaker sibling of KNOWN_VACUOUS
items.description: Make the guard parse the annotation and require (a) a backlog id matching a real row in one of the three review backlogs, and (b) an `until:` date, failing once it passes — mirroring known_vacuous_problems(). Otherwise allow-degraded is exactly the silence list KNOWN_VACUOUS was deliberately designed not to be, and the four annotations added in this PR (BL-20260730-CANDLE-FETCH-DEGRADES-TO-N0) will sit forever. Small change; worth doing before the annotation spreads.
items.trigger_condition: An `# allow-degraded:` annotation exists with no backlog row or no expiry.
items.resolution_criteria: The guard validates every allow-degraded annotation for a resolvable backlog id + an unexpired `until:`, and fails otherwise.

items.source: The re-audit run errored on squeeze_breakout_4h: 'unclassifiable (no donchian/pullback params or no symbol/timeframe)'. regime_debt_matrix.classify() only recognises Donchian-trend and pullback shapes, so a squeeze/breakout strategy maps to no offline harness at all.
items.title: [regime] squeeze_breakout_4h maps to NO offline harness — its 4 live cells can never be re-audited
items.description: squeeze_breakout_4h is execution: live and carries THREE 1-D cells (trending {long:on,short:on}, transitional {long:on,short:on}, chop {long:on,short:on}) plus ONE 2-D cell (trending/calm {short:off}). None can be re-measured: classify() returns None so the matrix errors the row. The cells therefore rest permanently on their 2026-06-01 authoring evidence with no mechanism to re-check. Options: (a) add a squeeze/breakout harness to scripts/ (the real fix — it also unlocks exit-refinement and tuning for this strategy); (b) if the strategy's cells are all-permissive on the 1-D axis (they are: every 1-D cell is on/on), note that they gate nothing and could be dropped as cosmetic, leaving only the 2-D cell to worry about. Do (b)'s analysis first — it may shrink the problem to one cell.
items.trigger_condition: A celled strategy errors as unclassifiable in a re-audit run.
items.resolution_criteria: squeeze_breakout_4h's cells are either re-measured by a new harness, or shown to be all-permissive/cosmetic and dropped.

updates.note:
DISPROVED — squeeze_breakout_4h DOES map to an offline harness and its cells ARE re-auditable. I ran the full offline audit today.

Harness run receipt (trainer-diag #8110): scripts/backtest_squeeze.py --data data/btc_1h_multiyear.csv --symbol BTCUSDT --timeframe 4h --resample 4h --bb-period 20 --bb-std 2.0 --kc-mult 1.0 --atr-period 14 --atr-stop-mult 2.5 --trail-mult 3.5  ->  trades=110, win_rate 38.18%, net_r 17.6142, maxdd_r 7.8888, span 2021-01-01..2026-06-01. That reproduces the documented basis in config/strategies.yaml:315 ('+17.6R multiyear ... lowest DD (7.9R)') to 4 significant figures, which is the independent check that the harness was driven with the strategy's REAL live params and not defaults. NOTE --kc-mult 1.0: the harness default is 1.5, so omitting it silently grades a different strategy.

The harness is named in config/strategies.yaml:303 ('harness: scripts/backtest_squeeze.py'), and scripts/research/regime_tag_emitted.py is the engine-agnostic post-processor for exactly this — its own docstring lists backtest_squeeze.py as a supported emitter. Tagged output with the vol axis attached, 96.4% vol coverage (106/110).

This mattered: the item as written ('its 4 live cells can never be re-audited') would stop a future session from even attempting the audit that just resolved a parked Tier-3 proposal. Leaving a false blocker standing is as costly as leaving a bug standing.

items.source: trend_donchian re-measured as APPROXIMATE — the trend harness omits its declared exit_head_action / exit_head_model / exit_head_threshold / trail_decay_arm_r / trail_decay_tight_mult. Per the no-cosmetic-cell rule an approximate row cannot source or un-source a cell, so its SIX cells (3x 1-D + 3x 2-D) are measurable but not actionable.
items.title: [regime] trend_donchian is only measurable as `approximate` — its 6 cells cannot be acted on either way
items.description: This is the most-celled live strategy and the one whose cells were used as the exemplar for the whole debt roster, yet a re-audit cannot act on it: any losing cell could be an artifact of the omitted lever, and any winning cell could be flattered by it. exit_head_* is inherently unreplayable offline (an ML exit head) — so the honest options are (a) port trail_decay into the trend harness (mechanical, mirrors the stale-exit port done for rec #5) which would leave only exit_head_* omitted, then judge whether that residual is small enough to call the row faithful; or (b) accept that a strategy carrying an ML exit head can never be re-audited offline and require a LIVE-evidence path for its cells instead. Note (a) is a real improvement regardless — the same omission blocks exit-refinement work on this leg.
items.trigger_condition: A cell decision is proposed or defended on an approximate row.
items.resolution_criteria: trail_decay is modelled in the trend harness (or an equivalent path exists), and trend_donchian's cells have a recorded re-audit verdict on a row whose omissions are declared acceptable.

items.source: The re-audit shows trend_donchian producing ZERO short trades in every regime over 730d (short-R 0.0, n=0 throughout) — it runs long-only — yet config/regime_policy.yaml carries short directions for it in all three 1-D regimes (chop {short:on}, transitional {short:off}, trending {short:off}).
items.title: [regime] trend_donchian carries SHORT cells while producing zero short trades — cosmetic cells, the named anti-pattern
items.description: A cell that gates a direction the strategy never takes is exactly the cosmetic cell the no-cosmetic-cell rule exists to prevent — it looks like governance and enforces nothing. Worse, it is actively misleading: the chop {short: on} cell carries the comment 'short +16 <- reclaims long-only drop', i.e. the authoring evidence measured shorts that the current config cannot produce, so the comment documents a configuration that no longer exists. Verify whether long_only was always set or is a later change (git log config/strategies.yaml), then either drop the short halves of those cells or record why they are retained (e.g. so the gate is already correct if long_only is ever lifted — a defensible reason, but it should be WRITTEN).
items.trigger_condition: An authored cell gates a direction the strategy cannot produce.
items.resolution_criteria: trend_donchian's short cells are dropped or their retention rationale is recorded in regime_policy.yaml.

items.source: scripts/research/regime_debt_matrix.py::_SQZ_TP_R_NONBINDING. Wiring backtest_squeeze.py into classify() exposed one infidelity: the harness has no --tp-r flag (it models the Chandelier trail as the sole profit-exit). The live config's tp_r: 50.0 cannot bind before a 3.5-ATR trail fires, so the omission is harmless there — but that is currently asserted via a THRESHOLD CONSTANT (20R), not measured.
items.title: [regime] squeeze tp_r non-binding bound is a threshold constant, not an empirical check
items.description: The honest version of this check is empirical: after the harness run, verify no emitted trade's MFE ever reached tp_r on the sample; only then is ignoring tp_r provably non-binding FOR THAT SAMPLE. The threshold form can be wrong in principle (a tighter trail or a calmer regime could let a 20R+ target bind, and a future strategy could sit just above the line). Implementing it needs a post-run fidelity adjustment in BOTH callers (regime_debt_matrix.run_one and regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell), which return fidelity before the subprocess runs — a real refactor, not a one-liner, which is why it is filed rather than inlined. Severity is low because the current bound fails CLOSED (below 20R the row degrades to `approximate`, blocking cell authoring) and the live value is 50R. Note this is self-filed: the guard I wrote is weaker than the guard I would want reviewing someone else's.

items.title: [regime] squeeze-harness wiring is unit-verified but has NEVER produced a real measurement
items.description: BUILT != VERIFIED. What is proven: classification resolves, the flag set is accepted by the harness's own declared options, adx degrades instead of crashing, and the tp_r bound fails closed. What is NOT proven: that an end-to-end run yields trades at usable n, that regime_tag_emitted.py can tag them, and therefore that squeeze_breakout_4h's FOUR live cells are actually re-auditable now. Until a runner-side run returns a populated matrix, the correct statement is 'the blocker is removed in code', NOT 'the cells are re-auditable'. Close this by dispatching regime-debt-matrix (or regime-cell-walkforward) for squeeze_breakout_4h on a GitHub-hosted runner once the wiring is on main, and recording the n per regime.

items.source: The session's working clone was SHALLOW: 57 commits, spanning 2026-07-28..07-30 only (.git/shallow present). Discovered because `git log -S'exit_head_model' -- config/strategies.yaml` dead-ended at a single 2026-07-28 whole-file commit, which looked like a real answer. `git fetch --deepen=2000` recovered history to 2026-03-22 (2718 commits) and immediately changed a research conclusion (see docs/research/regime-debt-matrix-corrected-cost-2026-07-30.md A6).
items.title: [tooling] shallow session clone silently defeats the mandated `git log -p` history check
items.description: CLAUDE.md § 'Every session' requires, for Tier-2/3 files, 'also read its recent history (git log -p <file>) so you don't undo a load-bearing, operator-approved decision.' On a shallow clone that check returns a PLAUSIBLE BUT WRONG answer with no error: the file reads as having one commit, three days old. This is the session's own bug class turned on its own tooling -- green relative to a wrong scope -- and it is the highest-leverage item here because it silently degrades EVERY session's compliance with a rule meant to prevent undoing operator-approved decisions. Concrete harm already observed: without the deepen, trend_donchian's regime cells appeared to have no authoring history, so the fact that all 6 predate the 2026-07-12 exit-head go-live (#6211) was invisible. Fix options: (a) have the session bootstrap/CLAUDE.md instruct `git fetch --deepen` (or --unshallow) before any history-dependent check; (b) better, make the check fail LOUD -- a tiny helper that refuses to answer a history question on a shallow clone rather than answering it wrongly. (b) is preferred and is the same fail-closed shape as the artifact-validity guard.

items.source: Dated via git after deepening the clone: trend_donchian's 1-D cells were authored 2026-06-01 (#2583), its 2-D trend_vol OFF cells 2026-06-28 (#4868), while exit_head_model exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 began driving REAL exits on 2026-07-12 (#6211, Tier-3 operator-approved). All 6 live cells predate the exit head by 2-6 weeks. Blast radius enumerated programmatically against regime_policy.yaml + strategies.yaml: 6 live cells (3x 1-D + 3x 2-D) on one live strategy.
items.title: [regime] trend_donchian's 6 live cells rest on evidence SUPERSEDED by the exit head — re-audit via the M20 exit-panel path
items.description: CORRECTED 2026-07-30 by the operator. This row previously claimed the cells could NEVER be re-measured because an ML exit head cannot be replayed offline. THAT WAS FALSE and the row is rewritten so the false premise is not carried forward. The M20 toolchain replays exactly this: scripts/research/build_intrabar_exit_panel.py builds the per-bar in-trade panel and scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py SIMULATES the head's exit decisions per trade (first bar the head says exit, the trade realizes its mark-to-market R there, net of an exit fee) under grouped-by-trade_id, purged, embargoed, uniqueness-weighted walk-forward, scored against the baseline fixed SL/TP exit. That is more rigorous than the harness I had treated as the only option. ROOT CAUSE OF THE ERROR: regime_debt_matrix.py::_UNREPLAYABLE carried the comment 'an ML exit head can never be replayed offline'; its real meaning is narrow (backtest_trend.py does not model this lever). A local scope limitation was read as a global impossibility and promoted to a research conclusion. Same bug class as the rest of this session, one level up -- a tool reporting IMPOSSIBILITY out of a wrong scope deserves at least as much suspicion as one reporting success, because it closes off work rather than merely mis-reporting it. The stale comment is fixed in place. WHAT STANDS: the dates. Cells authored 2026-06-01 (#2583) and 2026-06-28 (#4868); exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 began driving real exits 2026-07-12 (#6211). All 6 live cells predate it by 2-6 weeks, so the evidence IS superseded. ACTUAL NEXT STEP (no operator decision needed): (1) build the intrabar exit panel for trend_donchian over the regime-tagged window; (2) replay exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 at its LIVE threshold 0.10 / action close so simulated exits match the live exit policy; (3) split per-trade R by regime via regime_tag_emitted.py and apply the SAME short_stable_drag/long_stable_drag gate used for every other cell (#7915), so all six are graded on one consistent bar.
