items.source: Observed while driving PR #8069 to green. Verified against three independent PRs and the Actions run list.
items.title: P1: pull_request-triggered CI does not run on ANY PR — merges are landing unchecked
items.detail:
EVIDENCE (all read via the GitHub MCP, 2026-07-30):
1. PR #8069 (this session's): total_count=0 checks across FIVE separate real pushes (826cfe89, f6e2b100, c77344c7, 6f80d2e5, 1d9a7886).
2. PR #8039: mergeable_state 'blocked', total_count=0.
3. PR #8053 — **already MERGED to main today** — also total_count=0. So recent merges went in with NO checks run at all.
4. actions_list filtered to event=pull_request repo-wide returns only 'claude-run-failure-alert' runs (all on main). No ruff-lint / pytest-run / pytest-collect / secret-scan / dry-run-guard / env-gate-guard / silent-empty-guard / canonical-config-loaders / canonical-db-resolver run for any PR.

WHAT STILL WORKS (so Actions itself is NOT disabled):
- push-triggered workflows DO run (json-extract-guard.yml fired on two pushes to a claude/** branch).
- issues-triggered workflows DO run (the trainer-vm-diag relay served four requests this session: #8068, #8071, #8072, #8073).
So the fault is specific to the `pull_request` event, not to Actions or to runners.

WHY THIS IS P1: 'zero checks' renders identically to 'all green' in the PR UI and in the MCP status payload. Branch protection lists nine REQUIRED contexts (branch-protection-sync.yml) — if those are genuinely required and never report, PRs should be unmergeable; #8053 merged anyway, which means either protection is not actually enforcing or the contexts are not matching. Either way the repo currently has NO pre-merge verification, on a live-money system.

NOT DIAGNOSED (needs operator/console access this session does not have): repository Actions permission settings, branch-protection enforcement state, or an org policy. Ruled OUT: a `paths:` filter (the required guards deliberately carry none), workflow syntax (unchanged files that used to run), and runner availability (push + issue workflows run fine).

IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE for PR #8069: the promotion of provenance-consumer-guard to a REQUIRED context in that PR cannot be verified by a green run, because no PR run happens. The guard passes locally (`python3 scripts/check_provenance_consumers.py` -> OK) and its workflow is a copy of the canonical-db-resolver template validated with a duplicate-key-rejecting YAML loader, but 'CI green' is NOT available as evidence for it or for anything else merged right now.
items.observation_2026_07_30_evening:
NOT resolved — INTERMITTENT, which is worse than consistently broken because it reads as fixed. Checks attached for exactly three consecutive SHAs (8377f29c, 31d61f69, 09c7a11a; 25 runs each, 18:37-18:43Z) and then stopped again: f10d2b54, 19a5d883 and bf29519b produced ZERO runs. Correlation with the merge commit that brought #8039 down from main is therefore coincidence, not cause.

Ruled out this pass: no `draft` guard exists in any workflow (checked), so draft status is not the gate; `paths:` filters are not it either (pytest-run has none and still did not fire); and Actions is plainly not disabled, since push- and issue-triggered workflows have run reliably all session.

Note for whoever picks this up: `pytest-run.yml` CANNOT be dispatched as a workaround — its `push` trigger is `branches: [main]` only and it has no `workflow_dispatch`, so on a feature branch `pull_request` is the ONLY event that can run it. While that event is dropping, a feature branch has no way to run the test suite in CI at all.
items.why_critical: Zero checks renders identically to green in every UI and in `get_status`. This PR shipped 11 test failures, a false-positive guard trip and a deploy-safety gap that were ALL invisible until the event happened to fire — on a repo where main receives live-trading code.
items.evidence_2026_07_30_2000z:
SHARPENED, and one of my own earlier claims corrected. Correlating every branch SHA against actual workflow runs (ruff-lint, one run per SHA expected):
  8377f29c pull_request OK | 31d61f69 OK | 09c7a11a OK
  f10d2b54 NO RUN | 19a5d883 NO RUN
  bf29519b OK | 6c5273a1 OK | e02b0ada OK

So the gap is TWO SHAs, not three as I first wrote, and the two are not equally damning. f10d2b54 and 19a5d883 were pushed ~25s apart; a `synchronize` for a head that has already moved on is plausibly normal coalescing, so f10d2b54 alone would not evidence a defect. **19a5d883 is the real case**: it was the PR head for ~6 minutes with no event at all, then bf29519b (pushed later) fired normally. Concurrency cancellation is ruled out — neither ruff-lint nor pytest-run declares a `concurrency:` group.

TOOLING TRAP I fell into, worth recording: `pull_request_read get_status` returns `total_count: 0` on this repo ALWAYS, because it reads the legacy commit-status API while every check here is a Check Run. Some of my earlier 'zero checks' readings came from that call and were not evidence of anything. **Use `get_check_runs`, or correlate `actions_list` workflow runs by head_sha** — that is what the table above is built from. A watcher polling `get_status` would report a permanently-red repo.
items.severity_note: Lowered critical -> high on the sharper evidence: 1 confirmed dropped delivery out of 8 pushes, not the near-total outage the first reading suggested (part of which was the get_status artifact above). Still high, not medium: a check that runs SOMETIMES is not a check, and zero checks renders identically to green.

updates.note:
SCOPE CORRECTION + detail, so a review session doesn't start from a false premise. This row's TITLE says CI 'does not run on ANY PR' and its description is EMPTY. The 'any PR' claim is too broad, measured:
  #8085 15 checks all green | #8091 19 | #8097 15 | #8099 15 | #8102 15 | #8109 15 — six PRs merged by this session on 2026-07-30, every one fully checked. #8099 was a SINGLE-FILE docs-only change and still drew all 15.
Meanwhile #8069 read total_count:0 at 19:1x and 25/25 by 21:xx — i.e. INTERMITTENT, and PR/SHA-specific, not a repo-wide Actions outage.

Ruled out (checked directly, not inferred): no workflow carries a `draft == false` condition, so draft status is not the filter; and required checks deliberately carry NO `paths:` filter — env-gate-guard.yml documents exactly why ('trigger can never carry paths: — would leave the check permanently pending').

WHY IT STILL MATTERS AT THIS SEVERITY: zero checks renders identically to green in the UI and in get_status, so an unchecked merge is indistinguishable from a verified one. Keep it open. But the investigation should start from 'intermittent per-SHA' rather than 'Actions is down', which is a much cheaper problem.

Cross-referenced from a concurrent session's PR #8069, which independently reached the same intermittent conclusion.

items.source: Self-reported after THREE near-misses in ONE session (2026-07-30, session_01HSz1HjdRBCF63MhT5iXfvJ). Each destroyed or would have destroyed committed work; in every case the ONLY thing that surfaced it was git's own rejection on a LATER push, not any guard, check, or rule. (1) `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` discarded PR #8003's already-pushed commits; caught by the non-fast-forward rejection, recovered from origin/<branch> + cherry-pick. (2) `git reset --soft HEAD~1` on a MERGE commit during #8027's conflict resolution: --soft moves HEAD to the FIRST parent, silently dropping the second, so the union CONTENT landed while the merge LINK did not -- GitHub correctly kept reporting mergeable_state 'dirty' and I misdiagnosed it as a stale async computation, burning a diagnostic cycle before re-doing the merge properly. (3) `git reset --hard origin/main` at the start of the session-end doc sweep discarded commit 26333205 (vol-axis scoping), which was already PUSHED and open as PR #8051; caught by the non-fast-forward rejection, recovered by cherry-pick onto the remote tip.
items.title: [process/tooling] destructive git sync (`reset --hard` / `checkout -B` / `reset --soft` on a merge) has NO pre-flight guard — 3 near-miss data losses in one session, all caught by luck
items.description: ROOT CAUSE, stated as a behaviour not an accident: `git reset --hard <remote-ref>` and `git checkout -B <branch> <remote-ref>` are used as a 'sync to main' idiom WITHOUT first asking whether the branch carries commits that are not in the target. That question is one cheap command (`git log --oneline <target>..HEAD` must be empty, or `git diff <target> HEAD` must be empty when the content is expected to be equivalent). It was not asked in any of the three incidents. WHY THE CURRENT SAFETY NET IS NOT ONE: recovery depended on git's non-fast-forward / stale-info rejection on the NEXT push. That only fires IF a push happens, only AFTER the local work is already gone, and is easy to misread -- my push-retry loop treats every push failure as a transient network error and retried 4x with exponential backoff on a 'stale info' rejection, which is deterministic and will never succeed on retry. If a session resets, does not push, and the container is later reclaimed, the work is simply gone with no signal at all. THE MERGE-COMMIT SUB-CASE IS THE NASTIEST and deserves calling out separately: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` reads as 'undo one commit', but on a merge commit it moves to the FIRST parent and discards the merge relationship. The tree looks correct afterwards (content intact), so nothing local reveals the loss -- only the REMOTE disagrees, by continuing to report a conflict that the operator can see and the session cannot explain. BLAST RADIUS: bounded so far -- Tier-1 research/docs branches, all recoverable from the remote, zero production or live-VM impact. Severity is medium rather than high for that reason, NOT because the behaviour is acceptable; the same idiom on a branch whose commits were never pushed loses the work outright. PROPOSED FIXES (pick one or more; a later session decides): (a) a `scripts/ops/git_safe_sync.sh` helper that REFUSES to reset/checkout -B onto a ref when `<target>..HEAD` is non-empty unless an explicit --force-discard flag is passed, and which stashes-to-a-branch rather than discarding by default; (b) a binding line in `.claude/skills/git-actions/SKILL.md` requiring the emptiness check before any destructive sync, plus an explicit 'never `reset --soft` a merge commit' note; (c) make the push-retry loop classify failures -- non-fast-forward / stale info / rejected are DETERMINISTIC and must short-circuit to diagnosis, never burn 4 backoff retries (this half is cheap and independently useful); (d) consider a SessionStart or pre-tool hook, analogous to the existing `git_history_check` hook that refuses a history question on a shallow clone -- same spirit: refuse the unsafe operation rather than answer/perform it. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is NOT the same as the stop-hook's unverified-commit check, which watches commit ATTRIBUTION. Nothing currently watches DESTRUCTIVENESS. Three times today the hook's own suggested remedy (`git rebase --exec ... --reset-author`) would itself have rewritten published main history for GitHub-authored squash commits, which is a related instance of 'the suggested git operation is more destructive than the problem'.

items.title: [trainer][infra] trainer VM root filesystem at 95% — 2.4G free against a workload that writes ~480MB per dataset build
items.description: Not urgent-broken, but on a clear trajectory and cheap to fix now. The trainer's root fs is 43G/45G used with 2.4 GB free. That box's normal work is writing market_features builds of ~480 MB each (BTCUSDT/15m/v520 alone is 480,607,056 bytes), and `datasets-out/market_features/BTCUSDT/15m/` currently holds SIXTEEN versions (v001-v006, v104, v106, v107, v513-v515, v520, v903, v905, vfmac003), most of them 175,272-row siblings differing only in which optional side-stream was joined. Several are plainly superseded (v003/v004/v104/v106/v107 have NO fc_ columns at all; v513/v514/v515 are same-day predecessors of v520). WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND HOUSEKEEPING: a build that runs out of disk mid-write is exactly the failure mode that produces a TRUNCATED-BUT-PRESENT artifact — the 'green but vacuous' class the binding 'Green is not evidence' rule exists for. A half-written data.jsonl looks like a dataset until something asserts its row count. Two things worth doing: (a) prune superseded market_features versions on the trainer (keep the one each live/advisory head actually trained on — v520 for btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 — plus the newest), and (b) consider whether the dataset-build path should pre-check free space and fail loudly rather than write a partial file. NOTE the pruning is NOT purely mechanical: the registry pins heads to specific dataset versions, so a version must be confirmed unreferenced before deletion.
items.trigger_condition: Trainer root fs above ~90%, or any dataset build failing/short-writing.
items.resolution_criteria: Trainer root fs back under ~80% via a verified-unreferenced prune, and a decision recorded on whether build writes pre-check free space.

updates.note: RESOLVED. Measured first (trainer-diag #8087): root was at 96% (43G used / 2.3G free of 45G), worse than the 95% filed. Pruned CACHES AND LOGS ONLY (#8089): ~/.cache/pip 3.1G + journalctl --vacuum-size=200M freeing 1.5G of archived journals. Result 96% -> 85%, free 2.2G -> 6.8G. Deliberately did NOT touch datasets-out/ (15G) despite ~14 redundant market_features/BTCUSDT/15m versions: manifests PIN dataset versions (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 pins v520), so pruning there could strand a head's training provenance — that is a reviewed decision, not a disk-pressure reflex. Verified v520/data.jsonl intact at 480,607,056 bytes after the prune.

items.title: [macro][naming] eia_natgas_storage's scorecard uses the unsuffixed default filename — a `econ_event_study_*_scorecard.json` glob enumerates 4 of 5 kinds and looks complete
items.description: Low-severity but exactly the recurring wrong-roster shape, so it is filed rather than shrugged at. `scripts/macro/econ_event_study.py` writes to a per-kind suffixed path when given one and to the bare default otherwise; the #8053 run left natgas on the default. Consequence: any future consumer, audit, or re-grade that enumerates the family with a `econ_event_study_*_scorecard.json` glob gets FOUR kinds, no error, and no way to tell one is missing — and the missing one is natgas, the kind carrying the strongest (wrong-signed vs the pre-registered hypothesis) IC. NOT urgent: all five scorecards exist, all carry non-zero releases + price_bars, and the M1 null verdict is unaffected and already recorded. FIX (either is fine, pick one): (a) rename to econ_event_study_eia_natgas_storage_scorecard.json and have the producer ALWAYS suffix, so the default bare name never exists; or (b) if the bare name is deliberately 'the primary kind', document that in the producer + wherever the family is consumed, so a glob author knows to add it. Prefer (a) — an implicit primary is how the trap re-forms. Whichever is chosen, add the family to the artifact-validity registry so its COUNT is asserted, not its existence.

items.source: First real `verify` run of scripts/research/ml_vol_label_replay.py (trainer-diag #8079) comparing replayed btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 labels against the 34 live regime_ml_vol_shadow rows the gate itself recorded for BTCUSDT over 2026-06-28..06-30. Bar-alignment ruled out by a targeted +/-2-bar probe (#8080).
items.title: [regime][parity] the OFFLINE replay does not reproduce the LIVE P(volatile): 88.2% label agreement but median |dP| 0.043, p90 0.209, max 0.412 — and the agreeing rows do not match numerically either
items.description: WHAT WAS MEASURED. verify over the only window where live ML labels and offline-replayable bars both exist: comparable=34, agree=30 => 88.24% label agreement. The probability delta, which is the stronger check: median 0.042715, p90 0.208866, max 0.411516. WHY THE LABEL NUMBER IS MISLEADING ON ITS OWN. A label is a coarse threshold at 0.5, and most bars sit far below it, so two materially different probabilities usually threshold the same way. The 88% is therefore substantially COINCIDENCE, not agreement. BAR ALIGNMENT IS NOT THE EXPLANATION — checked, not assumed. The natural hypothesis was an off-by-one bar (live scores CLOSED bars; a 15m bar opening 13:00 closes 13:15, so a row logged 13:02 might legitimately carry the 12:45 score). #8080 printed the replayed p_volatile for every bar +/-2 around each of the 4 disagreements plus one AGREEING control. The live value matches NO adjacent replayed bar in any case: e.g. live 13:02:08 and 13:09:12 both read 0.21057753 while replayed 12:30/12:45/13:00/13:15/13:30 = 0.1935/0.2859/0.5512/0.4579/0.0730. THE CONTROL IS THE DECISIVE PART: an AGREEING row (live 09:03:33, p=0.07394825) also matches nothing — replayed 08:30/08:45/09:00/09:15 = 0.0376/0.0099/0.0511/0.0564. So even where the labels agree, the underlying probabilities differ. This is a genuine offline-vs-serve feature-row difference, not a join bug. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It does NOT invalidate the vol axis: grading a 2-D cell on the offline label is still far better than the 1-D pooling it replaces, which measured a population live never trades at all. It DOES bound the claim — any cell verdict produced from these labels must carry the ~88% live-label-agreement fidelity, and a cell whose verdict flips on a handful of near-threshold bars is NOT decision-grade. LIKELY CAUSES, none yet confirmed, ordered by suspicion: (a) the live row is built by feature_row_for_predictor from LIVE-FETCHED candles over a trailing window, while the offline row comes from the market_features builder — rolling_log_return_vol over a 20-bar window is the most sensitive shared input; (b) the live candle window may include a partially-formed current bar; (c) hour_of_day/dayofweek derived from the latest live bar vs the frame's ts. Note -v2 has NO fc_ features, so the Chronos side-stream is NOT a candidate here — which usefully narrows it to the 7 base columns. THIS IS THE GAP S-MLOPT-S17 EXISTED TO CLOSE. That sprint added build_parity_feature_row and asserted live==builder bit-for-bit in a unit test using MarketFeaturesBuilder as oracle. This measurement says the property does not hold in PRODUCTION over real bars. The unit test passing while live disagrees is itself the finding: the test's oracle and the live fetch path are not the same input. NEXT STEP TO ISOLATE: dump the live feature ROW (not just the score) for a handful of bars and diff it column-by-column against the builder's row for the same ts. shadow_predictions.jsonl already captures feature_row per prediction (added 2026-05-19), so this may be answerable from existing data with no new instrumentation.
items.trigger_condition: Any use of offline-replayed vol labels to grade, author, or retire a regime cell; and any claim that train/serve parity for the regime heads is closed.
items.resolution_criteria: The per-column source of the offline-vs-serve difference is identified from a real feature-row diff, and either fixed or documented as an irreducible bound with the agreement rate that every downstream cell verdict must carry.

updates.note: STALENESS RULED OUT — the finding is STRONGER, not weaker. Before letting the parity claim stand I tested the most likely benign explanation: _p_volatile_from_cache explicitly serves a STALE-but-present per-bar score ('the staleness is at most one bar duration'), and REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S can defer whole (symbol,timeframe) groups to a later tick, so the live value could simply be an older bar's score rather than a different computation. TEST (trainer-diag #8084): search the ENTIRE 175,272-bar replayed label file for each live p_volatile value, not just nearby bars. RESULT: 0 of 32 live values appear ANYWHERE in the replay. CONTROL that makes the test meaningful: the replay holds 171,381 DISTINCT p_volatile values across 175,272 rows, so values are essentially unique and a match would have been real signal rather than coincidence. Combined with the earlier +/-2-bar probe (#8080) and its AGREEING control row, three independent explanations are now excluded: bar misalignment, cache staleness, and join error. What remains is a genuine difference in the FEATURE ROW the head is scored on. ALSO CONFIRMED, and it removes a candidate cause: the live feature_row for btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 DOES carry all six fc_* columns (shadow_predictions tail, 2026-07-30T15:04:22Z), so forecast_live is populating them and a missing-fc_ hypothesis is dead. The live row also carries the full parity superset (parkinson/garman_klass/rogers_satchell/yang_zhang vols) beyond the head's own 13 features, as build_parity_feature_row intends. COLUMN ISOLATION IS BLOCKED ON A DATA WINDOW, and this is the concrete next step rather than a vague one: a column-by-column diff needs a MATCHED pair — one live feature_row and the builder's row for the SAME bar. shadow_predictions.jsonl is 85 MB and the diag log_file tail is capped at 1000 lines, which covers roughly EIGHT MINUTES of live scoring (400 lines spanned 15:03:58->15:11:22), while the newest market_features build (v002) ends 2026-07-29T22:30 — so the tail and the dataset do not currently overlap. Two ways to close it, neither started: (a) rebuild market_features BTCUSDT/15m through today and diff against a fresh live row — note BL-20260730-TRAINER-DISK-95PCT, the trainer root fs is at 95%/2.3GB so a ~480MB build needs the prune first; or (b) add a diag path that serves shadow_predictions filtered by model_id + since, so a historical live row can be pulled without a 200k-line tail. (b) is cheap and reusable and is probably the right one.

HYPOTHESIS worth testing, explicitly NOT a finding — but it connects two items tracked separately and would be easy to lose. FRAMING CORRECTION FIRST: I have been calling this 'the offline replay does not reproduce live', which quietly assumes LIVE is the reference and offline is the deviation. That assumption is not obviously right. The OFFLINE row comes from the canonical MarketFeaturesBuilder — literally the rows the head TRAINED on. The LIVE row is assembled by feature_row_for_predictor from live-fetched candles. If the two differ, it is at least as likely that the LIVE row is the deviant one, i.e. the head is being served feature rows unlike its training distribution. That is train/serve SKEW, and it is a live model-quality issue rather than an offline-tooling caveat. THE CONNECTION: M25's promotion work found the shadow regime fleet blocking FLEET-WIDE on `live_regime_discrimination` (the RG4 gate) — the same wall the vol-gate operating-curve study MB-20260701-001 hit, and the reason the 2026-07-19 gate reframe demoted RG4 to advisory so promotions could proceed on offline oos_edge instead. A head scored live on rows that differ from its training rows is EXACTLY what would produce good offline metrics and poor live discrimination. So 'the fleet cannot discriminate live' and 'the live feature row differs from the builder row' may be the same bug seen from two ends, and the fleet-wide-ness is itself suggestive — a per-head modelling failure would not hit every head equally, whereas a shared serve-path defect would. WHAT WOULD TEST IT: the same matched-pair column diff already needed for column isolation. If a specific column (rolling_log_return_vol over its 20-bar window is the prime suspect, being shared by every regime head) is systematically offset live-vs-builder, that single defect would explain both symptoms. If the columns match and only the score differs, this hypothesis is dead and the gap is elsewhere. DO NOT act on this as established. It is recorded so the column-diff, when it happens, is read against BOTH questions rather than only the narrow tooling one — and so nobody re-derives the connection from scratch. Refs MB-20260701-001 and the M25 RG4 reframe.

CORRECTION + SCOPE. While isolating the column difference I ran scripts/ml/_feature_parity_probe.py against the BTC ADVISORY head (#8088) and read its 'PREDICTED score(volatile)' line as mean 0.967 / min 0.504 over 2336 live rows — i.e. the live gate pinned to volatile on real money. THAT READING WAS WRONG and I did not escalate it. The shadow log's `score` is ShadowPredictor.predict -> MulticlassPredictor.predict = max(proba.values()) (ml/predictors/multiclass.py:38), the PREDICTED CLASS's confidence, hence >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class head. Fleet sweep (#8090) confirms: frac(score<0.5)==0.0000 for ALL ~30 regime heads, while non-multiclass heads in the SAME log (exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 0.036-0.452, setup-quality-lgbm-v2 -0.755-0.278, execution-quality-baseline-v0 constant -0.20) sit below 0.5 freely — a clean natural control. The live gate is NOT affected: regime_bar_scoring._maybe_publish_p_volatile reads predict_proba['volatile'] explicitly, and RG4 (replay_pregate_live.py:249) does the same, so neither the gate nor the fleet-wide RG4 block is an artifact of this. THE ORIGINAL FINDING IS UNAFFECTED — it was measured on p_volatile from the gate's own audit rows vs the replay, not on this `score` field. Still open; still ungraded cells.

LIVE-SIDE MEASUREMENT (fixed probe, trainer-diag #8092 + live audit rows #8094). The BTC advisory head btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 gates VOLATILE only 10/979 = 1.02% of advisory-stage rows (shadow stage 6/1357 = 0.44%); mean P(volatile) 0.0366. Training base rate on the MANIFEST-PINNED v520 is 4.6% (the buggy probe was reading vfmac003 at 16.04% — a 3.5x different base rate). My offline replay is 9.1%. Independently corroborated on the LIVE gate's own audit rows: 40/40 sampled regime_hard_gate rows for BTCUSDT carry vol_regime='calm' with vol_label_source='ml' and vol_regime_frozen='unknown' — so the ML label is the ONLY thing supplying the vol axis, and it reads calm essentially always. CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the claim: the live rows span 2026-07-07..2026-07-30, a calm ~3-week window, against 5 years of training — so part of the offline-vs-live gap is market conditions, not necessarily skew. The column-level residual: xa_breadth_up is present in TRAIN at 100% but CONSTANT 0.0, and entirely ABSENT from live rows (pres=0.0%) — the BL-20260628-XA-TRAINING-ZERO dead-feature class; a constant-0 column carries no information so the impact is probably nil, but that should be confirmed, not assumed.

SELF-CORRECTION — THE HEADLINE COMPARISON WAS EPOCH-MISMATCHED. I went looking for a reason my own finding might be wrong and found one. `v520` (the replay's dataset) covers **2021-07-01 -> 2026-06-30T22:30Z**. The live rows I compared it against start **2026-07-07** (shadow) / **2026-07-20** (advisory). The windows are effectively DISJOINT — the only overlap is a ~2-day sliver at the end of June, which is where the 34 'comparable' rows in the #8081 verify came from.

So 'offline 9.1% volatile vs live 1.02%' does NOT measure a serve-path gap: the 9.1% is a 5-year average (2021-07..2026-06) and the 1.02% is July 2026, a month absent from the dataset entirely.

The dataset's OWN per-month regime_label rate settles it — sub-1% months are common and recent:
  2025-05 0.64% | 2025-06 0.94% | 2025-07 0.27% | 2025-09 0.14% | 2026-04 1.42% | 2026-05 0.74% | 2026-06 4.73%
Last three available months pooled = 199/8731 = 2.28%. A live July reading of ~1% sits INSIDE this label's ordinary recent variation. It is not anomalous and is not evidence of skew.

WHAT SURVIVES: the #8081 matched-timestamp comparison (median |dP| 0.043, p90 0.209, max 0.412) — those 34 rows were joined BY TIMESTAMP inside the overlap, so they are genuinely apples-to-apples. That is now the ONLY evidence for a gap, and it is thin: n=34 over ~2 days.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY TEST IT: rebuild market_features BTCUSDT/15m through today (now unblocked — trainer went 96%->85%, 6.8G free) and re-run the replay over the SAME window the live rows cover. Until then this item should not be cited as an established gap. Severity dropped high -> medium accordingly.

RESOLVED — the matched-window comparison shows NO serve-path gap.

Ran the replay of btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 over market_features/BTCUSDT/15m/**v002** (regenerated by the nightly 2026-07-30 05:10, spans to 2026-07-29T22:30Z, so it COVERS the live advisory window — unlike v520 which stops 2026-06-30). Sanity gate passed before use: 175,272 rows, 108,873 distinct P values, feature_audit clean, not a degenerate split.

MATCHED WINDOW (2026-07-20..07-29, the live advisory window):
  offline replay : 11/955  = 1.15%  (meanP 0.0521)
  live serve     : 10/979  = 1.02%
Near-identical rates AND near-identical denominators. Offline reproduces live.

CONTROL, full span 2021-07..2026-07: 15,636/175,272 = 8.92% — which confirms the original 9.1% figure was correct as a FIVE-YEAR AVERAGE and simply not comparable to a ten-day live window. The whole apparent gap was the epoch mismatch recorded in the previous update.

Per-month P>=0.5 rate also settles the cell-dormancy question: 2026-02 20.50% | 2026-03 12.03% | 2026-04 3.44% | 2026-05 1.65% | 2026-06 8.51% | 2026-07 3.35%. July 2026 was genuinely calm. The three volatile-keyed trend_vol cells are dormant because of MARKET CONDITIONS, not a defect — which is what a vol-conditioned gate is supposed to do.

NOT CLAIMED, stated so it isn't mistaken for evidence: my shadow-window figure (2.95% offline vs 0.44% live) is NOT like-for-like. This head's live SHADOW rows end 2026-07-20 (it was promoted to advisory then), but I windowed offline 07-07..07-29. Same mismatch class as the original error; caught before publishing. Only the ADVISORY comparison above is sound, and it is the one that matters — that is the stage driving the live gate.

RESIDUAL CAVEATS: (a) v002 is builder_version v12 while v520 (what the head trained on) was v11; (b) the replay is IN-SAMPLE over the head's training window (the manifest's own fidelity block says so) — weaker than backtest bias since this is a market-state label, not a performance prediction, but real. Neither changes the conclusion: two independently-produced rates over the same bars agree to within 0.13pp.

The earlier #8081 matched-timestamp result (median |dP| 0.043, n=34 over ~2 days at end-June) is now best read as ordinary numerical/feature-path jitter rather than a systematic gap.

items.source: Found while using scripts/ml/_feature_parity_probe.py to isolate the offline-vs-serve feature gap (BL-20260730-OFFLINE-VS-SERVE-PVOLATILE-GAP). The probe is a PROMOTION-DECISION diagnostic, so a misleading line in it propagates into stage decisions.
items.title: [ml][tooling] feature-parity probe reported max(proba) as 'P(volatile)' and compared against the wrong dataset version — nearly produced a false P1 on the live money gate
items.description:
TWO defects, both fixed in the same PR that files this item.

(1) MISLABEL. The probe printed the shadow log's `score` under the label 'PREDICTED score(volatile)'. That field is max(proba.values()) — the predicted class's confidence — not P(volatile), so it is >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class regime head. Every regime head therefore rendered as saturated-volatile (BTC advisory read mean 0.967 / min 0.504). A head that is 97% sure the regime is CALM prints 0.97 under a label that says volatile: the meaning is INVERTED, not merely imprecise. I came within one step of escalating a false P1 against the live real-money BTC vol gate on the strength of this line.

(2) WRONG TRAINING DATASET. _training_rows took sorted(glob(...))[-1] — the alphabetically LAST version dir — not the manifest's pinned dataset. datasets-out/market_features/BTCUSDT/15m holds ~14 versions, so it silently selected vfmac003 while btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 actually pins v520. Every 'TRAINING dataset' distribution line was therefore potentially against data the head never saw — which is the probe's entire output.

FIX: the probe now (a) prints the logged value as 'LOGGED score = max(proba), NOT P(vol)' AND separately re-runs predict_proba to report the real P(volatile) the gate thresholds plus the would-gate-VOLATILE share, degrading honestly when the predictor can't be resolved; and (b) resolves ml/configs/<id>.yaml::dataset.version, warning LOUDLY on any fallback instead of silently substituting. Regression guard: tests/ml/test_feature_parity_probe_score_semantics.py pins max(proba) semantics (including the inverted 0.03 case) and forbids the old print label.

SEPARATE LIVE-VERIFIED FINDING (supports the cells' authoring premise): in 4 of the 11 trend_donchian rows the ML and frozen labels DISAGREE — all transitional, vol_regime_frozen='volatile' vs vol_regime_ml='calm'. CAUSE CONFIRMED — market conditions, not a defect. items.title: [infra][tooling] vm-diag-snapshot's failure comment blames the VM for what is actually a malformed request
items.description:
When the diag path fails VALIDATION, the workflow posts: 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY/DIAG_READ_TOKEN secret unset, malformed key, VM web-api down, token mismatch.' All four are infrastructure causes; none is what happened. No VM contact is even attempted on that path. I read that comment and recorded 'VM web-api down' — a false infra diagnosis — and later re-derived the same wrong conclusion, then posted it to the coordination board before checking the run log.

Root cause of the malformed request itself: the workflow reads the path from the issue BODY; a prose body ('path is in the title') is parsed AS a path and rejected.

FIX (this PR): the failure comment now branches on steps.resolve/resolve_multi.outcome and, for a validation rejection, leads with 'MALFORMED REQUEST, not a VM outage', states that the BODY is what is parsed, and shows a correct example body. The infra text is kept for genuine infra failures.

items.source: Tripped on PR #8069 against a DOCSTRING sentence, not a table declaration.
items.title: [ci][tooling] new-table-wiring-guard matches CREATE TABLE inside prose, producing false trips
items.description:
scripts/check_new_table_wiring.py scans a raw diff for CREATE TABLE and does not distinguish code from prose. On PR #8069 it failed on src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py for a docstring line that merely SAID the exchange_fills schema is created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. That module declares no table at all — it maps into the existing store.

Why this matters more than one false positive: the only ways to clear a false trip are to reword the prose (what PR #8069 did) or to add a `# data-wiring:` annotation for a table that does not exist. The second is FALSIFYING the wiring declaration the guard exists to protect, and it is the path of least resistance — so a prose-blind guard actively teaches contributors to lie to it. Combined with routine false trips, that is the alarm-fatigue failure mode CLAUDE.md names as itself a P1.

Third instance of this exact class in one session: my own json-extract guard first flagged 3 docstring-prose lines, and a structural test matched the explanatory comment NAMING the thing it forbade. Prose-vs-code is a systematic blind spot in this repo's diff-scanning guards, not a one-off.
items.resolution_criteria: The guard ignores CREATE TABLE occurrences inside string literals and comments. scripts/ci/check_json_extract_guarded.py::_prose_lines already solves this with ast+tokenize and is the reference implementation — but it parses FILES, while this guard parses a DIFF (hunks are not valid Python), so the fix likely means resolving each touched file at HEAD and mapping added line numbers onto it rather than porting _prose_lines directly. Add a test asserting a prose mention does NOT trip while a real CREATE TABLE does.

items.description:
The proposal was parked pending the ML vol axis. That axis now exists and is verified against live serve to 0.13pp on a matched window (PR #8109), so the block is cleared and the question is answerable.

THE QUESTION: trending/calm squeeze_breakout_4h {short: off} is ALREADY authored. So the 1-D proposal only adds value if trending/VOLATILE short ALSO loses.

THE ANSWER (offline, 4h BTCUSDT, 2021-01..2026-06, vol_axis present, coverage 106/110 = 96.4%):

    trending/unknown  short                       : net_R +0.4813  n=1

So the whole 1-D trending-short loss IS the calm sub-population, and that sub-population is already suppressed by the existing 2-D cell. trending/volatile has ZERO short trades in 5.4 years — authoring the 1-D cell would additionally gate a population with no evidence in either direction.

The existing cell is also well-targeted, which is worth recording: it gates only `short` in trending/calm and leaves `long` on — and trending/calm LONG is the strategy's best cell at +9.8014R over n=24.

EXPOSURE CONTEXT for weighting this: squeeze_breakout_4h is routed ONLY to bybit_1 (demo/PAPER). It was removed from real-money bybit_2 at its 2026-06-01 demotion and the 2026-06-23 re-promotion is paper-only (config/strategies.yaml:320-323). No real-money exposure today either way.

NOTE --kc-mult 1.0: the harness default is 1.5, so omitting it silently grades a different strategy.

HONEST LIMITS: (a) the -3.2101R/17t figure is a different measurement basis from the '-$55 / 30t' recorded in the cell's own comment (R vs dollars, different run/period) — they are not in conflict, they are not the same measurement, and I did not try to reconcile them; (b) n=0 in trending/volatile means NO evidence, which is not the same as evidence of no effect; (c) nothing here re-grades the OTHER five cells — see BL-20260730-VOL-AXIS-THREE-CELLS-DORMANT.

items.title: [tooling][meta] UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT is a defect CLASS — guard shipped (diagnostic-provenance-guard); residual sites grandfathered
items.description:
THE CLASS. A human-facing diagnostic asserts a labelled claim without emitting the derivation that would let a reader falsify it. The number is real; the label is confident; the substitution is invisible. Because every component is individually correct, line-by-line review keeps returning clean — the defect lives at the seams, exactly like the provenance/exit-leak incident the same day.

THREE SUB-CLASSES (mechanically distinguishable, different fixes):
  A SEMANTIC SUBSTITUTION — the printed label names quantity Q; the code called accessor f(); f() != Q.
    A1 inverted (max(proba) vs P(volatile) — meaning destroyed, low bucket empty by construction);
    A2 narrowed/widened ("every audited symbol is fully SL-covered" is TRUE at 444.7% coverage but asserts far more than the verdict measured);
    A3 untested causal claim (a failure comment names a cause no code path tested — the diag-relay 'VM down' for a pre-contact request rejection). A3 is really its own thing: the fix is to branch on the actual failure stage, not to rename a label.
  B IMPLICIT INPUT SELECTION — newest/alphabetically-last/default substituted for the declared or pinned input.
    B1 input artifact (sorted(glob(...))[-1] instead of the manifest's dataset.version);
    B2 input PARAMETER (a function default that differs from what the canonical caller passes — see the vol_threshold item below). Same class, and the one most likely to recur, because nothing in the output distinguishes the two label definitions.
  C UNASSERTED DENOMINATOR — an empty/zero/truncated result reads as a clean negative (a curl||echo '{}' poller turning HTTP 403 into '0 checks'; 'limit: 500' mistaken for a row count).

NOTE the division of labour with silent-empty-guard: that guard catches the PRODUCER (a broad except returning []). C is the CONSUMER (reading [] as a clean, labelled answer). Neither covers the other.

SYSTEMIC FIX SHIPPED (this PR, Tier-1): scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py + .github/workflows/diagnostic-provenance-guard.yml + tests/test_diagnostic_provenance_guard.py — same family as canonical-db-resolver / env-gate-guard / silent-empty-guard / provenance-consumer-guard. Diff-scoped in CI (pre-existing sites grandfathered, same contract as silent-empty-guard); `--all` is the standing audit mode. Its override is VERIFIED, not presence-only: `# provenance: <accessor> — <meaning>` must name an identifier that actually appears in the file, and the annotation is excluded from its own evidence pool. This is the direct lesson from new-table-wiring-guard, whose presence-only marker made the cheapest way to silence it naming a table that does not exist.

VALIDATION that the guard generalises rather than memorises: run against the tree it independently re-found bybit_bracket_audit.py:411 (the PR #8069 roll-up finding) and scripts/research/m20_ml_exit_probe.py:64 (a NEW instance nobody had reported), and it passes PR #8091's fixed parity probe.

RESIDUAL (grandfathered, discoverable via --all; ~20 sites, mostly B on market_raw candle dirs where a wrong version is far less dangerous than a wrong LABELLED feature dir): scripts/ml/_labeling_gap_probe.py, scripts/ml/fc_sltp_geometry_backtest.py, scripts/ml/gpu_burst/_remote.py, scripts/research/m20_exit_analysis.py, scripts/research/ws_a_s{2,3,3b}_*.py, ml/cli.py:579 (the promotion gate-check's candle pick — highest blast radius of the B residue), scripts/ml/m23_ev_gate.py:110 and scripts/research/build_research_panel.py:228 (A, latent: predictor is binary today, nothing enforces it).
items.resolution_criteria: Guard is a required check; the --all residue is driven to zero or each remaining site carries a verified `# provenance:` annotation.

items.title: [research][tooling] m20_ml_exit_probe bucketed max(proba) as 'P(volatile)' — its 'lo' bucket was empty by construction and 'hi' mixed calm with volatile
items.description:
Same defect as BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA, in a second probe, undetected.

scripts/research/m20_ml_exit_probe.py read the shadow log's `score` (line 64) and bucketed it at `score>=0.6`/`score<=0.4` (line 135), printing the result under the header '=== future_dR by P(volatile) bucket ==='. `score` is ShadowPredictor.predict -> wrapped.predict(row), and every regime head is a MulticlassPredictor whose predict is max(proba.values()). Therefore:
  * score >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class head, so the `lo` bucket (score<=0.4) was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and `mid` only spanned (0.5,0.6];
  * a row reading 0.97 may mean '97% sure the regime is CALM', so the `hi` bucket labelled high-P(volatile) was a MIXTURE of confidently-volatile and confidently-calm bars.

The probe's stated question — does a high regime-head P(volatile) predict a worse REMAINING hold? — was therefore unanswerable from what it computed, while the printed output (bucket means + an 'Interpretation:' paragraph telling the reader how to conclude) looked exactly like an answer.

BLAST RADIUS: this probe's output is the evidence for whether to build an ML exit trigger (M20). That decision is Tier-3 downstream (an exit-geometry change on live legs). No live-money decision was changed — as far as this session can establish the probe's output was never acted on — but it is the same severity CLASS as the parity probe, not merely confusing.

FIX (this PR): buckets the real predict_proba(row)['volatile'] — the quantity regime_bar_scoring._maybe_publish_p_volatile hands the live gate — via a new SHARED accessor, scripts/ml/_regime_score_semantics.py, which is now the one module that owns what `score` means. Rows whose predictor cannot be resolved are DROPPED and COUNTED (an honest coverage denominator, the rCoverage pattern), never bucketed on the substituted value; if nothing resolves the probe ABORTS rather than emitting a plausible wrong answer. Header now states the accessor and the gate cut.
items.resolution_criteria: Probe buckets predict_proba[volatile], reports coverage, and aborts rather than substituting. Regression-pinned.

items.title: [infra][tooling] trainer-vm-diag's failure comment blamed 'SSH timeout (VM down?)' for a pre-SSH request-parse rejection
items.description:
The sibling relay had the identical defect and PR #8097 did not reach it.

.github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml 'Parse command from issue body' (step at L138) exits 1 at L185 when the body carries no `cmd:` line. That step runs BEFORE 'Set up SSH key' (L198), so on a parse rejection the SSH key is never installed and NO trainer-VM contact is attempted. The failure comment nonetheless posted: 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY unset, SSH timeout (VM down?), malformed cmd: block' — lumping the one true cause in with two that are impossible on that path, with nothing telling the reader which applied.

This is exactly the reading that produced a false 'VM web-api down' diagnosis twice in one session on the sibling relay, and reached the coordination board before anyone opened the run log. It matters more here: a false 'trainer VM down' is a conclusion the ml-review / system-review skills treat as a mandatory standalone flag.

FIX (this PR): the comment branches on steps.parse.outputs.cmd_present. A parse rejection now leads with 'MALFORMED REQUEST, not a VM outage', states that the BODY is what is parsed (the title is display-only — the recurring operator trap), shows a correct example body, and points at the parse step's log. The infra text is kept, unchanged, for genuine post-parse failures.

STILL OPEN (lower severity, same shape, NOT fixed here): system-actions.yml — 'Validate action and tier policy' (L511) holds ~40 exit-1 paths, all ~250 lines BEFORE 'Set up SSH key' (L764), while the failure comment leads 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY secret unset/corrupted; SSH host unreachable'. It is milder (it does print `exitCode || '(set up failed before exec)'`, which a careful reader can use) but the cause list is still untested. health-snapshot.yml and set-diag-token.yml carry the same untested cause lists.
items.resolution_criteria: A pre-contact rejection produces a request-shaped message on every relay; infra text is reserved for genuine infra failures.

items.title: [ml][TIER-3 PROPOSAL] market_features vol_threshold default 0.003 silently disagrees with the canonical builder's 0.005 — two different regime_label definitions, no marker in the output
items.description:
VERIFIED: ml/datasets/families/market_features.py L504 defaults vol_threshold=0.003 (docstring L22 agrees). scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh — the CANONICAL builder — passes 0.005 for the Bybit legs (L275, L738) and a DATA-DRIVEN median for MES (L519-525, deliberately: a fixed threshold collapses MES intraday to all-range, MB-20260527-002).

So a hand-rolled `python -m ml build-dataset ...` that omits the argument produces a dataset whose `regime_label` means something DIFFERENT from every dataset the fleet trained on — measured on disk, 0.003 dirs read 16.04% volatile vs 4.6% at 0.005 — and NOTHING in the resulting dataset dir, the manifest, or any downstream metric says which definition it carries. This is sub-class B2 (implicit input PARAMETER selection) and it is the residue most likely to recur, because it needs no code change to bite: just a rebuild that forgets an argument.

It has already caused real confusion: the parity-probe incident (BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA) compared a head pinned to v520 (4.6% volatile) against vfmac003 (16.04%) — datasets built at DIFFERENT thresholds — and ml/cli.py:585 carries a comment recording an earlier burn by the same class ('the legacy hardcoded 0.003 that mis-scores the fleet', MB-20260628-RG4-THRESH).

NOT FIXED HERE — TIER-3. Changing the default changes the LABEL DEFINITION of every dataset built without an explicit argument, which changes what models learn. Three options for the operator, in preference order:
  1 (recommended) Make it REQUIRED, no default. A caller must state the threshold; the canonical builder already does. Nothing can drift because nothing is implicit. Cost: any ad-hoc caller must be updated (grep shows the canonical builder + the MES path already pass it explicitly).
  2 Stamp the resolved vol_threshold into the dataset dir's metadata AND require every consumer that compares distributions to read it. This is the provenance-consumer-guard shape and is strictly better than (3), but it is more code.
  3 Change the default 0.003 -> 0.005. Cheapest, but it silently reinterprets any historical rebuild and leaves the same class of trap for the MES data-driven path.
Recommendation: (1) + (2). (3) alone re-arms the trap.
items.resolution_criteria: Operator picks an option; vol_threshold can no longer be implicit, or the resolved value is stamped and read by every distribution consumer.

items.title: [ml][tooling] `python -m ml <heavy-cmd> --help` acquires the trainer heavy-job lock before arg parsing — printing help queues behind a training run
items.description:
VERIFIED: ml/cli.py::main resolves `cmd = argv[0]` and, at L1100, `if cmd in _HEAVY_COMMANDS: _heavy_lock = _acquire_heavy_lock(...)` — BEFORE the `build-dataset`/`validate-dataset` dispatch (L1102-1105) and before `_build_parser().parse_args()` (L1108-1109). `--help` is just another argv element at that point.

So `python -m ml build-dataset --help` takes the shared flock on a 1-core trainer VM with a FIFO queue: it blocks behind any running training cycle, and while held it blocks the next real job. The lock is bound for the whole process lifetime by design (correct for a real run), so a help invocation holds it until argparse exits. On a clean-timeout it raises SystemExit(75) — a documentation lookup failing with a queue-timeout exit code.

This is adjacent to the diagnostic-provenance class rather than an instance of it (nothing is mislabelled), but it shares the root: the tool's OBSERVABLE behaviour disagrees with what the invocation says it is doing. It is filed here because it was surfaced by the same sweep and would otherwise be lost.

FIX (Tier-1, trainer-autonomous, NOT applied here to keep this PR to one class): hoist a pure-help/version short-circuit above the lock — if any of {-h, --help, --version} appears in argv, dispatch to the parser and return without ever calling _acquire_heavy_lock. Guard it with a test asserting `main(['build-dataset','--help'])` never touches the lock. Deliberately left unmerged here because ml/cli.py is the trainer's real entry point and it deserves its own change + test rather than riding a tooling-guard PR.
items.resolution_criteria: `--help`/`-h`/`--version` on any heavy command returns without acquiring the flock; pinned by a test.

items.title: [ml] the multiclass evaluator type-checks its predictor; the BINARY evaluators do not — the guard runs in one direction only
items.description:
ml/evaluators/multiclass_classification.py L36-38 raises when handed a non-MulticlassPredictor. The reverse check does not exist: ml/evaluators/classification.py L37 and classification_auc.py L89 call `predictor.predict(row)` and treat the float as P(positive). Handed a MulticlassPredictor they would silently score accuracy / Brier / AUC on max(proba) — a quantity that is >= 0.5 by construction and HIGH for a confidently-CALM regime bar, i.e. a meaningless metric reported under a standard metric name.

NOT CURRENTLY LIVE — checked: all 70 regime manifests route to MulticlassClassificationEvaluator; the 11 ClassificationEvaluator + 1 ClassificationAUCEvaluator manifests are binary heads. So this is LATENT, and the exposure is one manifest edit away, with no error at the point of the mistake.

PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1, ml/ trainer-side, not applied here): mirror the existing isinstance check — ClassificationEvaluator raises when handed a MulticlassPredictor, pointing the author at MulticlassClassificationEvaluator. Two lines, symmetric with code already there, and it converts a silent wrong metric into a loud manifest error.
items.resolution_criteria: A binary evaluator handed a MulticlassPredictor raises instead of scoring max(proba).

items.title: [tooling] new-table-wiring-guard matched PROSE and accepted a presence-only marker — the cheapest way to silence it was to name a table that does not exist
items.description:
Two defects that made the guard's own output untrustworthy. A guard is a diagnostic; 'clean' is a claim a human acts on.

  1 PROSE MATCHING. `_CREATE_TABLE_RE = CREATE\s+TABLE` fired on any added line containing the words — a docstring sentence or a comment describing the rule. A guard that flags prose trains reviewers to wave its findings through, which is the alarm-fatigue failure this repo already classes as its own P1 bug (MB-20260719-DATASET-AUDIT-NOISE).
  2 PRESENCE-ONLY MARKER. Any `# data-wiring:` line anywhere in the file's added lines cleared every finding in that file, content unchecked. The path of least resistance to silencing a real finding was therefore to add a marker naming a table that does not exist — the guard actively taught contributors to lie to it.

FIX (this PR): (1) the pattern now requires an actual table NAME after CREATE TABLE and skips comment/docstring lines; (2) the marker must name either the table itself or an identifier that appears in the change's added lines, and — the subtle half — the annotation line is EXCLUDED from its own evidence pool, otherwise its own prose validates it. A marker that names nothing real now produces a distinct, explanatory finding rather than silence. (3) The all-clear now prints its denominator ('N changed file(s) scanned, 0 unannotated CREATE TABLE') so 'clean' is distinguishable from 'scanned nothing'.

The same verified-annotation rule is what the new diagnostic-provenance-guard uses for its `# provenance:` override, so the lesson is encoded in both. All 33 pre-existing new-table-wiring tests still pass.
items.resolution_criteria: Prose no longer matches; an annotation naming nothing real no longer clears a finding; the all-clear carries a denominator.

items.title: [ops][tooling] bybit_bracket_audit's roll-up printed 'every audited symbol is fully SL-covered' over a 444.7% over-coverage
items.description:
VERIFIED in code: the verdict ladder (L216-222) has no OVER_COVERED bucket — `covered + eps >= size` resolves to PROTECTED regardless of how far above `size` the summed SL legs run — and the roll-up (L397-411) buckets only PARTIALLY_NAKED / NAKED / *_UNRELIABLE, so an over-covered symbol fell into the `else` and printed the all-clear.

'Fully SL-covered' is LITERALLY TRUE at 444.7% coverage. That is what makes it sub-class A2 rather than a simple mislabel: the summary asserts a clean bill of health far stronger than the verdict measured, and a reader who stops at the roll-up walks past live leg over-accumulation — the very condition the runtime's own _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions flags as `over_covered` (BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING, live-verified firing the same day). The audit and the runtime disagreed about the same position, and only the audit was being read.

BLAST RADIUS: this audit is the operator-facing check for whether real-money positions are protected. It did not mis-state NAKED (under-coverage was always bucketed correctly), so no position was reported protected while actually naked — the failure is a missed anomaly, not a false safety claim about stop coverage.

FIX (this PR): over-coverage gets its own roll-up bucket with its own explanatory line ('not a naked risk but not clean either'), FLAT symbols are excluded from the denominator, the all-clear now carries the count it ranges over, and the JSON summary gains a `rollup` block so a machine consumer sees the same three numbers.
items.resolution_criteria: Over-coverage is bucketed and named; the all-clear carries its denominator.
